# Framework functions

Every function defined at file level in runtime/ and recompiler/, by file: name, line, what it does.
Look here first to find what a function does, how it is called and where it lives; then open the file at the line.
Lines are refreshed by `python tools/function_index.py`; a commit that adds, removes or changes what a function
does reruns it and writes the new descriptions in the same commit.

### recompiler/include/bios_rom_alias.h

Helpers that let a BIOS ROM be found whether its filename uses the bare model name or the region-qualified name.

- `bios_model_token` (L40) — The model token of a BIOS filename: the last '-'-separated piece of the stem, uppercased.
- `bios_name_matches` (L50) — Does 'candidate' name the same BIOS model as 'wanted_token', with a BIOS-ish extension?
- `resolve_bios_rom` (L63) — Resolve a configured BIOS ROM path to something that exists, tolerating either filename convention.

### recompiler/include/control_flow.h

Declares the control-flow graph structures and analyzer that find branches, loops and reachable blocks for each recompiled function.

- `rebuild_control_flow_metadata` (L72) — Rebuild reverse edges, static reachability and dominance-proven back edges.

### recompiler/include/gte_register_classification.h

Lists which COP2 (GTE) registers need a helper call instead of the fast raw-array path, shared by both code emitters.

- `data_read_needs_helper` (L10) — True when a read of this GTE data register must go through the helper, because it needs sign extension, masking or special packing.
- `data_write_needs_helper` (L20) — True when a write to this GTE data register must go through the helper instead of the raw register array.
- `ctrl_read_needs_helper` (L26) — True when a read of this GTE control register must go through the helper, because its value is sign-extended.
- `ctrl_write_needs_helper` (L33) — True when a write to this GTE control register must go through the helper instead of the raw register array.
- `helper_mask` (L38) — Builds a 32-bit mask with bit N set for each register number 0-31 for which the given predicate returns true.

### recompiler/include/host_path.h

Path helpers that keep Windows UNC and absolute paths intact on MinGW builds.

- `host_path_forward_slashes` (L12) — generic_string() can collapse a MinGW UNC root from "//server" to "/server".
- `host_path_is_absolute` (L24) — Some MinGW libstdc++ builds treat a readable UNC path as drive-relative: absolute("\\\\server\\share\\file") becomes "D:\\server\\share\\file".
- `host_absolute` (L34) — Returns the absolute form of a path, leaving paths that are already absolute (UNC included) unchanged; the error_code overload reports failure without throwing.
- `host_resolve` (L49) — A fully qualified config value must not be prefixed with its config root.

### recompiler/include/ps1_exe_parser.h

Defines the PS-X EXE header layout and the MIPS segment helpers that map program addresses to physical memory.

- `maps_physical` (L26) — True when 'pc' lies in one of the three windows that map the physical address space: KUSEG below 0x20000000, KSEG0 and KSEG1.

### recompiler/src/analysis_db.cpp

Builds the static analysis database for a PS1 executable, covering functions, call edges, jump tables, disassembly and symbol loading.

- `norm` (L28) — Masks an address to the 29-bit physical range so that KSEG aliases of the same address compare equal.
- `add` (L45) — Sets the bit for register r in a register mask, ignoring register zero.
- `reg_effect` (L49) — Returns which registers an instruction reads and writes, using an explicit table per opcode and funct.
- `mem_width` (L112) — Returns the size in bytes of a load or store opcode, or 0 for any other opcode.
- `is_store_op` (L122) — True when the opcode is a store instruction (SB, SH, SWL, SW, SWR or SWC2).
- `is_load_op` (L127) — True when the opcode is a load instruction (LB, LH, LW, LBU, LHU, LWL, LWR or LWC2).
- `classify_target` (L133) — Labels an address as mmio, image, ram or other, from the MMIO range, the image bounds and the RAM size.
- `format_instr` (L144) — --------------------------------------------------------------------------- Disassembly formatting ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
- `find_def` (L234) — Nearest preceding instruction that writes 'reg', searching back at most 'window' instructions and never before 'lo'.
- `const_value` (L248) — Constant value of 'reg' at 'at_pc', if it comes from LUI or LUI+ADDIU.
- `recover_jump_table` (L266) — Recovers a jump table behind a jr through a loaded register by matching the lw and address arithmetic that builds it; true when found.
- `recover_indirect_call` (L380) — Resolve 'jalr $rD' / 'jr $rD' where $rD holds a statically-known function address: either materialized inline (lui/addiu) or loaded from a fixed address whose stored word is a known function start.
- `render_prototype` (L414) — Renders a function's C prototype as text, with u32 as the return type and u32 arguments a0 onwards.
- `confidence_name` (L427) — Returns the lowercase name of a confidence level, such as verified, high, medium, low or data.
- `edge_kind_name` (L438) — Returns the lowercase name of a call edge kind, such as direct, jump_table, address_taken or indirect.
- `AnalysisDb::find` (L448) — Returns the function record that starts exactly at addr, or null when none starts there.
- `AnalysisDb::containing` (L455) — Returns the function whose address range contains pc, or null when pc is outside every function.
- `load_symbols` (L466) — --------------------------------------------------------------------------- symbols.toml ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
- `build_analysis_db` (L499) — --------------------------------------------------------------------------- Main build ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
- `disassemble_range` (L1036) — Disassembles the words from lo up to hi as text lines, one per instruction, stopping at unreadable memory.

Loads a file of address and note lines into a table, and looks up the note for an address.

### recompiler/src/bios_address_model.cpp

Address model for the BIOS image, mapping ROM, RAM and install-slot addresses so generated code dispatches to the right copy.

- `BiosAddressModel::from_config` (L18) — Builds the address model from the BIOS config's copy and install-slot lists, validating each copy's bounds and throwing on bad values.
- `BiosAddressModel::normalize` (L140) — Maps an address to the dispatch key used for lookup, folding the physical mask and mirrored RAM aliases to one value.
- `BiosAddressModel::ram_alias_to_rom` (L162) — Maps a RAM address inside a copied window back to the ROM address it was copied from, or returns it unchanged.
- `BiosAddressModel::runtime_pc` (L171) — Maps a ROM address to the runtime PC where that copy of the code runs, or returns it unchanged outside every copy.
- `BiosAddressModel::relocate_j_target` (L180) — Rewrites a jump target so it points into the copy window that holds the jump at rom_addr, or returns it unchanged.
- `BiosAddressModel::rom_to_ram_phys` (L191) — Maps a ROM address inside a RAM-keyed copy to its physical RAM address.
- `BiosAddressModel::remap_relocated_j_target` (L200) — Remaps the target of a jump found in a relocated copy so it points at the matching address in that same copy.
- `BiosAddressModel::kbless_ram_lo` (L229) — Returns the low RAM address of the kbless copy window.
- `BiosAddressModel::kbless_ram_hi` (L230) — Returns the end RAM address, exclusive, of the kbless copy window.
- `BiosAddressModel::kbless_rom_off` (L231) — Returns the offset of the kbless copy's ROM window from the start of the BIOS image.
- `BiosAddressModel::in_kbless` (L234) — True when a normalized address falls inside the kbless copy window.
- `BiosAddressModel::is_install_slot` (L238) — True when a RAM address is exactly the start of a configured install slot.
- `BiosAddressModel::in_install_slot_range` (L242) — True when a RAM address falls anywhere inside a configured install slot.
- `BiosAddressModel::install_slot_at` (L249) — Returns the install slot that starts exactly at this RAM address, or null when there is none.
- `BiosAddressModel::rom_keyed_ram_lo` (L256) — Returns the low RAM address of the ROM-keyed copy window.
- `BiosAddressModel::rom_keyed_ram_hi_incl` (L259) — Returns the last RAM address, inclusive, of the ROM-keyed copy window.
- `BiosAddressModel::emit_normalize_c` (L267) — Emits C source for the normalize function that generated runtime code uses to compute dispatch keys.
- `BiosAddressModel::emit_key_home_pc_c` (L299) — Emits C source recording, for each dispatch key, the runtime PC that its home body was compiled for.

### recompiler/src/bios_call_names.cpp

Maps BIOS call table numbers (A0, B0, C0) and function indices to the names of the BIOS functions.

- `lookup` (L100) — Returns the name at an index of a BIOS call table, or an empty string when the index is out of range.
- `bios_call_name` (L108) — Returns "" when the index is out of range or intentionally uncarried.

### recompiler/src/bios_slice_walker.cpp

Walks BIOS code from the ROM bytes, decoding instructions and recording the ones the recompiler cannot translate.

- `read_u32_le` (L16) — Reads a little-endian 32-bit word from the ROM at an offset, throwing if the read would pass the end of the data.
- `format_name` (L28) — Returns the text name of an instruction format, such as R, I, J, SPECIAL or REGIMM.
- `record_unsupported` (L42) — Adds an entry for an instruction the walker could not handle, recording its address, raw word, format and the reason.
- `BiosSliceWalker::walk` (L55) — Walks BIOS code from a start address through the ROM bytes, collecting decoded instructions and unsupported words into a result.

### recompiler/src/cli_boot_path.cpp

Helpers for the command line tool that normalize a boot path and derive the file name and serial from it.

- `normalize_boot_path` (L8) — SYSTEM.CNF uses backslashes for disc-internal paths.
- `boot_filename` (L15) — Returns the file name part of a boot path after converting backslashes to slashes.
- `serial_from_boot` (L19) — Builds a serial ID from the boot file name by keeping only its letters and digits, uppercased.

### recompiler/src/code_generator.cpp

Static recompiler core that turns MIPS instructions and functions into generated C code, including timing, cull and hook logic.

- `should_print_reserved_opcode_warning` (L30) — Reserved MIPS-II branch-likely words often appear when discovery sweeps ASCII/data as code.
- `codegen_cyc_fold` (L40) — Cycle-step folding (psx_cyc_steps2..4): on by default; PSX_CODEGEN_CYC_FOLD=0 emits one psx_cyc_step per instruction as before (A/B).
- `codegen_cycle_per_insn` (L46) — Reports whether each instruction charges its own cycle cost at its site, which is on by default for accurate timing.
- `CodeGenerator::set_bios_address_model` (L66) — Stores the BIOS address model pointer that the generator uses for address normalization.
- `ram_to_rom` (L84) — Translate a runtime RAM address to an address that exe_.read_word() can resolve.
- `CodeGenerator::CodeGenerator` (L106) — Creates a code generator for an executable and config, setting the code segment from the load address.
- `emit_stale_static_guard` (L123) — Inter-piece host transfers (fallthrough into a split piece / the next function, and the legacy non-CPS split-target transfers) hand execution to another compiled dispatch entry WITHOUT passing the dis
- `emit_stale_static_guard_named` (L132) — Same guard when only the emitted function NAME is at hand (the fallthrough-to-next-function edges).
- `CodeGenerator::partial_block_cycle_count` (L144) — Returns the cycles to charge for entering a block mid-way, or zero when the address starts a full block.
- `CodeGenerator::emit_mid_block_cycle_charge` (L164) — Emits the cycle charge for a mid-block entry point, or an empty string when block or per-instruction timing already charges it.
- `CodeGenerator::emit_interrupt_check` (L185) — Emits the C code that checks interrupts at a resume PC given as a constant, flushing deferred block cycles first.
- `CodeGenerator::emit_interrupt_check_expr` (L192) — Same as emit_interrupt_check but takes the resume PC as a C expression string.
- `CodeGenerator::reg_name` (L199) — Returns the C expression for a MIPS register, such as cpu->gpr[4].
- `CodeGenerator::translate_addiu` (L206) — Translates ADDIU into C that adds the sign-extended immediate to rs and stores the result in rt.
- `CodeGenerator::translate_lui` (L224) — Translates LUI into C that loads the 16-bit immediate into the upper half of rt.
- `CodeGenerator::translate_lw` (L236) — Translates LW into C that loads a 32-bit word from rs plus the offset into rt.
- `CodeGenerator::translate_sw` (L252) — Translates SW into C that stores the 32-bit value of rt at rs plus the offset.
- `CodeGenerator::translate_or` (L265) — Translates OR into C that stores the bitwise or of rs and rt in rd.
- `CodeGenerator::translate_and` (L285) — Translates AND into C that stores the bitwise and of rs and rt in rd.
- `CodeGenerator::translate_sll` (L297) — Translates SLL into C that shifts rt left by the shift amount and stores the result in rd.
- `CodeGenerator::translate_srl` (L318) — Translates SRL into C that shifts rt right logically by the shift amount and stores the result in rd.
- `CodeGenerator::translate_slt` (L330) — Translates SLT into C that sets rd to 1 when rs is less than rt as signed values, otherwise 0.
- `CodeGenerator::translate_sltu` (L343) — Translates SLTU into C that sets rd to 1 when rs is less than rt as unsigned values, otherwise 0.
- `CodeGenerator::translate_addu` (L356) — Translates ADDU into C that adds rs and rt into rd, ignoring overflow.
- `CodeGenerator::translate_add` (L376) — Translates ADD into C by reusing the ADDU translation, since overflow traps are not emitted.
- `CodeGenerator::translate_subu` (L381) — Translates SUBU into C that subtracts rt from rs into rd, ignoring overflow.
- `CodeGenerator::translate_sub` (L393) — Translates SUB into C by reusing the SUBU translation, since overflow traps are not emitted.
- `CodeGenerator::translate_lb` (L398) — Translates LB into C that loads a sign-extended byte from memory into rt.
- `CodeGenerator::translate_lbu` (L413) — Translates LBU into C that loads a zero-extended byte from memory into rt.
- `CodeGenerator::translate_lh` (L428) — Translates LH into C that loads a sign-extended halfword from memory into rt.
- `CodeGenerator::translate_lhu` (L443) — Translates LHU into C that loads a zero-extended halfword from memory into rt.
- `CodeGenerator::translate_lwl` (L458) — Translates LWL into C, the left-part unaligned word load that merges bytes into rt.
- `CodeGenerator::translate_lwr` (L480) — Translates LWR into C, the right-part unaligned word load that merges bytes into rt.
- `CodeGenerator::translate_swl` (L500) — Translates SWL into C, the left-part unaligned word store.
- `CodeGenerator::translate_swr` (L515) — Translates SWR into C, the right-part unaligned word store.
- `CodeGenerator::translate_sb` (L530) — Translates SB into C that stores the low byte of rt to memory.
- `CodeGenerator::translate_sh` (L543) — Translates SH into C that stores the low halfword of rt to memory.
- `CodeGenerator::translate_sra` (L556) — Translates SRA into C that shifts rt right arithmetically by the shift amount and stores the result in rd.
- `CodeGenerator::translate_andi` (L568) — Translates ANDI into C that ANDs rs with the zero-extended immediate into rt.
- `CodeGenerator::translate_ori` (L580) — Translates ORI into C that ORs rs with the zero-extended immediate into rt.
- `CodeGenerator::translate_xori` (L597) — Translates XORI into C that XORs rs with the zero-extended immediate into rt.
- `CodeGenerator::translate_xor` (L609) — Translates XOR into C that stores the bitwise exclusive or of rs and rt in rd.
- `CodeGenerator::translate_nor` (L621) — Translates NOR into C that stores the inverted bitwise or of rs and rt in rd.
- `CodeGenerator::translate_sllv` (L641) — Translates SLLV into C that shifts rt left by the low five bits of rs and stores the result in rd.
- `CodeGenerator::translate_srlv` (L653) — Translates SRLV into C that shifts rt right logically by the low five bits of rs and stores the result in rd.
- `CodeGenerator::translate_srav` (L665) — Translates SRAV into C that shifts rt right arithmetically by the low five bits of rs and stores the result in rd.
- `CodeGenerator::translate_slti` (L677) — Translates SLTI into C that sets rt to 1 when rs is less than the signed immediate, otherwise 0.
- `CodeGenerator::translate_sltiu` (L690) — Translates SLTIU into C that sets rt to 1 when rs is less than the immediate as unsigned, otherwise 0.
- `CodeGenerator::translate_mult` (L703) — Translates MULT into C that multiplies rs and rt as signed values into the HI and LO registers.
- `CodeGenerator::translate_multu` (L712) — Translates MULTU into C that multiplies rs and rt as unsigned values into the HI and LO registers.
- `CodeGenerator::translate_div` (L721) — Translates DIV into C that divides rs by rt as signed values, leaving the quotient in LO and remainder in HI.
- `CodeGenerator::translate_divu` (L732) — Translates DIVU into C that divides rs by rt as unsigned values, leaving the quotient in LO and remainder in HI.
- `CodeGenerator::translate_mfhi` (L743) — Translates MFHI into C that copies the HI register into rd.
- `CodeGenerator::translate_mflo` (L756) — Translates MFLO into C that copies the LO register into rd.
- `CodeGenerator::translate_mthi` (L767) — Translates MTHI into C that copies rs into the HI register.
- `CodeGenerator::translate_mtlo` (L773) — Translates MTLO into C that copies rs into the LO register.
- `ws_screen_x_site` (L790) — Explicit branch-site kinds ([widescreen.cull] bltz_sites, bgez_sites, branch_keep_sites) name one conditional branch each.
- `CodeGenerator::check_explicit_branch_site` (L796) — Checks a conditional branch against the configured explicit branch sites and records a match; does nothing in overlay mode.
- `CodeGenerator::generate_branch_condition` (L817) — Returns the C condition expression for a branch, with widescreen cull masking applied when the branch matches a configured site.
- `CodeGenerator::mod_instruction_call` (L940) — Returns a call to a mod hook for this address when it is a configured mod instruction site, otherwise an empty string.
- `CodeGenerator::draw_distance_clamp_prefix` (L952) — [[draw_distance.clamp]]: a main-EXE ordering-table range guard.
- `block_timing_rewrite` (L988) — [recompiler] cpu_timing = "block" (docs/PERFORMANCE_MODES.md): the loads take the block helpers (psx_cyc.h psx_blk_*), which charge only the access, from the emitter's packed cost of this load (blk_pi
- `blk_pipe_run` (L1013) — The R3000A load-delay pipeline of psx_cyc.h (Beetle's ReadAbsorb / ReadFudge / LDAbsorb / LDWhich: psx_cyc_step, psx_cyc_load_*, psx_cyc_lwc2_read) run over a block's instructions in execution order,
- `blk_body_observes` (L1048) — A body that can see the guest clock (or hand it to the runtime): memory, GTE and mult/div timing, COP0, exceptions, calls, hooks.
- `ram_fast_rewrite` (L1066) — [recompiler] ram_fast_path (docs/PERFORMANCE_MODES.md): the plain-RAM entries (psx_store_* in memory.c, psx_cyc_load_byte_fast in psx_cyc.h) in place of the CPUState store pointers and the out-of-line
- `CodeGenerator::translate_instruction` (L1080) — Translates one instruction, adding the draw-distance clamp prefix and any mod hook call before its core translation.
- `CodeGenerator::translate_instruction_core` (L1095) — Translates one instruction's opcode into C statements, dispatching on the opcode and funct fields.
- `CodeGenerator::translate_basic_block` (L2144) — Emits the C code for one basic block, including its label, cycle charges and each of its instructions.
- `CodeGenerator::func_has_screen_extent_cull` (L3210) — True when a function has both a width and a height compare against the widescreen sets, the signature of a screen-extent cull.
- `CodeGenerator::detect_cull_bltz_sites` (L3236) — Finds the left-edge bltz branch addresses of a screen-extent cull and records them for the function.
- `CodeGenerator::detect_backdrop_windows` (L3261) — Detects backdrop window sites in a function and records them, when automatic backdrop preload is enabled.
- `CodeGenerator::generate_function` (L3287) — Generates the C function for one recompiled function from its blocks and fallthrough target.
- `CodeGenerator::scan_jr_tables` (L3582) — Scans the blocks of a function for jr jump tables and adds their target addresses to the output edge map.
- `CodeGenerator::generate_alias_group` (L3619) — Generates C functions for a group of alias entries that share the same code.

Loads and validates the BIOS, game, options and user settings TOML files, and writes the user settings back to disk.

- `pad_mode_to_string` (L305) — Returns the settings name for a pad mode; it never returns hybrid, which is a runtime-only request and not a saved preference.

- `parse_hex` (L322) — Parses a hex string into a 32-bit value, throwing an error that names the field when the text is not valid hex.
- `parse_sxy_cull_site` (L339) — One [[widescreen.cull.sxy]] entry.
- `parse_aspect_ratio` (L440) — Parse a display aspect "W:H" string (e.g.
- `validate_project_relative` (L470) — Reject a config path that is not confined to the project directory.
- `parse_runtime_block` (L500) — Parse the optional [runtime] block.
- `find_project_root` (L1462) — Locate the project root by walking upward from 'config_path' until a directory containing '.gitignore', '.git', or 'CMakeLists.txt' is found.
- `draw_distance_clamp_reads` (L1483) — True when 'instr' is an ALU instruction (I-type or SPECIAL R-type, not a load, store, branch or jump) that reads GPR 'reg'.

- `quality_key_player_editable` (L1563) — True when a quality setting key may be changed by the player.
- `quality_key_supported` (L1568) — [quality.<name>] -- a named graphics preset (docs/QUALITY_PRESETS.md).
- `parse_quality_presets` (L1574) — Parses the quality presets of a game config into a list, checking each key against the supported set.
- `derive_out_stem` (L1627) — Derives an output name stem from a ROM file name by removing its extension, matched without regard to case.
- `load_bios_config` (L1644) — Load a BIOS config TOML.
- `load_game_config` (L1917) — Load a game config TOML.

- `upsert_game_toml_controller_bool` (L4040) — Sets a boolean key in the controller section of a game TOML file, adding or updating it, and returns whether the write succeeded.

### recompiler/src/config_loader.h

Declarations and inline helpers for config loading: pad binding limits and the video filter and edge mode names.

- `pad_bind_value_ok` (L60) — True when a pad binding value is within the allowed range, from zero up to the maximum.
- `video_fmv_filter_name` (L73) — Canonical settings.toml / game.toml spelling for each value, and its parse.

### recompiler/src/control_flow.cpp

- `ControlFlowAnalyzer::analysis_walk_hi` (L178) — Returns the upper address bound for walking a function: its alias range end, or the executable's analysis end.
- `ControlFlowAnalyzer::find_block_boundaries` (L195) — NOTE: find_block_boundaries / build_basic_blocks / link_basic_blocks below are NOT on the live path — analyze_function does its own single-pass walk (see the comment there).

- `ControlFlowAnalyzer::link_basic_blocks` (L303) — Sets the successor links between basic blocks from the exit instruction of each block.
- `rebuild_control_flow_metadata` (L349) — Recomputes the loops and metadata of a control flow graph, including any extra entry points.
- `ControlFlowAnalyzer::analyze_function` (L474) — Builds the control flow graph for one function, covering its blocks, edges and entries.
- `ControlFlowAnalyzer::analyze_all_functions` (L610) — Builds a control flow graph for every function in the list, keyed by start address.

### recompiler/src/function_analysis.cpp

Finds function starts and boundaries in a PS1 executable from prologues, return instructions, jump tables and exact control flow rules.

- `FunctionAnalyzer::FunctionAnalyzer` (L10) — Creates a function analyzer over the given executable.
- `FunctionAnalyzer::add_forced_entry` (L12) — Adds an address as a forced function entry point when it lies inside the executable's analysis range.
- `FunctionAnalyzer::is_jr_ra` (L19) — True when an instruction is jr $ra, the usual function return.

- `FunctionAnalyzer::is_epilogue` (L42) — True when an instruction is addiu $sp, $sp, +N, a stack frame teardown, and returns the size.

- `is_sw_reg_base` (L162) — True when an instruction stores value_reg with a store word to the offset of base_reg.
- `is_sw_reg_sp` (L169) — True when an instruction stores value_reg to the stack pointer with a store word.
- `is_lui` (L173) — True when an instruction is LUI, returning the register it loads.
- `is_nop` (L180) — True when an instruction word is zero, which is the MIPS nop.
- `skip_leading_padding_nops` (L184) — Skips zero padding words at the start of a function, within a 32-byte limit, and returns the first address that is not padding.
- `is_load_from_reg_base` (L203) — True when an instruction loads a word from the offset of base_reg, returning the destination register.
- `is_load_imm_zero` (L224) — True when an instruction loads a 16-bit immediate from zero into a register, returning that register.
- `preprologue_window_is_valid` (L232) — Checks that the words before a prologue form a valid setup window that does not start before the function start.
- `find_preprologue_setup_start` (L285) — Finds where the setup code before a prologue begins, returning that address through setup_start_out when found.
- `pointer_target_has_near_prologue` (L308) — True when a pointer target address has a prologue close by inside the executable's range.
- `FunctionAnalyzer::find_function_start` (L338) — Scans backward from a return address to the start of its function, using prologues and 16-byte alignment as guides.
- `FunctionAnalyzer::is_likely_data_section` (L414) — Heuristically decides whether an address range is data rather than code, for ranges of at least 100 bytes.
- `exact_is_jr_ra_word` (L505) — True when the word is exactly jr $ra (0x03E00008).
- `exact_is_addiu_sp_neg` (L509) — True when the word is addiu $sp, $sp with a negative immediate, which is a frame setup.
- `exact_is_valid_mips_word` (L517) — Forwards to the analyzer's valid MIPS word check.
- `exact_branch_target` (L521) — Returns the target address of a branch at pc, from its sign-extended offset relative to pc plus 4.
- `exact_jump_target` (L526) — Returns the target address of a J or JAL at pc, built from the top bits of pc plus 4 and the 26-bit index.
- `exact_instruction_writes_gpr` (L530) — True when an instruction writes the given general register; register zero is never written.
- `exact_resolve_constant_transfer` (L575) — Resolve the common absolute indirect-transfer idiom within one basic block: lui rN, hi(target) addiu/ori rN, rN, lo(target) jr/jalr rN The backward scan stops at control flow or any intervening write
- `exact_classify_cf` (L658) — Classifies the instruction at pc into a control flow kind with its targets, for the exact analysis.
- `resolve_computed_stride_jump` (L1138) — Tries to resolve a computed jump with a fixed stride from an entry point, bounded by a hard cap; true when the targets are found.
- `resolve_self_limited_jump_table` (L1294) — Tries to resolve a jump table whose bounds come from the table itself, bounded by a hard cap; true when resolved.
- `FunctionAnalyzer::analyze_exact_entries` (L1418) — Runs the exact analysis from the given entry points, using producer ranges and allowed cross-function calls, and returns the result.
- `FunctionAnalyzer::analyze` (L1792) — Runs the full function analysis over the executable and returns the discovered functions and counts.

- `psx_store_cycle_barrier` (L87) — Flushes overlay cycle counts before a store; it does nothing in a build without overlays.
- `psx_slice_block` (L183) — Runs a precise slice of a block for the CPU, returning 0 when precise slicing is off and the slice result otherwise.
- `psx_call_contract` (L328) — Validate a direct call site after the callee's C return.
- `debug_server_log_call_entry` (L378) — Records the address of the function just entered, for the debug server's call log.

### runtime/include/dirty_ram_interp.h

Dirty RAM tracking helpers that classify physical addresses into overlay regions and PS1 code segments.

- `phys_is_overlay_region` (L167) — 1 iff phys is runtime-loaded overlay RAM rather than main-EXE text — either side of the text image.
- `overlay_cache_window_contains` (L202) — Capture/candidate window membership.
- `psx_code_segment_index` (L331) — Returns the index of the code segment a PC belongs to: 0 for KUSEG, 1 for KSEG0, 2 for KSEG1, or -1 for other addresses.
- `psx_code_segment_base` (L339) — Returns the base address of a code segment given its index.
- `psx_code_segment_name` (L343) — The names the capture JSON and the per-segment cache directories use.
- `dirty_ram_dispatch_evidence_clear` (L353) — Clear dispatch evidence (the any-segment bitmap and its segment siblings) for 'nwords' bitmap words from 'first_word'.

### runtime/include/display_scanout.h

Renderer-neutral helpers that compute the PS1 display's canvas height, interlacing and vertical layout.

- `psx_display_present_height` (L26) — Depth24 staging expands the visible source into the full active-video canvas.
- `psx_display_interlaced_rows` (L32) — Doubles the row count when the display is interlaced, otherwise returns the row count unchanged.
- `psx_display_clip_source_height` (L40) — Canvas-origin clipping belongs only to staged depth24 presentation.
- `psx_display_source_height` (L55) — Preserve the legacy default for an unset/degenerate GP1(07h) range.
- `psx_display_vertical_layout` (L65) — Intersect a GP1(07h) range with the PAL or NTSC active region.
- `psx_display_vertical_offset` (L98) — Return the vertical position of a GP1(07h) display range relative to the broadcast centre.

### runtime/include/draw_distance.h

Draw-distance clamp helper that computes the value a clamp leaves in a register.

- `psx_draw_distance_clamp_value` (L62) — The value the clamp leaves in the register.

### runtime/include/execution_identity.h

Identity helper that binds a network session to a fixed execution implementation.

- `psx_execution_content_identity` (L10) — Bind every network session, including a no-mod LAN session, to its fixed execution implementation.

### runtime/include/frame_fingerprint.h

Per-frame fingerprint of RAM, scratchpad and MMIO writes, used to compare runs cycle by cycle.

- `psx_fp_write_term` (L55) — One write's contribution to wsum: the splitmix64 finalizer of (phys,val).
- `psx_fp_write_eligible` (L65) — Main RAM (phys < ram_live_bytes) and scratchpad feed the fingerprint; anything else a RAM write path reports is ignored.
- `psx_fp_record_write` (L71) — Adds one RAM or scratchpad write to the fingerprint; scratchpad writes are hashed separately and writes outside live RAM are ignored.
- `psx_fp_record_mmio` (L94) — Adds one memory-mapped I/O access, with its address, value and pc, to the MMIO hash and counter.
- `psx_fp_note_quiet` (L108) — A write FMV-quiet kept out of the fingerprint.

### runtime/include/gl_scale_limits.h

Limits for high-resolution OpenGL scaling, computing surface sizes, memory budgets and scale clamps.

- `psx_gl_full_vram_bytes` (L40) — Bytes of the full-VRAM hr surface (colour + depth-stencil) at scale s.
- `psx_gl_full_vram_fits` (L49) — 1 if a full-VRAM surface at scale s fits max_dim and budget_bytes.
- `psx_gl_clamp_full_vram_scale` (L59) — Largest scale <= req whose full-VRAM surface fits.
- `psx_gl_max_wide_width` (L80) — Widest native-wide surface (in native px) that fits max_dim at scale s.
- `psx_gl_native_wide_width` (L91) — Native-wide surface width (native px) for a display disp_w px wide at aspect num:den: the display plus two margins of disp_w*(3*num - 4*den)/(8*den), rounded exactly as gpu.c's ws_nw_configured_offset
- `psx_gl_fit_wide_aspect` (L104) — Narrow num:den, if needed, to the widest aspect whose native-wide surface is at most max_w native px (psx_gl_max_wide_width) at display width disp_w; 4:3 when not even one more column fits.
- `psx_gl_window_bytes` (L125) — Windowed high-resolution mode: the authoritative VRAM stays at 1x and only a window of the displayed columns (window_w native px, full 512-row height) is kept at S.
- `psx_gl_clamp_window_scale` (L130) — Lowers a requested scale until the windowed surface fits the ceiling, the maximum dimension and the byte budget, never below 1.
- `psx_gl_budget_bytes_from_env` (L147) — Parse a budget override in MiB (PSX_GL_VRAM_BUDGET_MB).

### runtime/include/gpu_primitive_reject.h

Rejects triangles and lines whose size exceeds the PS1 hardware limits.

- `psx_gpu_triangle_oversize` (L9) — PS1 hardware primitive-size rejection.
- `psx_gpu_line_oversize` (L27) — True when a line spans more than 1023 pixels horizontally or more than 511 vertically.

### runtime/include/gpu_projective_clip.h

Projective clipping helpers that clip triangles against camera depth and screen planes before dividing.

- `psx_projective_lerp` (L10) — Linearly interpolates every field of two projected vertices by t and returns the blended vertex.
- `psx_projective_distance` (L19) — Returns the signed distance of a projected vertex from one of the five clip planes, where plane 0 is the near plane.
- `psx_projective_clip_triangle` (L29) — Clips a projected triangle against the five planes, writes up to 12 output vertices into out and returns how many.

### runtime/include/gpu_vram_dirty.h

Dirty-row marking helper for GPU VRAM, kept inline so the hot path makes no call.

- `gpu_vram_dirty_mark_row` (L53) — Hot path: offline compiles to load + not-taken branch, no call.

### runtime/include/host_file_identity.h

Host file identity helper that gives a file an identity so caches can tell files apart.

- `host_file_identity` (L16) — A failed identity is never a cache hit.

### runtime/include/host_launch_timing.h

Records always-on timing of host launch stages in a ring buffer that the debug TCP reader can read.

- `host_launch_timing_ring` (L96) — Returns the process-wide ring buffer that stores completed host launch timing scopes.
- `host_launch_timing_parent` (L102) — Returns this thread's current parent timing scope, so nested scopes link to the scope that encloses them.
- `host_launch_now_us` (L106) — Returns the current steady-clock time in microseconds, used to stamp launch timing scopes.

### runtime/include/internal_resolution.h

Defines the Internal resolution presets, their persisted values, and the integer render scale each one asks the renderer for.

- `psx_ir_lower_eq` (L51) — Compares two strings for equality ignoring ASCII case of the first; b must already be lowercase. Returns 1 when equal.
- `psx_ir_value_valid` (L60) — 1 if value is a legal encoding (unset excluded).
- `psx_ir_parse` (L68) — Parse a persisted value: a preset id (case-insensitive) or a decimal line count in [PSX_IR_MIN_LINES, PSX_IR_MAX_LINES].
- `psx_ir_id_for` (L83) — The preset id for a value, or NULL for a custom line count (persist those as an integer).
- `psx_ir_label_for` (L89) — Returns the display label of the preset matching a value, or NULL when the value is a custom line count.
- `psx_ir_scale_for` (L97) — Unclamped scale a value asks for.
- `psx_resolve_internal_scale` (L108) — The scale to request: psx_ir_scale_for clamped to [1, s_max].
- `psx_ss_milli_clamp` (L126) — Clamps a supersample factor in thousandths to the allowed minimum and maximum.
- `psx_ss_parse_milli` (L132) — "1.5", "2", "2x" -> 1500, 2000, 2000.
- `psx_resolve_internal_scale_ss` (L147) — psx_resolve_internal_scale with the supersample factor on the target.
- `psx_ir_from_supersampling` (L167) — A legacy [video] supersampling factor as a value the launcher can show: the preset that resolves to the same scale (1 -> Native, 3 -> 720p, 5 -> 1080p, 6 -> 1440p, 9 -> 4K, 12 -> 5K, 18 -> 8K at 240 l
- `psx_ir_launcher_seed_supersampling` (L192) — The value seeded into the legacy Supersampling row.
- `psx_ir_adopt_launcher` (L216) — What the host adopts when the launcher returns.
- `psx_dynres_floor_scale` (L251) — ---- Dynamic resolution floor ([video] dynamic_resolution_min) ------------- A preset or line count resolves as usual.

### runtime/include/launcher_device.h

Converts controller and device names between the launcher's C ABI source codes and the stored device strings.

- `launcher_controller_can_share` (L11) — Returns true only in a developer build when the controller GUID matches exactly, which allows sharing a controller.
- `trim_launcher_device` (L16) — Returns the device string with leading and trailing whitespace removed.
- `normalize_launcher_device` (L24) — Trims the device string and lowercases it so device names compare reliably.
- `launcher_source_from_device` (L31) — Maps a device name to a source code: 0 for none or empty, 1 for keyboard, 2 for any gamepad.
- `launcher_device_from_source` (L38) — Maps a source code back to a device string: none, keyboard, or the previous gamepad name, or gamepad when none was set.
- `resolve_player_mode_after_launcher` (L81) — Pad mode for one seat on the way OUT of the launcher.

### runtime/include/mdec_capture.h

Declares the MDEC command capture format and functions that record decoder commands for offline replay and comparison.

- `mdec_fnv1a64` (L40) — Computes the 64-bit FNV-1a hash of n bytes, used to compare decoder output by hash.

### runtime/include/mod_capcom_bg2d.h

Helpers for Capcom's 16-pixel tile backgrounds: map tile lookup, scroll and parallax view mapping, and background packet rendering.

- `psx_capcom_ram_range` (L25) — Returns 1 when n bytes at physical address p lie inside the valid main RAM window.
- `psx_capcom_map_tile` (L30) — Reads the 16-bit metatile value at a screen pixel position from the authored map, or 0 when out of range.
- `psx_capcom_tile_uvclut` (L44) — Packs a tile descriptor into a combined UV and CLUT word, using the page and palette bits and the CLUT base.
- `psx_capcom_floor_div` (L51) — Integer division that rounds toward negative infinity instead of toward zero.
- `psx_capcom_scroll_view` (L58) — The title evaluates its retail scroll mapping at the camera and at the wider view's left edge.
- `psx_capcom_parallax_view` (L70) — Returns the view for a parallax plane by dividing the camera position by the plane's divisor before scrolling.
- `psx_capcom_background_activate` (L80) — Allocates the GPU DMA arena for the given number of background layers and hands it to the GPU; returns 0 on failure.
- `psx_capcom_background_render` (L92) — Return emitted packet count, or -1 if setup is invalid.

### runtime/include/mod_memory.h

Defines the enhancement DMA aperture and the address helpers that let trusted mods place GPU primitives in a larger arena.

- `psx_mod_gpu_dma_aperture_offset_for` (L26) — Maps a CPU address inside the enhancement aperture to its offset and returns 1; returns 0 for addresses outside it or an oversized used count.
- `psx_mod_gpu_dma_resolve_address_for` (L46) — Fold DMA addresses through live main RAM unless the address is inside the portion of the enhancement aperture that has actually been allocated.
- `psx_gpu_packet_key_for` (L65) — Identity of a GPU packet word at 'address' (a CPU pointer or a DMA tag): the allocated enhancement aperture keeps its own physical address, main RAM folds to its word-aligned live offset.

### runtime/include/mod_packages.h

Declares the mod package system: how trusted mod plugins are described, loaded, and how their media preparers are registered.

- `mod_register_media_preparer` (L342) — Implementations are linked trusted code.

### runtime/include/mod_runtime.h

Declares the mod runtime entry points that initialize the runtime, commit a disc, and prepare launcher and netplay plans.

- `mod_runtime_initialize` (L17) — Sets up the mod runtime for a game under the given root, game id and entry PC; returns false and sets error on failure.
- `mod_runtime_commit` (L22) — Commits the disc at disc_path to the mod runtime, optionally saving the selection; returns false and sets error on failure.
- `mod_runtime_prepare_for_launcher` (L26) — Prepare a preboot launcher selection; the audited runtime retains a ticket.
- `mod_runtime_commit_for_netplay` (L40) — Apply a host-published online/LAN plan without rewriting persisted offline choices.
- `mod_runtime_commit_netplay` (L49) — Install only the executable's trusted simulation profile (if registered).

### runtime/include/mod_session_baseline.h

Records the scalar host settings a trusted mod can change on the first session, then restores them at each later session start.

- `psx_mod_session_baseline_apply` (L39) — native_vblank_forced: psx_mod_set_native_vblank_rate() owns the frame periods.

### runtime/include/mod_visible_placements.h

Tracks which authored placements are visible and reports the newly exposed strips between two view rectangles.

- `psx_placement_contains` (L9) — Returns 1 when a point lies strictly inside the rectangle's bounds.
- `psx_placement_exposed` (L14) — Return only newly exposed strips.

### runtime/include/netplay_content_gate.h

Checks that both peers agree on a 256-bit content plan hash, fragment by fragment, before netplay continues.

- `np_content_init` (L10) — Loads the 64-character hex plan hash and the occupied slots into the gate; returns 0 on bad input, 1 when no hash is given.
- `np_content_note` (L27) — Records a fragment received from another slot and flags a mismatch when its words differ from the local plan.
- `np_content_ready` (L40) — Returns 1 when the gate is disabled, or when nothing mismatched and every occupied slot matched and was acknowledged.

### runtime/include/netplay_fmv_confirm.h

Counts hash-confirmed ticks after a movie so rollback netplay knows when both peers agreed enough to unlock prediction.

- `rb_fmv_confirm_gain` (L16) — Confirmed ticks gained when the confirmed frontier moves from 'from' (the highest tick already counted, or the movie's end) to 'resolved'.

### runtime/include/netplay_input_hist.h

Compares and corrects pad input history frames so rollback netplay can decide whether a stick value must be replaced or rewound.

- `netplay_ih_extra_pad_differ` (L35) — The portable stick contract deliberately omits controller type and RX/RY.
- `netplay_ih_pad_payload_equal` (L41) — Returns 1 when two pad frames have the same buttons and stick values and no extra pad fields differ.
- `netplay_ih_pad_correction_decide` (L48) — Decides whether a wire pad frame may replace the published one, returning a rewind when extra pad data differs for a completed tick.

### runtime/include/netplay_load_probe.h

Remembers the verified local save probe so a guest that already applied the host's exact save bytes does not restore them twice.

- `psx_netplay_load_probe_clear` (L19) — Resets the probe to empty: not valid, not applied, no slot, zero size and CRC.
- `psx_netplay_load_probe_record` (L29) — Stores a new local probe for a slot with its size and CRC; it is valid only when the size is nonzero and not yet applied.
- `psx_netplay_load_probe_mark_applied` (L41) — Marks the recorded probe as applied locally, but only when it is valid and belongs to the same slot.
- `psx_netplay_load_probe_can_reuse` (L51) — All four fingerprints are required: local probe, completed local apply, authoritative wire blob, and a fresh read of the still-unmodified save slot.

### runtime/include/netplay_local_view.h

Holds the host-only display sub-rectangle a title requests for the local netplay seat; it is never sent to peers.

- `psx_netplay_local_view_reset` (L25) — Clears the local view record to zero.
- `psx_netplay_local_view_set` (L31) — Rejects empty rectangles and anything outside 1024x512 VRAM space.
- `psx_netplay_local_view_get` (L53) — 1 and the rectangle when a request is still current at 'now' and fits a display of display_w x display_h; 0 otherwise.
- `psx_netplay_local_view_shed_step` (L92) — Updates the shed state from how far the remote seat leads; turns shedding on when far behind and holds it for a set number of ticks.

### runtime/include/netplay_peer_frontier.h

Tracks each seat's resolved frontier for rollback episodes, so the initiator opens at or below the slowest follower.

- `netplay_peer_frontier_reset` (L25) — Clears all per-seat frontier records to zero.
- `netplay_peer_frontier_note` (L32) — A RESOLVED advert from 'seat'.
- `netplay_peer_frontier_clamp` (L43) — Evidence above 'tick' was invalidated (realign) or a follower proved it cannot follow above it (NACK): no seat may stay above it.
- `netplay_peer_frontier_min` (L55) — Frontier every seat in 'seats' has reached: the lowest, and 0 while any of them has not advertised yet.
- `netplay_fork_cap_retired` (L78) — §55 bisect cap: after a baseline mismatch at load L the next load must be below L.
- `netplay_rb_concurrent_begin` (L95) — Concurrent BEGIN while an episode is active.

### runtime/include/netplay_sim_pad_cache.h

Host-only cache of the normalized pad rows published for each simulation tick, so a rollback can read them back.

- `psx_netplay_sim_pad_cache_reset` (L21) — Clears the validity flag of every seat in the cache.
- `psx_netplay_sim_pad_cache_publish` (L26) — Stores a seat's pad row for a tick and marks the seat valid, overwriting any earlier row for that seat.
- `psx_netplay_sim_pad_cache_read` (L36) — Copies the stored pad row for a seat and tick into out and returns 1; returns 0 when the seat, tick or entry does not match.

### runtime/include/openxr_color.h

Picks the OpenXR swapchain color format, preferring sRGB and falling back to RGBA8, or 0 when neither is offered.

- `psx_xr_color_format` (L6) — Returns the sRGB8 alpha format if the runtime offers it, otherwise RGBA8 if offered, otherwise 0.

### runtime/include/overlay_dispatch_preamble.c.inc

Overlay DLL dispatch shim that forwards the CPU, GTE, widescreen and PGXP calls to the host through a table of callbacks.

- `overlay_flush_cycles` (L8) — Publishes the overlay's batched CPU cycles to the host's cpu_charge callback and clears the pending count.
- `overlay_abi` (L29) — Returns the overlay ABI version combined with the build flavor, so the host can check compatibility.
- `overlay_init` (L33) — Stores the host's callback table and points the bail and last-store PC pointers at the host's state.
- `psx_dispatch_call` (L42) — Flushes pending cycles, then forwards a function dispatch to the host using register 31 as the return address.
- `psx_check_interrupts` (L47) — Called from the dispatch loop after each function returns.
- `psx_check_interrupts_at` (L51) — Interrupt check with the compiled guest PC to resume if a game-installed handler later RFEs to the sentinel outside the synchronous host window.
- `psx_cpu_charge` (L61) — The CPU charge (psx_cycles.h): overlay code is guest CPU work, so its charges accumulate here raw and publish through cpu_charge, the host's psx_cpu_charge, which applies [timing] guest_cycle_scale ex
- `psx_advance_cycles` (L65) — Adds the given cycles to the CPU charge through psx_cpu_charge.
- `gte_execute` (L66) — GTE (COP2) — defined in runtime/src/gte.cpp
- `psx_syscall` (L70) — Trap trampolines — defined in runtime/src/traps.c psx_syscall returns 1 if control transfers (cpu->pc set to a dispatch target; the caller must return to the trampoline), 0 for a directly-handled "voi
- `psx_native_bad_entry` (L74) — Fail-closed native entry guard: a function's CPS entry-switch calls this when dispatched at a PC that is not one of its legal entries (foreign interior PC from a range-ownership mismatch).
- `psx_unknown_dispatch` (L78) — Unknown dispatch — defined in runtime/src/traps.c
- `debug_server_log_call_entry` (L82) — Forwards a function entry address to the host's debug call log, when one is installed.
- `psx_restore_state_escape` (L85) — longjmp back to psx_check_interrupts for RestoreState redirection.
- `psx_rfe_mark_escape` (L94) — RFE escape marker (ABI v12): emitted at every 'rfe', including in overlay-resident exception-context code.
- `psx_game_text_native_ok` (L105) — Stale-static guard (ABI v22).
- `psx_cyc_load_word` (L112) — Faithful-timing functions (ABI v9): overlay code built with PSX_ENABLE_BLOCK_CYCLES emits these; forward to the runtime's real impls so native overlays charge cycles on the SAME timeline as the interp
- `psx_cyc_load_half` (L116) — Forwards a 16-bit load with its timing to the host, falling back to a plain read when no callback exists.
- `psx_cyc_load_byte` (L120) — Forwards an 8-bit load with its timing to the host, falling back to a plain byte read when no callback exists.
- `psx_cyc_lwc2_read` (L124) — Forwards a GTE LWC2 data read with its timing to the host, falling back to a plain word read when no callback exists.
- `psx_icache_fetch` (L128) — Flushes pending cycles and reports an instruction fetch at addr to the host's instruction cache model.
- `psx_muldiv_set` (L132) — Mult/div completion-stall timing (psx_cycles.c).
- `psx_muldiv_stall` (L136) — Flushes pending cycles and asks the host to stall for an unfinished multiply or divide.
- `psx_mult_latency_s` (L140) — Returns the signed multiply latency for rs from the host, or 0 when no callback exists.
- `psx_mult_latency_u` (L143) — Returns the unsigned multiply latency for rs from the host, or 0 when no callback exists.
- `psx_gte_stall` (L146) — Flushes pending cycles and asks the host to stall until the GTE is ready.
- `psx_gte_read` (L150) — MFC2/CFC2 GTE register read: stall to the deadline AND arm the load-delay give-back (ld_absorb=gte_ts_done-now, ld_which_t=rt) — Beetle MFC2/CFC2.
- `psx_slice_block` (L154) — Forwards a basic block's cycle cost to the host's slice function and returns its result, or 0 when none exists.
- `gte_read_data` (L169) — GTE special-register accessors (ABI v10).
- `gte_read_ctrl` (L173) — Flushes pending cycles and forwards a GTE control register read to the host.
- `gte_write_data` (L177) — Flushes pending cycles and forwards a GTE data register write to the host.
- `gte_write_ctrl` (L181) — Flushes pending cycles and forwards a GTE control register write to the host.
- `psx_ws_backdrop_x` (L188) — Widescreen hooks (ABI v3): forward to the runtime's live widescreen state.
- `psx_ws_x_margin` (L191) — Per-side X cull-margin (screen/world units) emitted into the game's draw- cull immediates by the recompiler ([widescreen.cull]); 0 unless stretching.
- `ovl_overdraw` (L196) — Overdraw guard band (ABI v31), added by the screen-cull helpers below only; same as gpu.c ws_cull_xm / psx_ws_cull_sltiu_y.
- `ovl_cull_xm` (L197) — Returns the widescreen cull margin plus the overdraw guard band, used for X-axis cull tests.
- `psx_ws_cull_sltiu` (L205) — Shared render-funnel screen-X cull widening ([widescreen.cull] auto_screen_x).
- `psx_ws_cull_sltiu_y` (L210) — Widescreen Y cull test: returns 1 when the screen Y is below the bound widened by the overdraw margin.
- `psx_ws_cull_sltu_band` (L216) — MUST stay byte-for-byte identical to gpu.c psx_ws_cull_sltu_band.
- `psx_ws_cull_slti` (L225) — Signed-funnel variants (min/max + center±halfwidth idioms).
- `psx_ws_cull_slti_lower` (L228) — Signed widescreen lower-bound cull: returns 1 when the screen X is below the immediate minus the margin.
- `psx_ws_cull_bltz` (L232) — Returns 1 when the screen X is below the negative cull margin, the widescreen bltz reject.
- `psx_ws_cull_bgez` (L239) — [widescreen.cull] bgez_sites and clip_edge_x_load_sites.
- `psx_ws_clip_edge_x` (L242) — [widescreen.cull] clip_edge_x_load_sites: a loaded screen-X clip bound of 0 becomes -margin and one of 'w' becomes w+margin; interior bounds and 4:3 are unchanged (see ws_cull_edge.h).
- `psx_ws_cull_lui_hi` (L248) — [widescreen.cull] screen_x_sites on 'lui' and 'bltz' (a screen X in the high half of a register).
- `psx_ws_cull_bltz_hi` (L251) — Returns 1 when a screen X held in the high half of v is left of the negative margin.
- `psx_ws_cull_vxrange` (L254) — Returns 1 when a vertex X falls inside the range widened by the margin around the immediate bound.
- `psx_ws_sprite_tag` (L260) — Forwards a sprite tag update to the host's widescreen state, when a callback exists.
- `psx_ws_backdrop_value` (L265) — Widescreen backdrop column-preload value (ABI v4).
- `psx_ws_player_x_bound` (L275) — Typed native-wide signed player-X bound (ABI v13).
- `psx_ws_screen_x_bound` (L278) — Widen a signed screen-pixel edge loaded by an explicitly guarded site.
- `psx_mod_instruction` (L281) — Flushes pending cycles and reports an executed instruction at an address to the mod host callback.
- `psx_mod_function_entry` (L285) — Reports a function entry at address to the mod host and returns its answer, or 0 when no callback exists.
- `psx_ws_depth_bound` (L289) — Widescreen depth bound: the host's adjusted value for imm, or imm unchanged when no callback exists.
- `psx_ws_plane_nx` (L292) — Widescreen plane X normal: the host's adjusted nx value, or nx unchanged when no callback exists.
- `psx_ws_xclip_bound` (L295) — Widescreen X clip bound: the host's adjusted bound, or the vanilla value when no callback exists.
- `psx_ws_cull_sxy_and` (L299) — [[widescreen.cull.sxy]] fold AND (ws_cull_edge.h).
- `psx_ws_cull_keep_result` (L302) — Widescreen cull keep result: the host's chosen result, or the vanilla result when no callback exists.

### runtime/include/overlay_loader.h

Overlay loader header: caches overlay DLLs after disc DMA, loads them, and dispatches their compiled functions ahead of the interpreter.

- `psx_overlay_code_segment_pc` (L36) — Returns 1 when a PC lies in the overlay code segment, which tells overlay code apart from game code.

### runtime/include/packet_address_index.h

Small hash index from packet addresses to array indexes, used by packet guards to find a node quickly.

- `psx_packet_address_bucket` (L10) — Hashes an address into a bucket index for a table whose capacity is a power of two.
- `psx_packet_address_index_clear` (L13) — Zeroes every slot of the index table.
- `psx_packet_address_index_add` (L16) — Adds an address with its index to the table; the first insertion of an address wins and duplicates are ignored.
- `psx_packet_address_index_find` (L23) — Returns the index stored for an address, or UINT32_MAX when the address is not in the table.

### runtime/include/pgxp_fast.h

Inline fast paths for PGXP's light memory mode: handles the common word loads, stores and register moves before falling back to the full hook.

- `pgxp_fast_unmarked` (L69) — The slot of a word access has no live bit (1), has one (0), or the hook must decide (-1).
- `pgxp_fast_load` (L84) — 1: done (psx_pgxp_load would have done exactly this), 0: call it.
- `pgxp_fast_store` (L100) — 1: done (psx_pgxp_store would have returned without a change), 0: call it.
- `pgxp_fast_move` (L115) — The ALU hook outside CPU mode is pgxp.cpp alu_halves alone.
- `pgxp_fast_alu` (L134) — 1: done (psx_pgxp_alu would have done exactly this), 0: call it.

### runtime/include/pgxp_session.h

Decides which PGXP corrections (geometry, texture, CPU mode) a session arms, from environment overrides, video settings and mod requests.

- `psx_pgxp_session_resolve` (L73) — Resolves which corrections a session arms from its inputs, using the video settings unless the session is mod-only.
- `psx_pgxp_session_env_flag` (L94) — Parse one of the env overrides: unset -> -1, "0" or empty -> 0, else 1 (the rule the runtime has always used for them).

### runtime/include/playtest_diagnostic_paths.h

Finds the executable and folder locations used for playtest diagnostic output, with a temp-folder fallback that never touches saves or settings.

- `psx_playtest_diagnostic_application_directory` (L38) — Returns the folder that holds the running executable, or the current folder if that path is empty.
- `psx_playtest_diagnostic_utf8` (L43) — Converts a filesystem path to a UTF-8 byte string.
- `psx_playtest_diagnostic_session_directory` (L48) — Creates and returns the diagnostics folder for a session under the application folder, falling back to the temp folder; the game id is sanitized first.

### runtime/include/projection_scale.hpp

Validates and parses a projection scale given as text, accepting finite values from above zero up to 8.

- `psx_projection_scale_valid` (L6) — Returns true when the value is finite, above zero and at most 8.0.

Little-endian field readers and writers for portable save-state blobs, so the same bytes come out on every platform.

- `pst_r_u8` (L58) — Reads one unsigned byte into v.

- `pst_r_i32` (L111) — Reads a signed 32-bit value into v.

- `pst_r_bool` (L122) — Reads one byte as a flag into v, set to 1 when nonzero and 0 otherwise.

- `pst_r_pod` (L159) — Reads nbytes into dst as elem-sized units; returns 0 when nbytes is not a multiple of elem. Byte order is handled for units of 2, 4 or 8 bytes.

### runtime/include/psx_controller_type.h

### runtime/include/psx_cyc.h

Models the R3000A load-delay pipeline interlock for CPU cycle timing only, so every backend charges the same guest cycle costs.

- `psx_cyc_bb_defer_begin` (L51) — The overlay shim already batches cycle charges until a host callback edge.
- `psx_cyc_bb_defer_end` (L52) — Ends a deferred cycle batch; in this build variant it does nothing, while the deferring variant decrements the depth and flushes at zero.
- `psx_cyc_bb_defer_flush` (L53) — Publishes the batched cycle charges now through the overlay's pending-cycle flush.
- `psx_cyc_local_begin` (L54) — Starts a local cycle accumulator; in this build variant it ignores acc and does nothing.
- `psx_cyc_local_end` (L55) — Ends a local cycle accumulator; in this build variant it does nothing.
- `psx_cyc_bb_defer_cleanup` (L90) — Cleanup hook for a deferred-cycle guard: ends the deferral when the guard goes out of scope.
- `psx_cyc_local_cleanup` (L94) — Cleanup hook for a local cycle guard: ends the local accumulator when the guard goes out of scope.
- `__attribute__` (L104) — Marks psx_cyc_charge_full as noinline, so the full charge path stays a separate call.
- `psx_cyc_charge_full` (L106) — Adds cycles on the full path: an overlay build forwards them to the host, otherwise they go through guest cycle scaling or the batch.
- `psx_cyc_charge` (L224) — psx_cyc_charge_full's common case, the same steps: no guest cycle scale, replay, conservative stepping, device service or local sink, and the sum joins the batch (deferred block, or a running batch st
- `psx_cyc_base` (L241) — §1 base (Beetle cpu.cpp:795-798).
- `psx_cyc_deps` (L250) — GPR_DEPRES (Beetle cpu.cpp:702-705): zero ReadAbsorb[n] for every source/dest GPR of this instruction, preserving ReadAbsorb[0] (skipping bit 0 == Beetle's save/restore of ReadAbsorb[0]).
- `psx_cyc_lds` (L277) — DO_LDS timing-commit (Beetle cpu.cpp:800).
- `psx_cyc_step` (L289) — Full per-instruction interlock for a NON-CPU-load instruction (ALU, shift, branch, jump, store, COP control, LWC2/SWC2 pre-step, mult/div, mfhi/mflo, ...).
- `psx_cyc_base_take` (L310) — Returns 1 when the instruction takes a base cycle, or 0 when the pending read-absorb count takes it instead, decrementing that count.
- `psx_cyc_steps2` (L315) — Charges the cycle cost of two consecutive non-load instructions, applying each one's dependency masks and load-delay state in order.
- `psx_cyc_steps3` (L320) — Charges the cycle cost of three consecutive non-load instructions, applying each one's dependency masks and load-delay state in order.
- `psx_cyc_steps4` (L326) — Charges the cycle cost of four consecutive non-load instructions, applying each one's dependency masks and load-delay state in order.
- `psx_cyc_region_wait` (L355) — Beetle MemRW device-region READ wait (libretro.cpp:859-1131), the device- dependent part of a load's access cost (added before the +completion).
- `psx_cyc_scratch_off` (L387) — Returns 1 and sets off when an access of width bytes lies inside the scratchpad, or 0 otherwise.
- `psx_cyc_scratch_timing` (L393) — Applies load-delay timing for a scratchpad load into register rt, when load-delay modelling is enabled.
- `psx_cyc_load_word` (L422) — CPU data load value+timing.
- `psx_cyc_load_half` (L461) — Reads a 16-bit value and applies the load-delay timing for register rt; returns the loaded half-word.
- `psx_blk_access_cost` (L518) — [recompiler] cpu_timing = "block" (docs/PERFORMANCE_MODES.md).
- `psx_blk_lwc2_read` (L544) — Reads a word for a GTE LWC2 load, charging its block access cost and flushing overlay cycles before the read.
- `psx_cyc_load_byte_fast` (L603) — Reads a byte with load timing by forwarding to psx_cyc_load_byte in this build variant.
- `psx_store_word` (L607) — Writes a 32-bit word to guest memory through the CPU's write hook.
- `psx_store_half` (L608) — Writes a 16-bit half-word to guest memory through the CPU's write hook.
- `psx_store_byte` (L609) — Writes one byte to guest memory through the CPU's write hook.
- `psx_cyc_lwc2_read` (L662) — Main RAM and scratchpad inline (psx_cyc_readmem's sequence with completion +1 and no arm; no PSX_LOAD_DELAY gate, as in the slow path); devices, BIOS and the recording modes take the slow path.

### runtime/include/psx_cycles.h

Guest CPU cycle clock and its optional timing scale: the single source of guest-visible time that peripherals schedule from.

- `psx_gcs_recip_for` (L129) — Returns the Q16 reciprocal of a cycle scale factor, capped at 64; 65536 means no scaling.
- `psx_gcs_session_profile` (L139) — Fixed session timing profile.
- `psx_gcs_scale` (L143) — Scales a CPU cycle count by the session's reciprocal, carrying the fractional remainder to the next call.
- `psx_cpu_cycles` (L155) — CPU cycles -> guest cycles.
- `psx_advance_cycles` (L173) — The common production path is inlined: bump the counter and only service devices when the next event deadline is due.
- `psx_cpu_charge` (L225) — Charges CPU cycles, scaling them first when cycle scaling is active, and skips the advance when the scaled count is zero.
- `psx_cyc_local_publish` (L238) — Publishes function-local cycle charges into the normal batch; in this build variant it does nothing.
- `psx_cyc_batch_flush` (L239) — Publishes the batched cycle charges now, through the overlay's pending-cycle flush.
- `psx_cyc_batch_flush_quiet` (L272) — [recompiler] gpr_locals (docs/GPR_LOCALS.md): psx_cyc_batch_flush when it needs no out-of-line call (no local sink to publish; the batch's advance reaches neither the slow path nor device service).

### runtime/include/psx_edge.h

Inline block-edge interrupt check for compiled code: handles the common case at each basic-block edge and defers other cases to the full check.

- `psx_edge_idle_site` (L76) — Returns 1 when the PC is one of the idle-loop edge sites recorded by the idle detector.
- `psx_edge_irq_fast` (L88) — The edge publishes the batched cycles first, in every case (it takes over the emitters' psx_cyc_bb_defer_flush, below).
- `__attribute__` (L132) — Marks psx_check_interrupts_at_inline as flatten, so the edge check is inlined into its caller.
- `psx_check_interrupts_at_inline` (L134) — Publishes pending cycles, then runs the block-edge interrupt check inline and calls the full check only when it is needed.
- `psx_cyc_charge_edge` (L158) — Adds cycles to the edge batch with a fast add when no gate is set and the sum does not overflow; otherwise calls the slow path.
- `psx_blk_lwc2_read_edge` (L207) — Reads a word for a GTE LWC2 load at a block edge, charging its cost inline for main RAM and scratchpad accesses.

### runtime/include/psx_gpr_locals.h

Inline forms of the register-local helpers that generated code uses when gpr_locals is on, so common cases avoid out-of-line calls.

- `psx_cyc_charge_quiet` (L53) — psx_cyc_charge_edge's common case (psx_edge.h): 1 added to the batch, 0 nothing.
- `psx_edge_quiet` (L63) — psx_check_interrupts_at_inline with nothing called out of line.
- `__attribute__` (L90) — Common-case GTE LWC2 read: returns 1 with the word in out when it can finish inline without an out-of-line call, otherwise 0.

### runtime/include/render_pass_sprite_scene.hpp

- `activate` (L212) — Resets the capture state and registers a frame-interpolation render pass at the flip-pending point.

### runtime/src/audio_music.c

Music at its own tempo under fast-forward: a second copy of the guest SPU plays the music voices while sound effects stay on the guest timeline.

- `am_set_classifier` (L51) — The title's voices of the music right now (bit v = voice v), read at each key-on; NULL = mode 2 unavailable (mode 1 is used).
- `am_ready` (L52) — Returns 1 when a voice classifier is installed, so the music SPU mode is available.
- `am_active` (L53) — Running (the fast-forward, trailing after it, or the crossfade out).
- `am_music_changed` (L54) — The title's song changed: the music SPU catches up (fade out, in).
- `sat16` (L56) — Clamps a 32-bit value to the signed 16-bit range.
- `silence` (L61) — Voices 'mask' out of a clone: keyed off (their release tails fade out; their other registers stay: a driver that writes a register only when its own copy changes, as BoF4's, would never give a zeroed
- `snapshot_live` (L67) — The guest SPU as it is now, into a buffer.
- `copy_ram` (L82) — A clone's sample RAM from the guest's (the snapshot has the registers and voices only: a savestate keeps SPU RAM apart).
- `music_from_live` (L85) — The music SPU from the guest's present, without the effects' voices.
- `q_push` (L97) — Queues a guest SPU access with its cycle, kind, address and value; sets an overflow flag when the queue is full.
- `tap` (L110) — Every guest access to the SPU while running: the effects SPU now, the music SPU later; a key-on goes to one or the other by its voices' owner.
- `enter` (L139) — Starts the music SPU from a snapshot of the guest SPU and its sample RAM; returns 0 when the snapshot cannot be read.
- `stop` (L163) — Detaches the SPU access tap and clears the running state and the event queue.
- `am_reset` (L169) — Stop at once (savestate load).
- `music_render` (L173) — The music SPU's next n frames at the wall clock's pace: the accesses held up to there applied at their own guest cycles, the frames between them made.
- `sfx_pull` (L223) — Catches the effects SPU up, pops its output frames into the buffer, and returns how many frames were read.
- `am_pump` (L231) — The pump's stream under mode 2: 'live' the guest SPU's frames just made; out gets what the host plays.
- `am_stats` (L279) — TCP audio_turbo: state (0 idle, 1 running, 2 crossfading out, 3 trailing), the music's delay behind the guest (ms of game time), events queued, catch-ups, entries.

### runtime/src/audio_turbo.c

Fast-forward time compressor: stretches or squeezes game audio at any speed using WSOLA grains so pitch stays intact.

- `win_init` (L44) — Builds the Hann window table once; later calls do nothing.
- `sx` (L51) — Reads one channel of an input frame as a float scaled to -1..1.
- `mono` (L52) — Sums the left and right input samples at a ring position into one mono value.
- `clamp16f` (L53) — Converts a -1..1 float to a saturated 16-bit sample, rounded to nearest.
- `at_reset` (L60) — Forget all input and state (savestate load, device change).
- `at_jump_direct` (L70) — Out of compressing at once: drop the input held (its delay) and go on with the newest, the last grain's falling half faded under it (~12 ms).
- `at_push` (L78) — Stereo frames the SPU made, in order.
- `corr` (L92) — Normalized correlation of the candidate at p with the continuation at nat.
- `best_pos` (L102) — Finds the input position between lo and hi whose waveform best correlates with the natural continuation, coarse search then a fine one.
- `take_fin` (L118) — Copies held finished frames into out, up to room, and returns how many were copied.
- `measure` (L127) — Updates the speed ratio from the input and output frames counted over a measuring window, smoothed and clamped to 0.5..64.
- `at_pull` (L137) — Up to 'want' frames into out (compress 1), or every frame held (compress 0, 'want' ignored past out_cap).
- `at_backlog` (L217) — Frames held, not yet played (latency the compressor adds).
- `at_stats` (L221) — Observability (TCP audio_turbo): grains made, ratio measured, frames skipped by an overflow jump, the mode (0 direct, 1 compressing).

### runtime/src/bios_hle.c

Opt-in high-level emulation of PSX BIOS kernel calls, with fallback to the recompiled BIOS and an always-on call ring.

- `hle_record` (L95) — Appends one HLE call to the observability ring, tagged with the current guest thread and the call's result.
- `psx_hle_ring_seq` (L148) — Snapshot accessors: seq is the total number of records ever written; entry i (seq-CAP ..
- `psx_hle_ring_entry` (L150) — Returns the ring entry for a sequence index, or NULL if it was not written yet or has been overwritten.
- `ev_free_slot` (L160) — get_free_EvCB_slot (kernel 0x1D00): first status==0 slot index, else -1.
- `hle_open_event` (L171) — OpenEvent (kernel 0x1D8C): claim a free EvCB, fill it, status=disabled, return 0xF1000000|slot; no free slot => 0xFFFFFFFF.
- `hle_close_event` (L189) — CloseEvent (kernel 0x1E1C): status=free, return 1.
- `hle_test_event` (L198) — TestEvent (kernel 0x1EC8): ready => re-arm to enabled and return 1, else 0.
- `hle_set_event_status` (L213) — EnableEvent (kernel 0x1F10) / DisableEvent (kernel 0x1F4C): a non-free event's status is set to enabled/disabled; return 1 either way.
- `hle_deliver_event` (L225) — DeliverEvent (kernel 0x1B44): for every ENABLED EvCB matching class+spec, mode MARK => status=READY; mode CALLBACK => call the handler exactly as the kernel's 'jalr v0' does (same $ra, args untouched)
- `hle_service_b0` (L267) — B0 vector service. Returns 1 iff serviced in HLE.
- `hle_boot_shell_skip` (L289) — Skips the BIOS shell once at boot by returning straight to the game-loading call site, while boot skip is on and the game has not started.
- `psx_bios_hle_boot_turbo_active` (L303) — True while the HLE boot-skip is driving the frontend unpaced: boot skip enabled and the game entry PC has not yet been dispatched.
- `bios_hle_dispatch` (L310) — Hook run at the BIOS entry vector: services B0 calls in HLE when enabled, and records each call.
- `psx_bios_hle_configure` (L332) — Select the BIOS backend.

### runtime/src/boot_state.c

Saves and loads full emulator snapshots, with sections for CPU, timers, RAM, VRAM and modules, in a versioned file format.

- `boot_state_mono_ms` (L35) — Monotonic millisecond clock used for save timing (QueryPerformanceCounter on Windows).
- `boot_state_ram_cookie` (L112) — Header compatibility cookie (h.reserved): enhancement-memory layout, live RAM geometry and the fixed execution implementation.
- `boot_state_layout_cookie` (L115) — Combines the memory layout, RAM size and execution cookies into one value that is checked on load.
- `boot_state_load_stats` (L140) — Copies the stored stats of the boot_state loads (timings, rejects, last reason) for TCP boot_state_stats.
- `boot_state_note_reject` (L144) — Counts a rejected boot_state load and keeps its reason and path, truncated.
- `boot_state_last_vram_dirty_rows` (L150) — §96 telemetry: after the latest save, how many VRAM scanlines were dirty and whether the incremental mirror path patched (vs full memcpy).
- `boot_state_last_vram_incremental` (L155) — Returns 1 when the last save patched only the dirty VRAM rows, rather than copying all of VRAM.
- `boot_state_vram_mirror_reset` (L160) — Drop the §96 VRAM mirror (RB shutdown / before re-enable).
- `sync_vram_mirror_for_save` (L170) — Build s_vram_mirror from live CPU VRAM using dirty rows when possible.
- `bs_write` (L245) — Writes bytes to the save output, either to the file or to the growing in-memory buffer; returns 1 on success.
- `write_header_le` (L264) — Writes the save file header in little-endian byte order.
- `write_section_raw` (L282) — Writes a section header (tag, flags, length) followed by the data, uncompressed.
- `write_section` (L297) — Prefer zlib for large blobs (smaller disk + faster load on slow storage).
- `write_module_section` (L321) — Writes a module's state as one section, using callbacks for its size and its bytes.
- `write_cpu_section` (L333) — Writes the general registers and the other CPU state as one section.
- `write_timer_section` (L364) — Writes the three timer counters, targets, modes and IRQ lines as one section.
- `write_vram_section_full` (L389) — Classic full VRAM section (offline / zlib / tracking off).
- `boot_state_save_to` (L420) — Writes a complete snapshot, header then sections, to an output stream.
- `boot_state_save` (L592) — Saves a snapshot to the file at path; returns 1 on success.
- `boot_state_save_buffer_ex` (L606) — Saves a snapshot into a newly allocated buffer, with zlib compression on or off.
- `boot_state_save_buffer` (L628) — Saves a snapshot into a newly allocated buffer, compressing large sections.
- `boot_state_save_buffer_raw` (L635) — Saves a snapshot into a newly allocated buffer with compression turned off.
- `apply_section` (L644) — Applies one saved section's data to the CPU, memory or devices, chosen by its tag.
- `timer_section_ok` (L873) — CPU-8: the timer section is fixed-size; its mode words must also be ones the timer block can hold (range check of the internal one-shot bit).
- `validate_section` (L886) — Checks that a section's length matches what this build expects for its tag.
- `boot_state_parse_header` (L923) — Reads and checks the file header; returns 0 for a bad or oversized file.
- `boot_state_append_reason` (L946) — Appends a part name to the reason text, separated by a comma, if it fits.
- `boot_state_check_buffer` (L960) — Checks whether a snapshot buffer can be loaded here, filling in a reason when it cannot.
- `boot_state_load_buffer` (L1037) — Loads a snapshot from a buffer into the CPU and machine state, after checking it.
- `boot_state_load` (L1193) — Loads a snapshot file from path into the CPU and machine state; returns 1 on success.
- `boot_state_set_capture` (L1232) — Sets the file path for an automatic snapshot taken when the game's entry point is first reached.
- `boot_state_trigger_capture` (L1240) — Called from fntrace when the game entry PC first dispatches.

### runtime/src/cosim.c

Co-simulation oracle engine: compares guest state at fixed instruction checkpoints and serves them over a small TCP server (PSX_COSIM builds only).

- `fold` (L67) — Mixes one 64-bit value into a running FNV-style hash, byte by byte.
- `cosim_block` (L75) — Block-leader hook (emitted under PSX_COSIM + called from the interp loop).
- `cosim_last_block` (L76) — Returns the PC of the most recent block leader.
- `cosim_cycles_to_next_checkpoint` (L78) — ---- engine (cosim.c) ---- void cosim_init(void); /* start the TCP oracle server (call once at startup) void cosim_block(uint32_t pc); /* block-leader pc stash (emitted + interp), reporting uint32_t c
- `cosim_record_checkpoint` (L92) — Instruction-count-keyed checkpoint — taken inside cosim_instr, which both backends call exactly once per retirement event (a branch and its delay slot retire as ONE event in both the dirty-RAM interp
- `cosim_tick` (L112) — Empty hook kept for the cycle-advance call sites; checkpoints happen in cosim_instr.
- `cosim_instr` (L117) — Counts one retired instruction and takes a checkpoint when the count reaches the next boundary, parking the guest for the coordinator.
- `send_line` (L148) — Sends one text line to a socket, retrying partial sends; returns 0 on failure.
- `server_loop` (L159) — Opens the listening TCP socket on the port and accepts clients, handling their commands one line at a time.
- `handle_line` (L195) — Runs one text command from the oracle client and sends back the reply.
- `server_thread` (L360) — Thread entry that runs the server loop on the given port.
- `cosim_init` (L367) — Call once at startup (from the clean-build main, before the guest runs).

### runtime/src/cosim_state.c

Computes the canonical hash of the guest's full architectural state for co-simulation comparisons (PSX_COSIM builds only).

- `fnv` (L23) — FNV-style hash over a byte buffer, continuing from a seed value.
- `fnv_u32` (L28) — Mixes a 32-bit value into a running hash.
- `fnv_u64` (L29) — Mixes a 64-bit value into a running hash.
- `cosim_state_reset` (L84) — Reset all incremental state (call once at machine init / after a full state load).
- `cosim_note_ram_write` (L92) — Incremental page-hash maintenance.
- `cosim_note_vram_write` (L98) — Marks VRAM as changed so the next state hash recomputes it.
- `cosim_inject_ram` (L101) — Gate-4 fault injection: after this is armed, the next cosim_state_hash perturbs one byte of RAM (addr) or one CPU GPR (reg 0..31, hi=32, lo=33) by XOR val, so the oracle MUST halt at exactly that fiel
- `cosim_inject_reg` (L102) — Arms a one-time fault injection that XORs one CPU register (index 0..33) at the next state hash.
- `blob_hash` (L104) — Hashes a variable-size state blob, using a size function and a writer, into a running hash.
- `hash_cpu` (L112) — Hashes the general registers and other CPU state into a running hash, leaving out the PC.
- `cosim_state_hash` (L154) — Compute the full canonical state hash of the LIVE machine (debug_cpu_ptr + globals).

- `crash_is_retaddr` (L259) — Windows: 1 when v inside the exe's text section follows a call instruction, so it looks like a return address.

Memoizes pure game functions: records what a call reads and writes, then replays the saved result when the live inputs still match.

- `ds_recorder_reset` (L222) — Clears the read and write flags of every touched page so a new capture starts clean.

- `ds_build_ranges` (L249) — Build ranges from a flag map over the touched pages.

- `ds_verify` (L386) — Checks that every recorded read range still matches live memory; returns 1 only when all of them match.
- `ds_apply` (L400) — Replays a shard's recorded writes into guest memory through the normal write paths and marks executable ranges.
