### runtime/src/debug_socket_io.h

Portable socket helpers for the debug server (non-blocking mode, readiness waits, accept and line receive), with Windows and POSIX variants.

- `psx_debug_socket_nonblocking` (L26) — Switches a socket between blocking and non-blocking mode; returns 1 on success.
- `psx_debug_socket_retryable` (L37) — Returns 1 when the last socket error means the call should be retried, such as would-block or interrupted.
- `psx_debug_socket_readable` (L46) — Waits up to 200 ms for a socket to become readable; returns 1 when ready, 0 on timeout and -1 on error.
- `psx_debug_socket_accept` (L62) — Accepts a client on a listening socket while the server is running, waiting in short slices; returns the client or the invalid socket.
- `psx_debug_socket_recv_line` (L86) — Reads bytes from a client until a newline arrives or the buffer is full, waiting while the server runs; returns the line length or -1.

### runtime/src/debug_trace_ranges.c

Parses the text form of debug trace address ranges, such as a list of hex ranges, into an array of range records.

- `skip_space` (L8) — Advances a text pointer past any leading whitespace characters.
- `parse_u32` (L16) — Parses an unsigned 32-bit number at the cursor, skipping leading spaces and advancing the cursor; returns 0 when the text is not a number.
- `psx_debug_parse_trace_ranges` (L37) — Parses a text list of address ranges into the given array, up to its capacity, and returns how many were read.

### runtime/src/device_trace.c

Keeps a large ring of device interrupt events (cycle, frame and source) for debugging, compiled identically into both host builds.

- `device_trace_arm` (L21) — Turns device-event tracing on or off.
- `device_trace_reset` (L22) — Clears the device event ring and its sequence counter.
- `device_trace_is_armed` (L23) — Returns 1 when device-event tracing is armed, otherwise 0.
- `device_trace_total` (L24) — Returns the total number of device events recorded since the last reset.
- `device_source_str` (L26) — Maps a device interrupt source code to its name, such as vblank, gpu, cdrom, dma or timer0.
- `device_trace_note` (L44) — Record one device-IRQ raise edge.
- `device_trace_get` (L56) — Readback: copies up to max_rows NEWEST events, oldest-first, into out[].

### runtime/src/dirty_ram_interp.c

Small MIPS interpreter that runs code written into RAM after boot, one basic block at a time, with debug and trace hooks.

- `interp_cyc_step` (L99) — Charges one cycle for an interpreted instruction, unless a pending load result is still absorbing it or a replay is active.
- `interp_exception` (L131) — ===== Minimal exception delivery from the interpreter path ===== Sets COP0 registers (BadVAddr, Cause, EPC, Status) and redirects PC to the hardware exception vector.
- `cosim_exec_one_begin` (L149) — Clears the co-simulation hook flag before an instruction runs; does nothing unless co-simulation is built.
- `cosim_exec_one_did_hook` (L150) — Returns 1 if the co-simulation hook ran during the current instruction, otherwise 0.
- `cosim_exec_one_transfer_hook` (L151) — Runs the co-simulation check for the instruction at the given PC and marks that it ran.
- `pc_table_get_or_insert_in` (L250) — Linear-probed insert/lookup keyed on entry PC.
- `pc_table_get_or_insert` (L261) — Returns the entry for a PC in the global PC table, inserting it if it is not there yet.
- `exec_pc_table_record` (L269) — Record every PC the interpreter executes (not just block entries) so overlay_capture can report execution-verified seeds for the region.
- `dirty_ram_interp_is_active` (L294) — Returns 1 while the interpreter is active for the current dispatch, otherwise 0.
- `psx_exec_phase` (L311) — Returns the current execution phase code, used by the wall-time sampler.
- `dirty_ram_ld_delay_flush` (L349) — Retire a deferred load writeback.
- `dirty_ram_ld_delay_discard` (L357) — Drop a deferred load-delay writeback WITHOUT applying it.
- `dirty_ram_ld_delay_save` (L364) — Copies the pending delayed load (register, value, age, armed flag) into the given structure so it can be restored later.
- `dirty_ram_ld_delay_restore` (L372) — Restores a pending delayed load from a structure saved earlier.
- `dirty_ram_irq_ambient_resync_after_restore` (L380) — Re-anchor host-only dirty IRQ pump ambient (entry-poll stride + 4096-insn gap) after snap restore.
- `callret_armed` (L442) — Returns 1 when the call-resolution watch range is set, otherwise 0.
- `callret_begin` (L468) — Records the start of a call in the call-resolution ring when its PC is in the watched range; returns the entry index or an invalid marker.
- `callret_end` (L486) — Completes the call-resolution record at the given index with its path code and the CPU state after the call.
- `interp_refused_game_text` (L528) — Game text that dispatch refuses because its live bytes differ from the boot EXE.
- `span_forced` (L544) — Returns 1 when a physical address lies inside the forced span range.
- `op_field` (L553) — MIPS instruction field decoders.
- `rs_field` (L554) — Returns the rs register field (bits 21 to 25) of a MIPS instruction word.
- `rt_field` (L555) — Returns the rt register field (bits 16 to 20) of a MIPS instruction word.
- `rd_field` (L556) — Returns the rd register field (bits 11 to 15) of a MIPS instruction word.
- `shamt_field` (L557) — Returns the shift amount field (bits 6 to 10) of a MIPS instruction word.
- `funct_field` (L558) — Returns the 6-bit function field (bits 0 to 5) of a MIPS instruction word.
- `imm16_field` (L559) — Returns the unsigned 16-bit immediate field of a MIPS instruction word.

- `sxy_fold_word` (L581) — Word reader for the [[widescreen.cull.sxy]] whole-fold check: the fold words around an interpreted PC are in main RAM like the PC itself.
- `ws_cull_site` (L601) — Classifies a PC as a widescreen cull site, using a small cache keyed on the PC and its instruction word.
- `ws_cull_bltz_site` (L632) — Widescreen LEFT-edge funnel-bltz classification (auto_screen_x, signed min/max + center±halfwidth idioms — ws_cull_detect.h).
- `ws_branch_keep` (L659) — Explicit [widescreen.cull] branch_keep_sites: the reject branch is forced not-taken only while a widened view is configured, exactly like the native emit (code_generator.cpp keep_branch_if_wide).
- `ws_clip_edge_load` (L667) — Explicit [widescreen.cull] clip_edge_x_load_sites (lh/lhu/lw): the loaded screen-X clip bound moves out by the live margin when it equals a screen edge (gpu.c psx_ws_clip_edge_x).
- `ws_backdrop_site_kind` (L680) — Widescreen far-backdrop column-PRELOAD site classification for the interpreter ([widescreen.cull] auto_backdrop).
- `dirty_ram_log_instruction` (L710) — Records one interpreted instruction in the instruction log when its PC is in the recorded range, and freezes the log when the watched target is reached.
- `dirty_ram_log_marker` (L776) — Marker entries delimit NATIVE candidate executions in the insn ring (native code emits no per-insn entries; markers keep the two runs' timelines alignable).
- `lwl_merge` (L791) — LWL/LWR are merge-only here; the timed aligned-word read is done by the caller via psx_cyc_load_word (Beetle reads the aligned word; GPR_DEP rs only, arms LDWhich=rt).
- `lwr_merge` (L800) — Merges the aligned memory word with the register value for an LWR (load word right) at the given byte offset.
- `interp_swl` (L809) — Interprets SWL (store word left): writes the upper bytes of a value into the aligned word in memory.
- `interp_swr` (L821) — Interprets SWR (store word right): writes the lower bytes of a value into the aligned word in memory.
- `abort_unsupported` (L853) — Records an unsupported instruction (its PC, word and reason) as an abort and returns 1 so the caller stops.
- `phys_is_overlay_flow_region` (L878) — A dirty page that should run as a locally-chained overlay: anything ABOVE the kernel window.
- `is_local_dirty_target` (L882) — Returns 1 when a jump target lies in an overlay flow region and its RAM page is dirty, so it should be interpreted locally.
- `dirty_ram_word_looks_decodable` (L900) — A dirty-RAM target only deserves interpretation if its first word decodes as a plausible MIPS instruction.
- `dirty_ram_same_pc` (L943) — Returns 1 when two PCs refer to the same physical address, ignoring the segment bits.
- `dirty_ram_pump_boundary` (L947) — Runs the interrupt check at a block boundary and records the safe resume PC; returns 1 when control was transferred.
- `dirty_ram_finish_call_return` (L973) — Finishes a call by moving the PC to the return address and running the boundary check; returns 1 if control was transferred, else sets the next PC.
- `dispatch_nonlocal_call` (L985) — Sends a call to a target outside the interpreted block through the compiled dispatcher and returns the next PC through an output parameter.
- `psx_mixed_owner_enabled` (L1027) — ── Mixed interp<->compiled dispatch owner (host-stack recursion fix) ────── The dirty interpreter nests psx_dispatch_game_compiled when an interpreted block transfers into compiled code.
- `interp_host_stack_used` (L1035) — #include <intrin.h> /* __readgsqword — fiber TEB StackBase
- `psx_mixed_stack_watermark` (L1045) — Returns the host stack limit in bytes at which nesting of compiled calls stops, from PSX_MIXED_STACK_KB (default 700 KB, minimum 64 KB).
- `xprobe_env_init` (L1125) — Reads the flight-recorder limits from environment variables, once.
- `dirty_ram_xprobe_arm` (L1132) — Sets the flight-recorder trip limits (frame, stack KB, warmup) and re-arms the trip.
- `xprobe_flush_frame` (L1137) — Stores the current frame's flight-recorder summary (crossings, depth, stack, cycles) into the summary ring.

- `g_xprobe_watch` (L1189) — Env seeding is lazy so it works no matter which subsystem touches the ring first, and costs one branch after the first call.
- `dirty_ram_xprobe_watch_set` (L1205) — Control plane for the 'xprobe_watch' TCP command.
- `dirty_ram_xprobe_watch_get` (L1211) — Returns the watched address at an index through phys_out; returns 1 when the index is valid, otherwise 0.

- `dirty_ram_xprobe_call_note` (L1225) — Watched-target call note for NON-interp call sites (overlay shard call-outs via dispatch_call).
- `xprobe_event` (L1230) — Records one control-flow crossing in the flight recorder, flushing the previous frame's summary when the frame changes.
- `dirty_ram_xprobe_json` (L1270) — Emit the flight-recorder rings as JSON (called by crash_trace).
- `interp_enter_compiled` (L1366) — Hands a jump target to compiled code when its game text is native-ok and the host stack is not too deep; returns 0 so the interpreter runs it instead.
- `exec_one` (L1396) — Fetches the instruction at a PC and executes it, returning the next PC through an output parameter.
- `exec_delay_slot` (L1401) — Forward: helper for delay-slot execution on jumps/branches.
- `exec_one_fetched` (L1436) — Executes one already-fetched instruction, first retiring any pending delayed load writeback.
- `exec_one_fetched_inner` (L1537) — Decodes and executes one fetched MIPS instruction, updating registers, memory and the next PC.
- `dirty_ram_dispatch` (L2507) — Public entry point. Caller (psx_dispatch) has translated 'addr' to a KSEG-stripped form already in some cases, so accept any address and mask.
- `dirty_ram_span_get` (L2621) — The open span (0,0 = none), for landings that longjmp past its exit.
- `dirty_ram_span_set` (L2626) — Sets the physical address range that the span-forced check tests against.
- `dirty_ram_span_last_failure` (L2633) — Copies the reason and details of the last failed span run into the given structure.
- `dirty_ram_run_span` (L2637) — Runs guest code from a start PC to a stop PC through the interpreter, up to a maximum instruction count; returns 1 on success and records a failure otherwise.
- `precise_irq_deliverable` (L2694) — Is a hardware interrupt deliverable to the guest at this exact instruction boundary?
- `precise_pc_dispatchable` (L2720) — Is 'pc' a point the TOP-LEVEL dispatcher can re-enter?
- `psx_run_precise` (L2740) — Run the guest per-instruction from cpu->pc through the interpreter, taking any deliverable interrupt at the EXACT instruction boundary, until a safe resume point.
- `psx_precise_slice_init_from_env` (L2901) — Reads PSX_PRECISE_SLICE from the environment to turn precise per-instruction slicing on or off.
- `psx_slice_block_impl` (L2912) — Block-leader slice guard impl.
- `dirty_ram_dispatch_inner` (L2949) — Dispatches a PC in dirty RAM: classifies its page and interprets the basic block there.
- `ls_set_window` (L3729) — Arm the comparator over a guest-frame window [lo,hi].
- `ls_set_record_only` (L3730) — Diagnostic: record blocks but skip the inline replay (to test whether the inline replay, not recording, is what perturbs the run).
- `ls_func_set_window` (L3731) — Arms the dispatch-segment lockstep comparator over a frame window.
- `ls_func_set_record_only` (L3732) — Turns record-only mode on or off for the dispatch-segment lockstep comparator.
- `ls_note_exception_entry` (L3734) — Called at real IRQ exception entry.
- `ls_shadow_record_begin` (L3739) — Side-effect-free whole-call trace used by the overlay differential gate.
- `ls_shadow_record_end` (L3756) — Ends a shadow recording: returns 1 when it can be replayed, and reports the operation count and whether an exception was seen.
- `ls_shadow_record_unreplayable` (L3765) — A recorded effect the replay cannot reproduce fails the record closed (the comparison is skipped, as for a device touch).
- `ls_shadow_replay_begin` (L3769) — Starts replaying a recorded shadow trace; returns 0 when another owner or a replay is already active.
- `ls_shadow_replay_end` (L3784) — Ends a shadow replay and reports whether it completed, plus any mismatch details; returns 0 when this is not the replay owner.
- `ls_shadow_abort` (L3803) — Cancels any shadow record or replay and restores the normal memory-operation mode.
- `ls_suppress_begin` (L3811) — Suppress lockstep memory recording while runtime/debug observers read guest RAM for diagnostics.
- `ls_suppress_end` (L3815) — Ends one suppression of lockstep memory recording.
- `ls_read_hook` (L3819) — Memory chokepoint hooks, called from the psx_read_ and psx_write_ funcs.
- `ls_write_hook` (L3840) — Memory write hook for lockstep: during replay it checks the write against the trace, otherwise it records the write.
- `ls_latch` (L3864) — Stores the first divergence found by the lockstep comparator; later divergences are ignored.
- `ls_replay_and_compare` (L3874) — Re-interpret the just-recorded block from the entry snapshot, comparing the interp result to native (cpu == post-block native state).
- `ls_same_phys` (L3934) — Returns 1 when two addresses are the same physical address, ignoring the segment bits.
- `lsf_copy_div_trace` (L3938) — Copies up to 48 trace entries around a divergence into the dispatch-segment comparator record.
- `lsf_latch` (L3946) — Stores the first divergence of the dispatch-segment comparator with its kind, frame, entry and details; later ones are ignored.
- `lsf_compare_regs` (L3965) — Compares the replayed and native CPU states (PC and general registers) and records the first mismatch.
- `lsf_replay_and_compare` (L3987) — Replays one dispatch segment through the interpreter from its entry and compares the result with the native state.
- `ls_func_enter` (L4076) — Dispatch-segment comparator: wraps one clean psx_dispatch_game_compiled() invocation and replays the same callable through exec_one until it reaches the same returned cpu->pc.
- `ls_func_exit` (L4102) — Ends a dispatch-segment comparison at the segment exit, comparing the result or skipping it on a conflict.

- `ls_at_leader` (L4141) — Per-basic-block-leader entry, called from debug_server_cyc_observe.
- `ls_get_diverge_json` (L4189) — Drain the first-divergence record as JSON into buf.
- `ls_get_func_json` (L4210) — Writes the dispatch-segment divergence record as JSON into a buffer and returns its length.

### runtime/src/disasm_shim.cpp

Thin shim that turns PS1 MIPS R3000 instruction words into readable text for disassembly and debug output.

- `gte_cmd_name` (L26) — Name of the GTE (geometry engine) command in the low six bits of a COP2 instruction word, for disassembly.
- `psx_disasm_one` (L54) — Format one MIPS R3000 instruction as text into out (NUL-terminated).

### runtime/src/disc_identity.cpp

Identifies a PS1 disc image: reads its serial, region, header, CRC32 and SHA-256, and checks it against any expected values or netplay policy.

- `uppercase_ascii` (L28) — Returns a copy of the string with ASCII letters converted to upper case.
- `read_at` (L33) — Seeks to an offset in the file and reads len bytes into out; true only when the whole read succeeded.
- `is_iso_pvd` (L41) — True when a 2048-byte sector is an ISO 9660 primary volume descriptor (type 1 with the CD001 magic).
- `region_from_serial` (L46) — "SCUS-94236" -> region.
- `normalize_serial` (L58) — Normalize a scanned EXE-style id "SCUS_942.36" to the game-id form "SCUS-94236".
- `scan_boot_serial` (L74) — Scan the SYSTEM.CNF text region for the BOOT serial.
- `crc32_stream` (L104) — CRC32 of the whole file, read from the start, returned as a 32-bit value; false if the read fails.
- `hex_sha256` (L118) — SHA-256 of the canonical identity string, returned as hex text.
- `fill_toc_from_mount` (L129) — Copies the cue and mount details of the resolved disc path into the identity's table-of-contents fields.
- `is_chd_path` (L170) — True when the path has a .chd extension, ignoring case.
- `crc32_chd` (L176) — CRC32 over every raw 2352-byte sector of the disc; false if any sector cannot be read.
- `apply_netplay_disc_expect` (L190) — Apply / re-apply netplay mount policy onto an already-identified disc.
- `identify_disc` (L236) — Identifies a disc from a path: resolves the data track, reads serial, region and header, optionally CRC32, and checks expected serial, CRC and netplay policy.

### runtime/src/disc_path.cpp

Resolves a user-picked disc file (cue, CHD or raw image such as bin/img/iso) to the image and cue that actually hold the data.

- `is_cue` (L21) — True when the path has a .cue extension, ignoring case.
- `is_chd` (L22) — True when the path has a .chd extension, ignoring case.
- `is_raw_image` (L24) — True when the path ends in one of the raw image extensions (.bin, .img, .iso, .car).
- `same_file_path` (L31) — True when both paths name the same file: by filesystem identity when both exist, else by normalised text.
- `absolute_or_self` (L41) — The absolute form of the path, or the path unchanged when it cannot be made absolute.
- `first_existing_binary` (L50) — The BINARY payload an unusable cue still points at: the data track when it is present, else the first existing BINARY FILE entry.
- `find_sibling_image` (L61) — <stem>.bin / .img / .iso / .car next to a cue we could not use.
- `find_owning_cue` (L87) — The cue that owns 'image': try <stem>.cue first (the common single-bin layout), then any cue in the same directory whose FILE list names it (the redump multi-track layout, where the cue is "Game.cue"
- `resolve_disc_path` (L118) — Never fails: an unrecognizable or missing path resolves to itself, so the caller's existing "could not open the disc" reporting still fires.

### runtime/src/dma.c

Emulates the PS1 DMA controller: its seven channels, transfer timing, interrupt flags, and the GPU, MDEC, CD-ROM, SPU and OTC transfers.

- `cd_dma_log_push` (L105) — Appends one CD-ROM DMA transfer (LBA, destination, size) to the ring log, overwriting the oldest entry once full.
- `cd_dma_log_get_total` (L113) — Total number of CD-ROM DMA transfers logged since start.
- `cd_dma_log_get_entry` (L114) — Reads logged CD-ROM DMA transfer idx into lba, dest and size; lba is -1 when that entry is no longer kept or not yet logged.
- `trace_dma` (L189) — Records one DMA event (kind, channel, word count, DMA and IRQ registers before and after) in the DMA trace ring.
- `trace_dma_reg_write` (L212) — Records a CPU write to a DMA register (address, value, mask) in the DMA trace ring, with the IRQ state before it.
- `gpu_ot_record_walk_stats` (L236) — Stores node count, word count and cycle count of the last GPU ordering-table walk and updates the maxima.
- `update_master_irq` (L250) — No-op: the DICR master IRQ flag is computed on read, not stored.
- `dicr_master_flag` (L261) — Returns bit 31 of a DICR value: set when bit 15 is set, or bit 23 is set together with any channel flag.
- `dicr_read_value` (L266) — The DICR value as the CPU reads it: the stored bits with the computed master flag in bit 31.
- `raise_dma_irq_on_master_edge` (L270) — Raises IRQ3 when the DICR master flag went from 0 (before) to 1 (now), passing the per-channel flags as detail.
- `start_cdrom_dma_capture` (L279) — Starts a CD-ROM DMA history entry for a transfer, snapshotting the CD-ROM and DMA registers at the start.
- `record_cdrom_dma_word` (L308) — Adds one moved word to the active CD-ROM DMA history entry, keeping its first and last words and a count.
- `finish_cdrom_dma_capture` (L325) — Closes the active CD-ROM DMA history entry with its final address and end state, and stores it in the history ring.
- `channel_enabled` (L354) — True when the DPCR enable bit of the given DMA channel is set.
- `channel_irq_flag_armed` (L360) — True when both the channel's DICR interrupt bit and the master DMA interrupt bit are set.
- `transfer_word_count` (L369) — Number of words a channel transfer moves, from its BCR block size and count; CD-ROM uses the sector size when the block size is 0.
- `validate_transfer_length` (L398) — Halts the emulator with a fatal error when the channel's transfer length exceeds the sanity limit (0x80000 words).
- `complete_transfer` (L413) — Completes a channel transfer: clears its busy and start bits, latches the DICR flag if armed, and logs the completion.
- `cancel_async_transfer` (L428) — Stops any in-flight asynchronous transfer on the channel (MDEC, CD-ROM or GPU linked list) and resets its counters.
- `schedule_delayed_complete` (L467) — Completes the transfer at once in render passes or when it is empty; otherwise queues completion after total words times cycles per word.
- `advance_delayed_complete` (L485) — Counts a queued channel completion down by the given cycles and completes the transfer when it reaches zero.
- `start_async_mdec_transfer` (L499) — Starts an asynchronous MDEC transfer on channel 0 (in) or 1 (out) when none is active, sized from its BCR.
- `finish_async_mdec_transfer` (L517) — Finishes an MDEC transfer: logs its end, cancels the async state and completes the channel.
- `start_async_cdrom_transfer` (L527) — Starts the asynchronous CD-ROM (channel 3) transfer, or completes it at once when it has no words.
- `dma_host_cdrom_write` (L546) — RAM-side effects of a completed CD-ROM (ch3) transfer of host-supplied sector data, for seamless-loading adapters serving a game's own CdGetSector or read loop: overlay capture before the first word,
- `finish_async_cdrom_transfer` (L579) — Finishes a CD-ROM transfer: closes its capture and, for game data (not FMV buffers), logs it and captures the overlay bytes.
- `psx_dma_set_mdec_batch` (L617) — Sets the MDEC DMA batch size (words per step) from configuration.
- `mdec_out_batch` (L618) — The MDEC DMA batch size: PSX_MDEC_DMA_BATCH from the environment, else the configured value, clamped to 1..256.
- `advance_mdec_channel` (L628) — Advances an MDEC DMA channel by the given cycles, moving its words in steps and completing it when all are moved.
- `execute_ch0_mdec_in` (L722) — Runs the whole channel 0 transfer (RAM to MDEC) at once, moving each word and completing the channel.
- `execute_ch1_mdec_out` (L756) — Runs the whole channel 1 transfer (MDEC to RAM) at once, moving each word and completing the channel.
- `gpu_ll_resolve_address` (L777) — Linked-list callback: maps a guest address to the host address the GPU DMA reads from, through the mod hook.
- `gpu_ll_read_word` (L782) — Linked-list callback: reads one guest RAM word.
- `gpu_ll_observe_header` (L787) — Linked-list callback: checks each linked-list node header for the widescreen validator.
- `gpu_ll_begin_node` (L793) — Linked-list callback: starts a node of num_words words, validates it and sets the GP0 node source; always returns 1.
- `gpu_ll_emit_word` (L801) — Linked-list callback: sends one word of the node to GP0 with its source address.
- `gpu_ll_complete` (L807) — Linked-list callback: counts a completed walk and records its statistics and timeline event.
- `start_async_gpu_linked_list` (L828) — Starts the asynchronous GPU linked-list walk on channel 2 unless one is already active (counted as dropped then).
- `hold_host_ticks` (L863) — Host monotonic clock tick count, used only for hold diagnostics.
- `hold_host_ticks_per_sec` (L872) — Ticks per second of the host clock behind hold_host_ticks.
- `ll_bulk_enabled` (L890) — While the CPU is held and no other DMA moves RAM, the list's words cannot change under the walk: its end is known in advance (dma_gpu_ll_cycles_to_ finish), and the hold advances there in one go.
- `hold_cpu_for_gpu_linked_list` (L899) — Holds the CPU while the GPU linked list walks, advancing guest cycles to the walk's end in one go when possible.
- `dma_debug_get_gpu_hold` (L953) — Debug accessor: copies the GPU-hold statistics and returns the hold ring.
- `execute_ch2_gpu` (L959) — Runs a channel 2 GPU transfer: block mode moves the words to or from the GPU, linked-list mode starts the list walk.
- `execute_ch3_cdrom` (L1027) — Runs a channel 3 CD-ROM transfer: copies sector data from the CD-ROM buffer into RAM, or completes it when it is to the device.
- `execute_ch4_spu` (L1043) — Returns the number of words moved so the caller can schedule a faithful delayed completion (DMA_SPU_CYCLES_PER_WORD).
- `execute_ch6_otc` (L1080) — Runs an OTC transfer: writes a backward-linked ordering table into RAM ending with the 0xFFFFFF marker.
- `execute_ch5_pio` (L1105) — Runs a PIO transfer: moves words directly to or from RAM and completes at once.
- `try_execute` (L1135) — Starts a transfer on the channel when its start bit is set and the channel is enabled in DPCR, dispatching by channel.
- `dma_get_dicr` (L1210) — The DICR register value as the CPU reads it.
- `dma_gpu_linked_list_active` (L1212) — A GPU linked-list walk is in flight (render passes refuse to start then).
- `dma_get_dpcr` (L1213) — The DPCR register value (DMA channel priority and enable).
- `dma_cdrom_transfer_active` (L1214) — Nonzero while the asynchronous CD-ROM transfer is active.
- `dma_cycles_to_irq` (L1227) — Cycle-budgeted precise event slicing: guest CPU cycles until DMA raises a DELIVERABLE IRQ (bit3 unmasked in i_mask).
- `dma_cycles_to_internal_event` (L1250) — Mask-blind scheduler boundary: next DMA word movement or delayed completion, not merely the final IRQ.
- `dma_cycles_to_deliverable_irq` (L1306) — Strict deliverability form for wait-loop elision: unlike the conservative scheduler bound, ignores channel completions whose DICR IRQ is disabled.
- `dma_advance` (L1333) — Advances all DMA activity by the given guest cycles: MDEC and linked-list walks, delayed completions and CD-ROM transfers.
- `dma_init` (L1410) — Resets all DMA channels and registers to their power-on state.
- `dma_read` (L1422) — Reads a DMA register at the given address (DPCR, DICR or a channel register) and returns its value.
- `dma_write_masked` (L1466) — Writes a DMA register under a bit mask, handling DPCR, DICR acknowledge bits and the channel control registers.
- `dma_write` (L1531) — Writes a full 32-bit DMA register value.
- `dma_debug_get_gpu_ot_stats` (L1535) — Debug accessor: copies the GPU ordering-table statistics into out.
- `dma_debug_get_trace` (L1542) — Debug accessor: returns the DMA trace ring and its entry count.
- `dma_debug_clear_trace` (L1547) — Clears the DMA trace ring.
- `dma_debug_get_cdrom_history` (L1552) — Debug accessor: returns the CD-ROM DMA history ring and its entry count.
- `dma_debug_clear_cdrom_history` (L1557) — Clears the CD-ROM DMA history ring.
- `dma_debug_get_state` (L1565) — Debug accessor: fills out with the DMA state (registers and channel status).
- `dma_w_async` (L1603) — Saves one asynchronous channel's state into a snapshot writer; returns 1 on success.
- `dma_r_async` (L1608) — Restores one asynchronous channel's state from a snapshot reader; returns 1 on success.
- `dma_w_gpu_ll` (L1613) — Saves the GPU linked-list state into a snapshot writer; returns 1 on success.
- `dma_r_gpu_ll` (L1623) — Restores the GPU linked-list state from a snapshot reader; returns 1 on success.
- `dma_w_delay` (L1635) — Saves a delayed-completion state into a snapshot writer; returns 1 on success.
- `dma_r_delay` (L1639) — Restores a delayed-completion state from a snapshot reader; returns 1 on success.
- `dma_snapshot_bytes` (L1644) — Byte size of the DMA snapshot section.
- `dma_snapshot_write` (L1646) — Writes the DMA state into the snapshot buffer p.
- `dma_snapshot_validate` (L1667) — Pass-1 check for boot_state's two-pass load: parses into locals and refuses an async start address outside live RAM or remaining words above the total.
- `dma_snapshot_read` (L1681) — Restores the DMA state from a snapshot buffer of len bytes; returns nonzero on success.

### runtime/src/dma_gpu_ll.c

Walks a GPU linked list (ordering table) in RAM node by node as an asynchronous DMA, charging guest cycles and sending each word to the GPU.

- `resolve_address` (L12) — Maps a guest address to the host address the list walk reads from, through the supplied ops callbacks.
- `finish` (L17) — Ends the list walk: marks it inactive and calls the completion callback.
- `dma_gpu_ll_start` (L26) — Starts a list walk at start_addr, limited to max_nodes nodes.
- `dma_gpu_ll_cancel` (L38) — Cancels a list walk by clearing its whole state.

### runtime/src/dynamic_resolution.c

Adaptive render-resolution controller: picks a resolution level from measured frame load and steps it down fast and up slowly, with a separate runtime variant.

- `dynres_default_params` (L6) — Fills a parameter block with the default window sizes, load factors and hold times.
- `clamp_level` (L36) — Clamps a level to the controller's floor and ceiling.
- `dynres_init` (L42) — Sets up a controller with its floor, ceiling, starting level and parameters.
- `dynres_predict` (L67) — Predicted load at level 'to' from 'load' measured at 'from'.
- `dynres_up_blocked_s` (L73) — Up steps into 'level' blocked for this many seconds from now_s (0 = not).
- `window_reset` (L79) — Clears the current measurement window.
- `discard` (L85) — Everything that needs consecutive clean windows starts over.
- `dynres_hold` (L96) — Hold sampling and decisions until now_s + tail_s (the latest hold wins).
- `dynres_note_step_cost` (L102) — The measured wall time of a step the host applied.
- `dynres_force` (L107) — Pin a level (debugging); 0 releases the pin.
- `learn` (L123) — Updates the learned cost of a level change from the load measured before and after it.
- `begin_post` (L132) — Starts the measurement window that judges a recent level change.
- `step_down` (L143) — Steps the level down toward the floor when load is too high; returns the new level or the same one if nothing changed.
- `step_up` (L169) — Steps the level up to a given level when load allows it; returns the new level or the same one.
- `close_window` (L186) — A window closed: judge a recent step, then the rules.
- `dynres_sample` (L273) — One guest interval ending at now_s.
- `dynrt_default_params` (L305) — Fills a runtime parameter block with the default values.
- `rt_clamp` (L336) — Clamps a level to the runtime controller's floor and ceiling.
- `dynrt_init` (L342) — Sets up the runtime controller with its floor, ceiling, starting level and parameters.
- `dynrt_arm_descent` (L365) — Arm fast descent (see RULES): a savestate load, game entry, a resize.
- `dynrt_descent_target` (L376) — Pure area (f = 1): the cost's fixed part only makes a level dearer than this predicts, so a jump never lands below the level that fits; a jump that lands too high is still over budget and jumps again
- `dynrt_predict` (L382) — Predicted load at level to, from the load measured at level from.
- `dynrt_up_blocked_s` (L388) — Seconds from now_s that up-steps into the given level stay blocked (0 when not blocked).
- `rt_window_reset` (L394) — Clears the current measurement window of the runtime controller.
- `rt_discard` (L400) — Drops the current measurement windows, counting them as held.
- `dynrt_hold` (L408) — Holds decisions and sampling until now_s plus tail_s.
- `dynrt_force` (L414) — Pins the runtime controller to a level, or releases the pin when the level is 0; returns 1 when accepted.
- `rt_step` (L428) — Applies one level step (up or down) with its reason, recording it for later judgement.
- `rt_learn` (L462) — Learns the cost of a runtime level change from the load before and after it.
- `rt_close_window` (L471) — Closes a measurement window at time now and applies the rules; returns the level chosen.
- `dynrt_sample` (L616) — One guest interval ending at now_s; returns the level to render at.

### runtime/src/event_ring.c

- `kind_name` (L62) — Returns the name of an event kind for printing.
- `mode_name` (L77) — Returns the name of an execution mode for printing.
- `format_entry` (L86) — Formats one event entry as a text line into out; returns the length written.
- `event_ring_dump_file` (L97) — Write the whole live window (oldest->newest) as a JSON array to 'path'.
- `event_ring_dump_json` (L116) — Emit a bounded JSON tail (most-recent 'max_entries', oldest->newest) into 'out'.

### runtime/src/frame_gen.c

Generated in-between frames: fits a camera between two game frames from their primitives and places intermediate views, with pacing, cost and breaker logic deciding how many to draw.

- `fg_prims_reset` (L9) — Empties a primitive list without freeing it.

- `src_cmp` (L143) — qsort comparison of two source records.

- `dist3` (L188) — Euclidean distance between two 3D points.
- `median_z` (L193) — Median depth (z) of a sorted list of source points.
- `fit_view` (L209) — Fits the camera motion of one view between the older and newer frames and its zoom (median ratio of older to newer projection distance); returns nonzero on success.
- `fg_cam_fit` (L335) — Fits the camera between two frames from their primitives into fit and per-vertex data; returns nonzero on success.
- `proj` (L464) — Projection of a camera-space point (0 when behind the near plane).
- `fg_cam_place` (L473) — Places the in-between view at phase t: writes screen positions x and y and edge margins for the primitives.
- `fg_plan` (L723) — Decides how many in-between frames to draw for a game frame, given costs, budget and the cap.
- `fg_step_s` (L742) — How many in-between frames to draw per game frame.
- `fg_slots` (L753) — fg_slots: display intervals a game frame 'flip_s' long fills on a 'refresh_hz' display as the clock (fg_clock_phase) schedules it: the in-between frames it shows plus the real one.
- `fg_slots_carry` (L764) — The display intervals this game frame gets: flip x refresh rounded down (within 0.015), the remainder carried in *carry (30 fps on 144 Hz: 4, 5, 5, 5, 5).
- `fg_image_slot` (L775) — The display interval (1..slots) image k (1..n+1, n+1 the real frame) is shown at, n in-between frames spread evenly over slots.

- `fg_next_due` (L785) — The next present time on the global grid after presenting at 'now'.
- `fg_clock_phase` (L792) — Phase (0..1) of the display clock at a time since the last real frame, for choosing the next frame slot.
- `fg_breaker_init` (L804) — Initialises a circuit breaker with its base hold, maximum hold and repeat window.
- `fg_breaker_trip` (L813) — Trips the breaker at time now (it stays open for its hold time); reason is recorded.
- `fg_breaker_open` (L827) — 1 while the breaker is open (generation must stay off) at time now.
- `fg_cost_init` (L829) — Initialises the frame cost estimator with the probe interval and its maximum.
- `fg_cost_cold` (L836) — Records how many cold-start measurements the cost estimator needs.
- `fg_cost_add` (L838) — One measured frame; 'fit_s' is what one generated frame may cost to fit.
- `fg_cost_estimate` (L862) — The estimate to plan with at 'now': 0 when unknown or due for a probe.
- `fg_pace_note` (L885) — Notes one pacing sample against the period and slack; returns nonzero when pacing is on track.
- `fg_ceiling_init` (L895) — Initialises a ceiling on generated frames per game frame, with its maximum and recovery time.
- `fg_ceiling_trip` (L901) — Lowers the ceiling after a trip with n planned frames at time now.

- `fg_hud_match` (L923) — HUD motion: 2D triangles (no GTE projection: gauges, needles) of the redrawn list L that the other frame O draws too (same key: op, texture, colour, UVs, in the same order among the 2D triangles) and
- `fg_hud_lerp` (L946) — Interpolates the HUD 2D triangles that the two frames share, at phase u, into x and y.

### runtime/src/frame_pacing.c

Frame pacer: sleeps until the next frame deadline and then advances the deadline by one period, using a short spin for sub-millisecond accuracy.

- `frame_pacing_sleep_ms` (L17) — Milliseconds to sleep until a deadline, given the current time; 0 when the deadline has passed.
- `frame_pacer_wait` (L49) — Block until the pacer's next deadline (sleep + final sub-ms spin), then advance the deadline by one period.

Decides when a freeze dump is written: classifies stalls, ranks wedge kinds and limits how many full dumps are authorised per run.

- `wedge_priority` (L5) — Ranks a wedge kind so the more important kind wins when several occur; higher is more important.
- `freeze_dump_policy_observe` (L15) — Feeds one observed wedge into the dump policy; returns nonzero when a full dump should be written now.

### runtime/src/freeze_heartbeat.c

Freeze watchdog: a heartbeat thread records progress and, on a hang, writes dumps of the guest stack, RAM, scratchpad and ring buffers.

- `freeze_heartbeat_set_paused` (L192) — Suppress automatic wedge classification while the host intentionally parks guest execution, such as save-state/rewind overlays or netplay admit waits.

- `heartbeat_write` (L810) — Writes one heartbeat record (frame, guest state and timing) to the heartbeat file.
- `heartbeat_thread` (L1179) — Thread body that writes a heartbeat at intervals, so a hung emulator can be seen from outside.
- `freeze_heartbeat_start` (L1188) — Spawn the heartbeat thread.

### runtime/src/golden_hash.c

Golden-run recorder: hashes GPU words, SPU samples and frame state into a per-frame ring so runs can be compared for divergence.

- `mix` (L26) — Mixes a value into a 64-bit running hash.
- `hash_bytes` (L28) — 64-bit hash of a byte buffer.
- `golden_gpu_word` (L36) — Adds one GPU word written on a port to the golden hash.
- `golden_spu_block` (L41) — Adds one block of stereo SPU samples to the golden hash.
- `golden_pgxp_note` (L46) — Adds a PGXP geometry note to the golden hash.
- `reset_frame_hashes` (L50) — Clears the per-frame hash values.
- `golden_arm` (L54) — Arms or disarms the recorder, and whether it arms on savestate load.
- `golden_note_savestate_loaded` (L66) — Savestate load completed: an armed-on-load recorder starts here.
- `golden_frame` (L72) — Frame boundary (debug_server_record_frame).
- `golden_total` (L98) — Total number of golden entries recorded.
- `golden_entries` (L100) — Copies the golden entries from a frame range into the ring output; returns the count.

### runtime/src/gpu.c

The PS1 GPU emulation: GP0 and GP1 command handling, software rasterising, VRAM and display output, plus the widescreen, shadow and native-wide presentation hooks.

- `ws_local_native_split` (L130) — 1 when the local viewport is split natively in a native-wide frame.
- `ws_ui_prepass_nodes_reset` (L190) — Clears the UI prepass node list before the next linked list.

- `gpu_ws_set_auto_ui_proportional` (L298) — [widescreen] auto_ui_size: 1 = proportional (the auto-UI HUD shrinks by sqrt((16:9) / aspect) beyond 16:9), 0 = original.

### runtime/src/gpu_edge.inc

Fixed-point helpers that give each triangle edge its starting X and per-line step for the GPU rasterizer.

- `gpu_edge_start` (L8) — Observed: every x gets the same fraction, 0xFFFFF800 (2^32 - 2^11), just under one column.
- `gpu_edge_step` (L14) — Observed: the size of dx/dy is rounded up, then the sign is put back, so the steps for dx and -dx are exact mirrors.

### runtime/src/gpu_hd_textures.cpp

Hosts the HD texture replacement layer that finds, composes and dumps replacement textures for PS1 draws and tracks VRAM upload residency.

- `fail` (L71) — Writes the given message into the caller's error buffer when one is supplied, truncated to its capacity.
- `is_beetle_root` (L74) — True when the folder holds a Hashes.ini file or is named like a Beetle texture-replacements folder.
- `window_coord` (L83) — Applies a texture-window mask and offset to one texture coordinate and returns the windowed value.
- `make_query` (L86) — Fills a draw query from texpage, CLUT and texture window; returns false when the draw cannot use replacements.
- `replacement_class` (L113) — Maps a replacement pixel's alpha to a PS1 class: 255 opaque, 0 transparent, or 128 semi-transparent.
- `replacement_pixel` (L119) — Samples the replacement image at x,y, nearest or linear, into RGBA output while keeping the PS1 alpha class.
- `native_pixel` (L146) — Decodes one native VRAM texel at u,v into RGBA using the page depth and palette, with PS1 alpha rules.
- `composition_signature` (L157) — Builds the key that identifies a draw's native texture, palette and matched parts, used to cache compositions.
- `find_composition` (L183) — Looks up a cached composition by signature and ready mask, counts a hit and returns it, or null if absent.
- `compose` (L191) — Builds a composed replacement texture from the matched parts for one draw; returns null when it cannot be built.
- `dump_query` (L255) — Dumps the draw's native texture to the pack folder when dumping is on; a failure stops dumping safely.
- `gpu_hd_textures_configure` (L269) — Starts or replaces the texture-pack session for a root folder with replacement and dump options; returns 1 on success.
- `gpu_hd_textures_shutdown` (L346) — Turns off HD texture mode, clears the GL texture cache and drops the active session.
- `gpu_hd_textures_reload` (L351) — Reconfigures the active session again from its stored root and options; returns 1 on success.
- `gpu_hd_textures_set_dump_enabled` (L356) — Turns texture dumping on or off, syncing the render thread and flushing pending dumps when turned off.
- `gpu_hd_textures_replacements_enabled` (L371) — Returns 1 when texture replacements are active in the current session.
- `gpu_hd_textures_dump_enabled` (L372) — Returns 1 when texture dumping is active in the current session.
- `gpu_hd_textures_active` (L373) — Returns 1 when a session exists with replacements or dumping turned on.
- `gpu_hd_textures_get_diag` (L374) — Copies the session's counters and settings into the output struct, after syncing the render thread.
- `gpu_hd_textures_note_applied` (L400) — Counts one draw that was drawn with a replacement texture, for the diagnostics.
- `gpu_hd_textures_note_gl_cache` (L401) — Counts one GL texture cache eviction or upload, chosen by the flag.
- `gpu_hd_textures_bind_vram` (L407) — Move to another copy of the same native VRAM (the GL render thread's private copy and gpu.c's array match at every hand-off); keeps residency.
- `gpu_hd_textures_suppress_dumps` (L408) — Smooth motion's generated frames replay real frames' draws for presentation only: their queries never dump (renderer thread).
- `gpu_hd_textures_set_vram` (L409) — Native VRAM and residency hooks.
- `gpu_hd_textures_reset_tracking` (L410) — Clears the GL texture cache, cached compositions and upload tracking in both texture packs.
- `gpu_hd_textures_begin_upload` (L418) — Header-before-payload invalidation and pre/post native copy observations.
- `gpu_hd_textures_begin_copy` (L423) — Starts tracking a VRAM-to-VRAM copy, invalidates the destination and notes whether the copy is pending.
- `gpu_hd_textures_end_copy` (L433) — Completes a pending VRAM copy and resets all tracking if the pack reports an error.
- `put32` (L443) — Writes a 32-bit value into four bytes in little-endian order.
- `get32` (L444) — Reads a little-endian 32-bit value from four bytes.
- `gpu_hd_textures_residency_save` (L446) — Savestate sidecar: the Beetle upload residency at save time, bound to a CRC of the whole native VRAM.
- `gpu_hd_textures_residency_load` (L462) — Restores saved residency after checking the blob's magic, version, pack identity and VRAM checksum; returns 1 on success.
- `gpu_hd_textures_invalidate` (L472) — Invalidates tracked textures and pack data that overlap a VRAM rectangle, resetting all tracking for very large rectangles.
- `gpu_hd_textures_track_upload` (L478) — Records an upload rectangle as Beetle-keyed residency, reading the applied words from the native VRAM mirror.
- `gpu_hd_textures_restage` (L516) — A full VRAM restage (savestate, rewind): reset residency, then re-admit the Beetle-keyed upload rectangles seen this session whose restored words still carry the same key.
- `acquire_draw` (L533) — Shared draw lookup: builds the query, dumps it, and returns a replacement image lease, optionally from the GL cache.
- `gpu_hd_textures_acquire_draw` (L617) — Looks up a replacement texture for a draw; returns 1 and fills the image when one applies.
- `gpu_hd_textures_acquire_gl_draw` (L621) — Same as the normal draw lookup but also lets the GL texture cache supply the replacement image.
- `gpu_hd_textures_release_image` (L625) — Releases the lease held by an image from an acquire call and clears the image struct.
- `gpu_hd_textures_observe_draw` (L629) — Dumps a draw's texture when dumping is on, without asking for a replacement image.

### runtime/src/gpu_render.c

Front door of the GPU layer: selects the active renderer backend (software, OpenGL or Vulkan) and forwards every draw, VRAM and native-wide call to it.

- `hd_observe_triangle` (L74) — Dumps a textured triangle's texture for HD texture packs when dumping is on; does nothing for OpenGL.
- `hd_observe_rect` (L83) — Dumps a textured rectangle's texture for HD texture packs when dumping is on; does nothing for OpenGL.
- `hd_note` (L92) — A backend that replays commands on another thread (the GL render thread) owns its VRAM copy there, so residency changes travel with its commands.
- `hd_invalidate_draw` (L103) — Residency describes guest native words, so any draw/copy which can touch an upload ends its identity.
- `hd_invalidate_triangle` (L114) — Ends the residency identity of any uploaded texture that a triangle or line bounding box may touch.
- `gr_set_backend` (L123) — Selects OpenGL, Vulkan or software rendering, falling back to software when the requested backend is unavailable.
- `gr_backend` (L149) — Returns the backend actually in use, which can differ from the one requested after a fallback.
- `gr_refresh_backend` (L154) — Re-fetch the OpenGL table after the render thread starts or stops (gl_backend_get then returns the recording table, or the direct one).
- `gr_init` (L162) — ---- Dispatch wrappers (one line each; forward to the active backend) ----
- `gr_set_scale` (L163) — Sets the internal resolution scale factor on the active backend.
- `gr_scale` (L164) — Returns the internal resolution scale factor of the active backend.
- `gr_set_texture_filter` (L165) — Sets texture filtering on the active backend: 0 nearest, 1 bilinear.
- `gr_texture_filter` (L166) — Returns the active backend's texture filter mode (0 nearest, 1 bilinear).
- `gr_set_semi_transparency` (L167) — Per-primitive draw state
- `gr_set_mask_bits` (L168) — Sets the set-mask and check-mask bits for the next primitives on the active backend.
- `gr_set_texture_window` (L169) — Sets the texture window from its raw GP0 value and remembers it for HD texture lookup.
- `gr_set_color_modulation` (L170) — Sets the per-primitive color modulation values and the raw color word on the active backend.
- `gr_set_precise_triangle` (L171) — Passes sub-pixel vertex positions for the next triangle to a backend that supports them.
- `gr_set_perspective_triangle` (L176) — Perspective-correct UV weights for the NEXT triangle ([video] perspective_texturing).
- `gr_set_dither` (L181) — GP0(E1h) bit 9 (dither enable).
- `gr_set_depth_triangle` (L184) — PGXP depth for the NEXT triangle (docs/ENHANCEMENTS.md G1.14): the GTE SZ of each vertex (1..65535), taken from validated dataflow shadows.
- `gr_fill_rect` (L188) — Primitives
- `gr_copy_rect` (L189) — Copies a VRAM rectangle, first noting the copy for HD texture tracking when HD textures are active.
- `gr_draw_flat_triangle` (L204) — Draws a flat-shaded triangle on the active backend, then invalidates HD texture residency it may touch.
- `gr_draw_gouraud_triangle` (L209) — Draws a triangle with per-vertex colors on the active backend, then invalidates HD texture residency it may touch.
- `gr_draw_textured_triangle` (L215) — Draws a textured triangle, first noting it for HD texture dumps and passing CLUT and texpage to the backend.
- `gr_draw_shaded_textured_triangle` (L224) — Draws a textured triangle with per-vertex colors and CLUT, texpage and raw flags, forwarded to the backend.
- `gr_draw_flat_rect` (L235) — Draws a flat-colored rectangle on the active backend, then invalidates HD texture residency it covers.
- `gr_draw_textured_rect` (L236) — Draws a textured rectangle, first noting it for HD texture dumps, then invalidates the covered residency.
- `gr_draw_textured_rect_scaled` (L242) — Draws a textured rectangle whose texture spans from u0,v0 to u1,v1, with the same HD texture hooks.
- `gr_draw_line` (L248) — Draws a flat-colored line on the active backend and invalidates HD texture residency along its box.
- `gr_draw_shaded_line` (L249) — Draws a line with two vertex colors on the active backend and invalidates HD texture residency along its box.
- `gr_render_display` (L253) — Renders the displayed VRAM area into a 32-bit buffer for the CPU readout path; returns the backend's result.
- `gr_render_display_hires` (L256) — Renders the displayed area at the high-resolution scale into a 32-bit buffer; returns the backend's result.
- `gr_vram_upload_begin` (L259) — VRAM transfers A0 header invalidation precedes payload writes; an interrupted transfer cannot leave a prior immutable texture identity resident.
- `gr_vram_upload_commit` (L263) — The A0 payload is complete: hand the staged words to the renderer and end the open upload.
- `gr_vram_upload_set_open` (L267) — gpu.c's GP0 state says whether an A0 payload is still streaming into its array: GP1(01h) aborts one, a savestate load can restore one.
- `gr_vram_write` (L268) — Writes one 15-bit pixel into VRAM at x,y and invalidates HD texture residency for that pixel.
- `gr_vram_read` (L269) — Reads one 15-bit pixel from VRAM at x,y.
- `gr_vram_transfer_in` (L270) — Copies a CPU-supplied block of pixels into VRAM and notes the upload for HD texture tracking.
- `gr_vram_transfer_out` (L271) — Copies a block of VRAM pixels out to a CPU buffer.
- `gr_set_draw_area` (L272) — Draw area / offset
- `gr_get_draw_area` (L273) — Returns the current draw area corners through the four output pointers.
- `gr_set_draw_offset` (L274) — Sets the draw offset on the active backend and remembers it for HD texture lookup.
- `gr_wide_supported` (L277) — Native-wide compositor — present only on backends that supply it.
- `gr_wide_configure` (L278) — Configures native-wide rendering with a wide width and offset, when the backend supports it.
- `gr_wide_set_view` (L281) — Presentation-only origin and padding, independent of the symmetric budget.
- `gr_wide_set_target` (L284) — Selects which native-wide surface receives mirrored draws for the back buffer at base_x.
- `gr_wide_disable_target` (L287) — Stops mirroring draws into a native-wide surface, for offscreen draws without a framebuffer target.
- `gr_wide_clear` (L290) — Clears a band of the native-wide surface for base_x across the full wide width, when the backend supports it.
- `gr_wide_clear_margins` (L293) — sides: bit 0 = left synthetic margin, bit 1 = right.
- `gr_wide_feedback_rect` (L297) — Copies a rectangle inside the native-wide surface with a color and flags, used for blending trails, when supported.
- `gr_render_wide_display` (L303) — Converts the native-wide surface for the displayed buffer into an output pixel buffer; returns 0 if unsupported.
- `gr_wide_dump_full` (L309) — Dumps the entire native-wide surface for base_x into an output buffer for diagnostics; returns 0 if unsupported.

### runtime/src/gpu_sw_edges.h

Edge stepping helpers for the software rasterizer: fixed-point edge walking that gives PS1-exact triangle coverage.

- `psx_edge_fp` (L11) — PS1 polygon coverage uses a biased 32.32 edge DDA with exclusive bottom and right edges.
- `psx_edge_step` (L12) — Returns the 32.32 fixed-point step for an edge with the given dx and dy, from the shared edge helper.
- `psx_edge_unfp` (L14) — Converts a 32.32 fixed-point edge value back to a whole pixel coordinate by taking the integer half.
- `psx_triangle_edges_at_y` (L19) — Vertices must already be sorted by Y.

### runtime/src/gpu_sw_renderer.c

Software rasterizer: draws PS1 primitives (triangles, rectangles, lines, textures, blending) into VRAM, the supersampled mirror and the native-wide surface.

- `clamp_i` (L110) — Clamps an int to the range lo..hi.
- `min_i` (L116) — Returns the smaller of two ints.
- `max_i` (L117) — Returns the larger of two ints.
- `vram_get` (L119) — Reads one 15-bit pixel from the canonical VRAM array, wrapping x and y to the VRAM size.
- `rt_native` (L141) — Describes the native-resolution VRAM as a render target with the current clip rectangle.
- `rt_hires` (L148) — Describes the supersampled high-resolution mirror as a render target, scaled to the current scale factor.
- `rt_wide` (L170) — Describes the active native-wide surface as a render target with the current scale factor.
- `wide_dx` (L183) — X-translation (native px) from canonical VRAM space into the active wide surface: local_x = vram_x - base_x + OFFSET.
- `wide_bd_get` (L193) — Reads the current backdrop stretch settings from the widescreen module into a WideBd struct.
- `wide_bd_x` (L208) — Maps an x coordinate through the backdrop stretch, rounding half away from zero; returns x if no stretch is on.
- `blend_pixels` (L223) — Blends a front 15-bit pixel over a back pixel using the PS1 semi-transparency mode (average, add, subtract, quarter-add).
- `put_opaque` (L265) — Write an opaque (untextured) pixel with semi-transparency if enabled
- `put_textured` (L289) — Write a textured pixel — semi-trans only if texel bit 15 is set
- `texel_fetch` (L338) — Fetches one texel at u,v applying the texture window and CLUT lookup for 4, 8 or 15-bit textures.
- `bl_fetch` (L385) — Fetches one texel for bilinear sampling, with texture window wrap, returning the raw 15-bit value.
- `texel_fetch_bilinear` (L405) — Bilinear texel sample, in RGB space (after the CLUT lookup — never interpolate palette indices).
- `bilinear_center_shift_for_target` (L441) — Returns the sample offset for bilinear filtering on a target with the given scale, so texels are sampled at their centers.
- `sw_tri_uv_limits` (L452) — Computes the sampled UV bounds of a textured triangle, from world-space UVs when perspective is valid, else affine.

### runtime/src/gpu_timeline.c

Keeps a fixed-size ring of recent GPU events with cycle and frame stamps, for the debug server to read.

- `gpu_timeline_note` (L11) — Records one GPU event of the given kind with two values into the ring, unless the timeline is frozen.
- `gpu_timeline_set_frozen` (L22) — Freezes or unfreezes the timeline so no new events are recorded while frozen.
- `gpu_timeline_total` (L24) — Returns how many GPU events have been recorded since start, including ones already overwritten.
- `gpu_timeline_get` (L26) — Copies the event with sequence number seq into out; returns 1 if it is still in the ring, else 0.
- `gpu_timeline_kind_name` (L32) — Returns a readable name such as vblank or draw_area for an event kind code.

### runtime/src/gpu_uv.h

Shared PS1 texture-coordinate model used by every render backend to decide which texels a textured primitive samples.

- `psx_uv_tri_dirs` (L49) — Signed uv step along each screen axis, area2-scaled (only signs matter; area2's sign normalizes winding).
- `psx_uv_axis_limits` (L66) — Pre-wrap one axis' exact sampled range into lim_lo/lim_hi.
- `psx_uv_tri_limits` (L77) — Inclusive sampled uv bounds for a textured triangle, from its ORIGINAL (uncompensated) vertex uvs.
- `psx_uv_rect_limits` (L93) — Inclusive sampled uv bounds for a rect prim, from its ORIGINAL uv corners (u0/v0 at the top-left raster corner; u1/v1 at the exclusive corner — u1 < u0 / v1 < v0 means mirrored).
- `psx_uv_tri_mirror_offset` (L103) — Mirrored-2D compensation for center-sampled rasterizers (GL/VK ONLY — never the software DDA): bump the uv +1 along each decreasing axis.
- `psx_uv_rect_mirror_offset` (L112) — Rect form: bump each mirrored axis' corner pair.
- `psx_uv_tri_world_limits` (L119) — Perspective mapping has no affine, integer-DDA exclusive texel endpoint.
- `psx_uv_tri_center_sample` (L131) — GL/VK polygon sampling: preserve world UVs; apply the existing PS1 center-sampling compensation only to affine primitives.

### runtime/src/gpu_vk_renderer.c

Vulkan GPU backend: owns the Vulkan device, swapchain, VRAM image, batched geometry and textured draws, and presents frames; builds as an inert stub when Vulkan is absent.

- `vk_renderer_init_context` (L39) — Vulkan SDK headers/glslc were not found at configure time: compile an inert backend so the runtime still builds and simply falls back to software.
- `vk_renderer_shutdown` (L40) — Tear down all Vulkan objects (idempotent).

- `vk_renderer_present_blank` (L44) — Stub in builds without Vulkan: does nothing; the real version presents a blank frame.

- `gpu_vram_dirty_mark_all` (L72) — Marks every scanline as dirty.

### runtime/src/gte.cpp

Emulates the PS1 Geometry Transform Engine (COP2): matrix, lighting, color and projection commands, plus host-side precision and debug recording for them.

- `gte_init_div_table` (L44) — Builds the reciprocal lookup table used by the GTE division unit, once.
- `gte_calc_recip` (L55) — Computes the reciprocal of a 16-bit divisor using the GTE lookup table, returning a fixed-point value.
- `gte_clz16` (L62) — count leading zeros of a 16-bit value (0 -> 16)

- `gte_instr_sf` (L91) — Returns the fraction shift of a GTE instruction: 12 when its sf bit is set, else 0.
- `gte_mac44_stage` (L93) — Wraps a 64-bit MAC value to the 44-bit GTE accumulator, sign-extends it, and reports overflow.
- `gte_store_mac_ir` (L102) — Stores a shifted MAC value into its MAC register and the matching saturated IR register.
- `light_transform` (L112) — Transform a vertex by Light matrix → IR1/IR2/IR3 (step 1 of lighting)
- `light_color` (L125) — Apply light color matrix + background color to IR → IR (step 2 of lighting)
- `push_rgb_from_mac` (L140) — Pushes a new color FIFO entry built from the MAC1 to MAC3 values, saturated to 8 bits per channel.

- `bcd_to_binary` (L76) — Converts one BCD byte to its decimal value.
- `binary_to_bcd` (L80) — Converts a decimal value below 100 to a BCD byte.

- `ISOReader::ISOReader` (L188) — Constructs a closed reader with an empty root directory.

- `ISOReader::ReadSubChannelQ` (L554) — Fills the subchannel Q data for an LBA, using replacements from the SBI file first; valid says whether the data is real.
- `ISOReader::SpanForLBA` (L588) — Returns the data span that contains lba, or nullptr; a linear scan over the spans.
- `ISOReader::ReadSector` (L599) — Reads one 2048-byte data sector at lba into buffer, from CHD or the BIN file; returns false on failure.
- `ISOReader::ReadRawSector` (L664) — Reads one full 2352-byte raw sector at lba into buffer; returns false on failure.
- `ISOReader::IsOpen` (L702) — True when an image is open.
- `ISOReader::GetVolumeID` (L706) — Returns the volume identifier from the disc's primary volume descriptor.
- `ISOReader::GetBinPath` (L710) — Returns the path of the image that was opened.
- `ISOReader::GetSectorCount` (L714) — Returns the number of sectors on the disc, or 0 when no image is open.
- `ISOReader::TrackCount` (L722) — Returns how many tracks the disc has.
- `ISOReader::TrackStartLBA` (L726) — Returns the start LBA of a track number, or 0 when that track does not exist.
- `ISOReader::TrackPregapLBA` (L733) — Returns the pregap LBA of a track number, or 0 when that track does not exist.
- `ISOReader::TrackIsAudio` (L740) — True when the given track number is an audio track.
- `ISOReader::GetRootDirectory` (L747) — Returns the location and size of the root directory.
- `ISOReader::Read733` (L751) — Reads the little-endian half of a both-endian 32-bit field.
- `ISOReader::ParseVolumeDescriptor` (L756) — Reads the primary volume descriptor at sector 16 and stores the volume ID and root directory; returns false when it is missing.
- `ISOReader::ParseDirectoryRecord` (L789) — Parses one ISO 9660 directory record into a file entry; returns false for an invalid or padding record.
- `ISOReader::ListFilesByLBA` (L838) — Lists the files of the directory at the given LBA and size; empty when the image is closed or the arguments are invalid.
- `ISOReader::ListFiles` (L888) — Lists the files in a directory path on the disc.
- `ISOReader::FindFile` (L925) — Looks up a file path on the disc and fills entry; returns false when it is not found.
- `ISOReader::ReadFile` (L984) — Reads a file's contents into buffer, up to max_size bytes; returns the number of bytes read.
- `ISOReader::GetFileSize` (L1023) — Returns the size in bytes of a file on the disc, or 0 when it is not found.

### runtime/src/iso_reader_c.cpp

C wrapper that gives the C side opaque-handle functions for the C++ disc reader, with mod overrides for sectors and CD audio tracks.

- `iso_open` (L14) — Opens a disc image and returns an opaque handle, or NULL when it cannot be opened.
- `iso_read_sector` (L23) — Reads one 2048-byte data sector into buffer, mod extents first; returns 1 on success and 0 otherwise.
- `iso_read_raw_sector` (L31) — Reads one 2352-byte raw sector into buffer, mod extents first; returns 1 on success and 0 otherwise.
- `iso_read_subq` (L39) — Fills the 12-byte subchannel Q data for an LBA and sets valid; returns 1 on success.
- `iso_has_subq_replacements` (L66) — Returns nonzero when the image carries subchannel Q replacement data.
- `iso_sector_count` (L70) — Returns the disc's sector count, including any mod-supplied extent.
- `iso_track_count` (L77) — CD-track TOC accessors (multi-track / CD-DA support).
- `iso_track_start_lba` (L82) — Returns a track's start LBA; the track after the last one maps to the mod extent when one is set.
- `iso_track_pregap_lba` (L89) — Returns a track's pregap LBA, with the same mod extent rule for the track after the last.
- `iso_track_is_audio` (L95) — Returns 1 when the track is an audio track, else 0.
- `iso_close` (L100) — Closes the image and frees a handle returned by iso_open.
- `iso_cdda_track_count` (L108) — Audio-only overrides never affect filesystem reads, XA or disc validation.
- `iso_cdda_track_start_lba` (L112) — Returns a CD audio track's start LBA, from the mod override when one is set, else from the disc.
- `iso_cdda_track_pregap_lba` (L115) — Returns a CD audio track's pregap LBA, from the mod override when one is set, else from the disc.
- `iso_cdda_track_is_audio` (L118) — Returns 1 for an audio track: tracks 2 up to the override count when one is set, else the disc's answer.
- `iso_cdda_sector_count` (L122) — Returns the CD audio sector count from the mod override when one is set, else the disc's count.
- `iso_read_cdda_sector` (L125) — Reads one 2352-byte CD audio sector from the mod override or the raw disc sector; returns 1 on success.

### runtime/src/kernel_patch_ranges.c

Checks whether guest RAM still matches the kernel ROM image outside the kernel patch ranges, for the patch bookkeeping.

- `psx_kernel_patch_cmp` (L7) — Compares guest RAM with the ROM image over the byte span lo to hi, skipping the patched ranges; returns 1 at the first difference, 0 when they match, and counts skipped ranges into skips_out.
- `psx_kernel_patch_ends_at` (L33) — Returns 1 when one of the patch ranges ends exactly at the physical address phys, else 0.

### runtime/src/latency_ring.c

Always-on ring of per-frame timestamps that measures input-to-screen latency and frame timing for the latency summaries.

- `qpc` (L21) — Current value of the SDL high-resolution performance counter.
- `qpc_freq` (L22) — Performance counter frequency in ticks per second, never below 1 so divisions are safe.
- `latency_ring_frame_begin` (L27) — Begin a new frame slot and stamp LAT_INPUT.
- `latency_ring_mark` (L36) — Stamp the current frame slot at 'stage' (no-op for LAT_INPUT — use latency_ring_frame_begin for that).
- `latency_ring_restamp_input` (L43) — Re-stamp the current slot's LAT_INPUT to now.
- `latency_ring_set_backend` (L48) — Note which present backend produced the most recent swaps ("opengl", "software", "vulkan").
- `latency_ring_set_present_mode` (L54) — Note the effective present mode / swap interval for the summary label (e.g.
- `collect` (L61) — Collect a delta series (in microseconds) over the last 'window' completed frames into 'out', returning the count.
- `dcmp` (L88) — qsort comparison for doubles, in ascending order.
- `stat_obj` (L94) — Append "name":{mean,min,max,p50,p95,n} stats for a delta series to buf.
- `latency_ring_summary_json` (L111) — JSON summary over the last 'window' completed frames (clamped): mean/min/max/ p50/p95 in microseconds of frame_period, input->swap, and swap_block (the present/swap blocking time — the key vsync/queue
- `latency_ring_dump_json` (L139) — JSON array of the last 'max_frames' raw frame records (timestamps in microseconds relative to the oldest reported frame).

### runtime/src/load_accel.c

Load-time shortcut for the BIOS VSync query routine, which can skip the wait for the next frame while the CD is busy.

- `psx_vsync_query_hle_configure` (L58) — Stores the guest addresses of the VSync query routine and its counter and timer data, so calls to that routine can be intercepted.
- `psx_vsync_query_hle_try` (L69) — If dispatch_addr is the configured VSync query routine, runs the shortcut and returns 1; otherwise returns 0 and the real routine runs.
- `psx_vsync_query_hle_set_enabled` (L76) — Turns the VSync query shortcut on or off.
- `psx_vsync_query_hle_set_horizon_enabled` (L77) — Turns the event-horizon skip for the main list of return sites on or off.
- `psx_vsync_query_hle_set_extra_horizon_enabled` (L80) — Turns the event-horizon skip for the extra list of return sites on or off.
- `psx_vsync_query_hle_set_horizon_any` (L83) — When set, any VSync(-1) may event-horizon while CD is busy (not only listed return PCs).
- `psx_vsync_query_hle_add_event_horizon_site` (L85) — Adds a return address to the main event-horizon site list, ignoring zero and duplicates.
- `psx_vsync_query_hle_add_extra_event_horizon_site` (L94) — Adds a return address to the extra event-horizon site list, ignoring zero and duplicates.
- `is_event_horizon_site` (L104) — Returns 1 when return_pc is in the main site list, 2 when it is in the extra list, else 0.
- `psx_vsync_query_hle_enter` (L112) — Runs the VSync query shortcut for a call that matches the rules; returns 1 when it handled the call and 0 when the real routine must run.
- `psx_vsync_query_hle_stats_json` (L241) — Writes the shortcut's enable flags and call counters as JSON fields into buf, up to cap bytes.
- `psx_vsync_query_hle_horizon_totals` (L264) — Cumulative VSync(-1) event-horizon skips (for post-load probe deltas).

### runtime/src/lobby_ws/rnet_sha1.c

Compact public-domain SHA-1 implementation used by the lobby WebSocket handshake.

- `rol` (L13) — Rotates a 32-bit value left by n bits.
- `sha1_process` (L15) — Runs the SHA-1 compression function over one 64-byte block and folds it into the context state.
- `sha1_init` (L60) — Resets a SHA-1 context to the standard initial hash values.
- `sha1_update` (L71) — Feeds len bytes into the SHA-1 context, processing each 64-byte block as it fills.
- `sha1_final` (L84) — Pads the message and writes its 20-byte SHA-1 digest to out.
- `rnet_sha1` (L110) — One-call SHA-1: hashes len bytes at data into the 20-byte out buffer.

### runtime/src/lobby_ws/rnet_ws.c

Minimal WebSocket helpers for the lobby: the accept-key handshake, sending all bytes, and writing and reading text frames.

- `socket_would_block` (L16) — True when the last socket call failed only because it would block and should be retried later.
- `socket_interrupted` (L25) — True when the last socket call was interrupted by a signal and can be retried.
- `b64_encode` (L37) — Base64-encodes n bytes of in into out with padding; out must have room for the encoded text.
- `rnet_ws_accept_key` (L82) — Computes the WebSocket accept key from the client key (SHA-1 then base64) into out_b64; returns -1 on bad arguments.
- `send_all` (L99) — Sends all len bytes on the socket, looping over partial sends; returns -1 on error.
- `rnet_ws_write_text` (L123) — Returns bytes written to out, or -1.
- `rnet_ws_read_text` (L173) — Read one text frame into buf (NUL-terminated).

### runtime/src/local_mouse_policy.cpp

Decision logic for a title's local mouse control: when the host mouse may capture the game, how events are timed, and when the capture is released.

- `LocalMousePolicy::install` (L8) — Registers the title's mouse policy once; rejects a null, invalid, or repeated policy and returns false.
- `LocalMousePolicy::clear` (L16) — Resets the capture state and drops the registered policy and host state.
- `LocalMousePolicy::persistent_capture` (L28) — Turns click-to-capture persistence on or off; returns false when no policy is installed.
- `LocalMousePolicy::capture_across_transitions` (L34) — Turns keeping the capture through title transitions on or off; returns false when no policy is installed.
- `LocalMousePolicy::dispatch` (L40) — Sends one mouse event (type, time, dx, dy) to the policy's event callback.
- `LocalMousePolicy::reset` (L45) — Releases any mouse capture and clears the capture and suspend state.
- `LocalMousePolicy::hold_control` (L55) — Returns the control key (right button or left Alt) that holds the capture, or none.
- `LocalMousePolicy::allowed` (L60) — True when the policy is installed, the game has focus, an analog pad is connected, and the policy's eligibility check passes.
- `LocalMousePolicy::capture_allowed` (L64) — True when the policy is installed, the game has focus, an analog pad is connected, and the right stick is not in use.
- `LocalMousePolicy::suspend` (L68) — Pauses mouse output, keeping the capture, and blocks a held hold button until it is released.
- `LocalMousePolicy::update` (L76) — Each frame, stores the time and host state; resets the policy when the clock has stalled.
- `LocalMousePolicy::valid_time` (L106) — True when an event time is recent, not before the last release, and in order; otherwise resets the policy and returns false.
- `LocalMousePolicy::control` (L116) — Handles a button or hold-key press or release, starting or ending the capture; returns true when the control was used.
- `LocalMousePolicy::sync_left` (L196) — Releases the left activation when the physical button is up, so a missed release does not stick.
- `LocalMousePolicy::motion` (L200) — Forwards a mouse movement (dx, dy) to the event callback while captured and allowed; otherwise resets or suspends the capture.
- `LocalMousePolicy::sample` (L213) — Writes the current mouse stick offsets into rx and ry while captured; resets or suspends the capture when not allowed.
- `LocalMousePolicy::wheel` (L228) — Forwards a wheel step to the event callback when captured, allowed, finite and timely; returns true when sent.

### runtime/src/local_mouse_sdl.cpp

SDL glue for the local mouse policy: window capture, event timestamps, focus checks, and the psx_local_mouse_* calls the frame loop uses.

- `now_ns` (L11) — Current time in nanoseconds from SDL's tick counter.
- `event_ns` (L29) — Converts an SDL event's timestamp to nanoseconds, lifting SDL2's wrapping millisecond stamp to the nearest current time.
- `scancode` (L40) — Maps a mouse control (Escape, Left Alt or a mouse button) to its SDL scancode.
- `capture` (L47) — Turns relative mouse mode on or off for the game window; returns false when there is no window.
- `suppress` (L55) — Blocks the keyboard binding of one control so its key press is not also sent to the game.
- `notice` (L58) — Shows a short on-screen message for two seconds.
- `state` (L59) — Returns the one shared local mouse policy, created with the SDL callbacks on first use.
- `focus` (L63) — True when the game window has keyboard focus and is neither hidden nor minimized.
- `conflict` (L68) — True when the key bound to the hold control is also bound to a game button, so the two would clash.
- `update` (L76) — Each frame, refreshes the focus and conflict flags and updates the shared policy with the current time.
- `control` (L81) — Forwards a control press or release to the policy, releasing its keyboard binding; returns true when it was used or suppressed.
- `psx_mod_set_local_mouse_policy` (L89) — Installs a title's local mouse policy; returns 1 on success, or prints the reason and returns 0.
- `psx_mod_set_local_mouse_persistent_capture` (L97) — Optional action-game capture: click once to capture, Escape to release.
- `psx_mod_set_local_mouse_capture_across_transitions` (L100) — Optional persistent-capture companion: keep existing capture through title eligibility changes (menus/cutscenes/loading), Start and host stalls, while clearing mouse motion and suspending output.
- `psx_local_mouse_clear` (L103) — All calls, including reset/release, belong to the SDL owner thread.
- `psx_local_mouse_installed` (L104) — Returns 1 when a local mouse policy is installed.
- `psx_local_mouse_reset` (L105) — Resets the policy and clears the host pad's connected and analog flags.
- `psx_local_mouse_begin` (L109) — Start of each frame: when a policy is installed, records the game window and whether it is live, then updates the policy; otherwise does nothing.
- `psx_local_mouse_event` (L138) — Handles one SDL event for the mouse policy (motion, buttons, wheel, keys); returns true when the event was consumed.
- `psx_local_mouse_pad` (L211) — Stores the host pad's connection, analog state, buttons and right stick for the policy, when one is installed.

Entry point and main loop of the recompiled PS1 runtime: starts the host, presents video and audio, reads input, and hosts the menus, mod hooks and netplay.

### runtime/src/mdec.c

PS1 MDEC (motion decoder) emulation: the input and output FIFOs, command handling, macroblock decode, DMA hooks, debug trace and snapshot save and load.

- `trace_event` (L99) — Appends one MDEC debug event (kind, value, frame and sequence number) to the trace ring; compiled out without debug tools.
- `clamp_int` (L125) — Returns the value limited to the range lo..hi.
- `clear_output` (L131) — Empties the MDEC output buffer and resets its read position.
- `ensure_input_capacity` (L136) — Grows the input halfword buffer to hold the given count; returns 1 on success, 0 if allocation fails.
- `ensure_output_capacity` (L147) — Grows the output byte buffer to hold the given byte count; returns 1 on success, 0 if allocation fails.
- `append_byte` (L158) — Appends one byte to the output buffer, growing it when needed.

### runtime/src/mdec_core.c

Core MDEC math: dequantisation, inverse DCT, block decode and YCbCr to RGB colour conversion for blocks and macroblocks.

- `floor_shr` (L24) — floor(v / 2^n) for either sign.
- `sat` (L28) — Clamps v to the range lo..hi.
- `sgn` (L32) — Returns -1, 0 or 1 for the sign of v.
- `sext10` (L36) — Sign-extends the low 10 bits of w to a signed 32-bit number.
- `sext16` (L41) — Sign-extends a 16-bit value to a signed 32-bit number.
- `clip8` (L46) — clip8 (2): the low 9 bits as a signed number, then saturated to 8 bits.
- `idct_round` (L53) — R(s) = floor((s + 2^14) / 2^15), the rounding of each IDCT pass (4.4).
- `mdec_core_set_scale` (L57) — Command 3: the 64 halfwords as received -> the table the decoder keeps (and the snapshot stores): table[8c + r] = floor(raw[8r + c] / 8).
- `dequantise` (L66) — 4.2: value x at scan index k, q = quant[0] (DC) or qscale * quant[k] (AC), to a coefficient in sixteenths of psx-spx's units.
- `idct` (L78) — 4.4: out[8y + x] = P[y][x] from coef[8u + h] = C[u][h], with S[r][c] = table[8c + r].
- `mdec_core_decode_block` (L107) — Decodes one block of compressed input (DC plus run-length AC codes) into 64 coefficients, dequantises and inverse-transforms them into out; returns 0 when no input is left.
- `to5` (L150) — 5.4: one channel (-128..127) to five bits.
- `mdec_core_color_macroblock` (L155) — Converts one 16x16 macroblock from its Cr and Cb blocks and four Y blocks into packed pixels in out, at the given depth.

- `psx_cyc_readmem` (L2578) — Beetle ReadMemory data-access timing (cpu.cpp:369-448), after §1/deps/DO_LDS.

- `psx_cyc_load_timing` (L2624) — The interlock half of a load (§1+deps+(cancel)+DO_LDS+ReadMemory).

- `psx_cyc_load_byte` (L2688) — Timed 8-bit load for generated code: charges the load timing, then returns the byte from RAM or the full read.
- `psx_cyc_lwc2_read_slow` (L2700) — LWC2 (GTE load): §1/DO_LDS done by psx_cyc_step(cpu,0); the GTE deadline stall by psx_gte_stall — both emitted before this call.
