- `psx_guest_read_half` (L2721) — Untimed 16-bit read for guest code, with no load timing charged.
- `psx_guest_read_byte` (L2722) — Untimed 8-bit read for guest code, with no load timing charged.
- `psx_cyc_load_word_host` (L2728) — The overlay DLLs' timed loads (overlay_loader.c callbacks): the same entries the main program inlines (psx_cyc.h), main RAM and scratchpad on the short path, everything else on the slow one.
- `psx_cyc_load_half_host` (L2731) — Timed 16-bit load for overlay DLLs, the same as the main program's inline load.
- `psx_cyc_load_byte_host` (L2734) — Timed 8-bit load for overlay DLLs, using the fast byte-load path.
- `psx_cyc_lwc2_read_host` (L2737) — Timed GTE load for overlay DLLs: reads a word for LWC2 with its timing.
- `psx_blk_load_slow` (L2743) — [recompiler] cpu_timing = "block": a load outside main RAM and the scratchpad (psx_cyc.h psx_blk_load_*): its access cost, then the read.
- `psx_write_byte` (L2753) — Guest 8-bit store entry point, with the same fast path and special cases as the word store.
- `psx_host_write_word` (L2772) — Host stores: the same paths as a guest store, but never cache-isolated (cpu_store_isolated).
- `psx_host_write_half` (L2778) — Host 16-bit store: works like a guest store, but is never cache-isolated.
- `psx_host_write_byte` (L2784) — Host 8-bit store: works like a guest store, but is never cache-isolated.
- `psx_write_byte_raw` (L2791) — Performs an 8-bit store to RAM or a device, honouring cache isolation and KSEG2.
- `psx_mem_gate_value` (L2876) — psx_mem_gate.h (g_psx_mem_gate lives in psx_cycles.c): raised by every writer that sets one of the stores' global gates; lowered here once all are clear.
- `__attribute__` (L2889) — The gate was raised: lower it if every flag is clear (1: the short path may go on).
- `psx_mem_gate_flags` (L2896) — Returns the combined store gate flags that decide whether the fast store path may be used.
- `psx_store_pages_forget_all` (L2901) — Clears every cached store-page classification so each page is recomputed on its next store.
- `psx_store_page_kind` (L2906) — 1: every aligned store to the page is a plain store here; 2: one is when its text line is already marked (text_line_mark would do nothing); 0: neither (kernel window, executed code, watched overlay pa
- `psx_store_pages_audit` (L2917) — Debug check: aborts if a cached page classification no longer matches the current state.
- `psx_store_fast_ptr` (L2934) — Where a plain store may go directly: main RAM (above the kernel window, on a page no code watcher acts on) or the scratchpad, which the full path writes with nothing else to do (no mod aperture reache
- `psx_store_try_word` (L2970) — Tries a 32-bit store through the fast path; returns 1 when it wrote the value, 0 to fall back to the full path.
- `psx_store_try_half` (L2982) — Tries a 16-bit store through the fast path; returns 1 when handled, 0 to fall back.
- `psx_store_try_byte` (L2991) — Tries an 8-bit store through the fast path; returns 1 when handled, 0 to fall back.

### runtime/src/mod_builtin_bezel.c

Built-in mod that enables the bezel artwork overlay, using the artwork the player picked.

- `builtin_bezel_activate` (L13) — Activation hook: applies the selected bezel image, or logs that none is chosen.

### runtime/src/mod_builtin_hd_textures.c

Built-in mod that turns on the HD texture pack with its replacement and dump options.

- `hd_texture_option` (L8) — Reads a true or false option for the HD texture pack, returning the fallback when it is missing.
- `builtin_hd_textures_activate` (L14) — Activation hook: sets the HD texture pack with its replacements and dump options.

### runtime/src/mod_builtin_pgxp.c

Built-in mod that enables PGXP geometry precision, with its CPU mode and culling options.

- `pgxp_option_flag` (L32) — Reads a true or false option from the PGXP feature; false when it is missing.
- `builtin_pgxp_activate` (L38) — Activation hook: enables PGXP with its CPU mode and culling options.

### runtime/src/mod_builtin_ram.c

Built-in mods that change the main RAM size, such as the 8 MB option.

- `builtin_8mb_ram_activate` (L9) — Activation hook: switches main RAM to 8 MB.

### runtime/src/mod_builtin_speed.c

Built-in mods for fast loading and CD speed, with their option readers.

- `speed_option_number` (L23) — Reads a positive integer option, returning the fallback when it is missing or not a valid positive number.
- `speed_option_flag` (L34) — Reads a true or false speed option; false when it is missing.
- `builtin_fast_loading_activate` (L41) — Activation hook for fast loading: sets the load acceleration multiplier, where 0 means uncapped.
- `builtin_cd_speed_activate` (L53) — Activation hook for CD speed: sets the instant scheduler budget, or the disc speed divisor.

### runtime/src/mod_controller_source.c

Holds the controller sources that mods can attach to each player port, and samples them once per frame with validation.

- `psx_mod_set_controller_source` (L15) — Attaches or detaches a controller source on a player port; a detach keeps a neutral release pending. Returns 0 for a bad port.
- `psx_mod_set_controller_source_connected` (L25) — Presence of an attached offline source (default connected).
- `mod_controller_source_connected` (L31) — Returns 1 when the port has an attached source that reports connected.
- `mod_controller_source_reset` (L36) — Detach every source but keep a neutral release pending for each port that had one, so held buttons/sticks are cleared even on a port with no device.
- `mod_controller_source_begin_frame` (L45) — Clears the per-frame sample cache so each port is sampled once per frame.
- `mod_controller_source_present` (L48) — Returns 1 when a source is attached to the port.
- `note_bad` (L51) — Logs an invalid controller state from a source, rate-limited, and counts it.
- `mod_controller_source_sample` (L62) — Reads a port's controller state for this frame into state, using the per-frame cache; returns 1 when a state is available and sets released when a release is pending.

Services that trusted mods use to call guest functions and touch guest memory, with cycle-uncharged spans and GTE and CPU state readers.

- `psx_mod_call_guest` (L18) — Calls a guest function with up to four arguments, saving and restoring the CPU registers, and returns its result.

- `timing_restore` (L61) — Restores the CPU timing state from a saved caller record.

- `psx_mod_uncharged_span_end` (L118) — Ends an uncharged span, restoring timing when it was uncharged, and reports the counted cycles.
- `psx_mod_uncharged_span_active` (L132) — Returns 1 while an uncharged span is open.
- `psx_mod_dma_write_ram` (L134) — Copies host data into guest RAM through the CD DMA path, tagged with a disc LBA; returns 0 in host output.
- `ram_span` (L140) — Returns 1 when a guest address range of the given length lies within live main RAM.

- `psx_mod_spu_private_voice_stop` (L176) — Stops the private SPU voices in the mask.

- `psx_mod_set_overdraw` (L243) — Overdraw guard band: keep geometry up to x / y screen px past the picture's edges (the game's auto_screen_x culls and their paired height compares, see [widescreen.cull]); the picture itself is unchan
- `psx_mod_set_overdraw_share` (L244) — The share of the band (the overdraw, not the extra) in use, of 16: 16 = whole (the default), 0 = none while it stays on.
- `psx_mod_set_overdraw_extra` (L245) — More of that band for part of a frame: x / y px past it while the overdraw is on (shadows), e.g.

- `psx_mod_cpu_gpr` (L255) — A CPU general register (0..31) as the guest left it; 0 before the CPU is bound.

### runtime/src/mod_internal_resolution.c

Resolution hints for mod render settings: sets the internal rendering height that a mod session requests, with a reset back to the default.

Input policy helper for local presentation plugins: says whether live host input may be read while the controller is available offline.

### runtime/src/mod_media.cpp

Media loading for mods: reads donor disc sectors, checks media files against their expected size and SHA-256, and reads big-endian and little-endian values.

- `le32` (L15) — Reads a little-endian 32-bit value from a byte pointer.
- `be32` (L19) — Reads a big-endian 32-bit value from a byte pointer.
- `read_disc_sector` (L24) — Reads one 2048-byte data sector from a donor disc, taking the user data from raw sectors when needed; throws when the sector cannot be read.
- `load_mod_media` (L36) — Loads a mod media file, checking its expected size and SHA-256; returns false with an error message on failure.

### runtime/src/mod_netplay.c

Netplay profile for title mods: registers the title's compatibility id, aspect and settings, and reports the session state.

- `psx_mod_register_netplay_profile` (L11) — Registers the title's netplay profile after validating its ids, aspect mask and settings; returns 0 when invalid.
- `psx_mod_netplay_profile` (L33) — Returns the registered netplay profile, or NULL when none is set.
- `psx_mod_netplay_version` (L34) — Returns the profile's compatibility id as the netplay version, or the vanilla version when no profile is set.
- `psx_mod_netplay_rollback_supported` (L37) — Returns 1 unless the profile says rollback is not supported.
- `psx_mod_netplay_savestates_supported` (L40) — Returns 1 unless an active profile says savestates are not supported.
- `psx_mod_netplay_set_active` (L43) — Turns the netplay profile on or off; it only turns on when a profile is registered.
- `psx_mod_netplay_is_active` (L46) — Returns 1 while the netplay profile is active.
- `psx_mod_netplay_session_id` (L47) — Mixes the profile's compatibility id, aspect and settings into the session id with FNV-1a, so matching builds agree.
- `psx_mod_netplay_set_options_identity` (L59) — Stores the settings identity as 64 lowercase hex characters; returns 0 when the length or the profile does not match.
- `psx_mod_netplay_content_identity` (L77) — Extend the modern execution/content handshake with a canonical SHA-256 profile identity.
- `psx_mod_netplay_set_aspect` (L132) — Selects a fixed aspect index (0 to 2) the profile allows; returns 1 on success.
- `psx_mod_netplay_aspect` (L138) — Returns the current netplay aspect index.
- `psx_mod_netplay_has_state_digest` (L139) — Returns 1 when an active profile supplies a state digest.
- `psx_mod_netplay_state_digest` (L142) — Returns the profile's state digest, or 0 when none is available.
- `psx_mod_netplay_requires_texture_banks` (L145) — Returns 1 when the profile needs retained texture banks.
- `psx_mod_netplay_renderer_allowed` (L148) — Runtime renderer index: 0=software, 1=OpenGL, 2=Vulkan.

- `effective_resource_path` (L886) — Returns the file or folder a resource uses: the player's path, or the package default.

### runtime/src/mod_pad_transform.c

Pad transforms for mods: lets a mod rewrite a player's pad output each frame, with validation and neutral releases when a transform ends.

- `psx_mod_set_pad_transform` (L17) — Sets or clears the pad transform for a player port; clearing sends a neutral release if one was active. Returns 0 for a bad port.
- `mod_pad_transform_reset` (L44) — Clears every pad transform, sending neutral releases on ports that had one.
- `mod_pad_transform_initial_type` (L53) — Returns the pad type a transform starts with for a port, or -1 when no transform is active.
- `pass_through` (L58) — Copies the frame's buttons, pad type and sticks into the output unchanged.
- `neutral` (L66) — Fills the output with no buttons pressed and centred sticks, for the given pad type.
- `output_valid` (L74) — Checks a transform's output: correct size, a known pad type the port allows, and values in range.
- `mod_pad_transform_run` (L82) — Runs a port's pad transform on a frame and writes the result to out; returns 1 when a result is produced.

### runtime/src/mod_resident.cpp

Resident packs: builds, verifies, caches and serves a title's files and derived blobs from one pack per disc, with an event log.

- `records` (L83) — Returns the list of resident pack records kept in memory.
- `sha` (L88) — Returns the SHA-256 digest of a byte range.
- `hex` (L93) — Formats the first n bytes of a digest as lowercase hex.
- `put32` (L103) — Appends a 32-bit value to a byte buffer, little-endian.
- `put64` (L104) — Appends a 64-bit value to a byte buffer, little-endian.
- `get32` (L105) — Reads a little-endian 32-bit value from a byte pointer.
- `get64` (L108) — Reads a little-endian 64-bit value from a byte pointer.
- `valid_spec` (L110) — Checks a resident-pack spec: a title, a format made of safe characters, files, and a known policy.
- `cache_key` (L127) — Computes the cache key for a spec and fingerprint, hashing its title, format, files and settings.
- `cache_dir` (L149) — Returns the cache folder for a title's resident pack, from PSX_RESIDENT_CACHE or the local app data folder.
- `add_blob` (L163) — Adds bytes to the pack payload, reusing an identical blob already there, and returns its index.
- `index_lba` (L178) — Builds the index that finds files by disc sector, and counts the files that differ from the stock disc.
- `build` (L187) — Builds a resident pack from a spec by reading each listed file into blobs; returns null and sets error on failure.
- `table` (L224) — Serializes a pack's header and tables (magic, version, counts, key) into bytes.
- `publish` (L249) — Writes a pack to its final path through a temporary file, then moves it into place.
- `load` (L281) — Structure, key and every blob hash.
- `extents_match` (L329) — A cache from another disc with the same plan fingerprint cannot match the extents of every listed file on this one.
- `prune` (L339) — Removes older pack files of the same format from the cache folder, keeping the given one.
- `record_for` (L356) — Returns the record for a title and format, creating it when missing.
- `json_string` (L366) — Appends text to a string as a JSON string literal, escaping quotes, backslashes and control characters.
- `psx_resident_emit` (L378) — Adds a derived blob for a file to a pack being built, with its tag and metadata; returns 1 on success.
- `psx_resident_prepare` (L393) — Load (verified) or build the pack.
- `psx_resident_file_count` (L466) — Returns how many files a resident pack holds.
- `psx_resident_file` (L470) — Returns the bytes of a file in a resident pack, with its size and padded size; NULL when the index is bad.
- `psx_resident_file_lba` (L479) — Effective-disc LBA of the file's first sector (relocations by mods apply).
- `psx_resident_file_stock` (L483) — Returns 1 when a pack file is the stock disc copy, 0 when it was modified or the index is bad.
- `psx_resident_modified_files` (L487) — Returns how many pack files differ from the stock disc.
- `psx_resident_find_lba` (L491) — Finds the pack file that covers a disc sector range and returns its bytes, or NULL when none does.
- `psx_resident_derived_count` (L506) — Returns how many derived blobs a pack holds.
- `psx_resident_derived` (L510) — Returns a derived blob of a pack with its file, tag and metadata; NULL on a bad index.
- `psx_resident_guest_ranges_match` (L522) — Checks that guest memory ranges hash to the given SHA-256 text; returns 1 when they match.
- `psx_resident_status_json` (L542) — Debug server: JSON array describing every prepared pack.
- `psx_resident_record` (L583) — Logs a resident-pack event (operation, file, sector, size and whether it was served) into the event ring.
- `psx_resident_events_json` (L596) — Writes the recent resident-pack events within a frame range as JSON into out; returns the length.

### runtime/src/mod_texture_banks.c

Keeps the mod-side texture banks (pixel tables by id) and the GPU packet arena used to batch textured draws.

- `psx_mod_set_texture_bank_batching` (L18) — Default-off GL optimization: batch immutable-bank semi triangles in painter order on the single-pass dual-source path only.
- `mod_texture_bank_batchable` (L19) — 1 when texture-bank batching is on and the draw is immutable, unmasked, and has semi-transparency mode 0, 1 or 3.
- `psx_mod_set_texture_bank_resolver` (L24) — Installs the callback the mod calls to fill a bank id that has no pixels yet.
- `psx_mod_define_texture_bank` (L28) — Stores a w by h 16-bit pixel bank under id as a copy; returns 1 when stored or identical, 0 on bad input or the size limit.
- `mod_texture_bank_pixels` (L46) — Returns the bank's pixel pointer and sets w and h, calling the resolver once when the bank is empty; NULL when unknown.
- `psx_mod_alloc_texture_packet_memory` (L58) — A dedicated GPU-DMA packet arena.
- `mod_texture_packet_bank` (L69) — Reads the 9-word texture packet at source and returns the bank id it encodes, or 0 when it is not inside a known arena.
- `mod_texture_packet_precision` (L80) — Fills q and xy with high-precision vertex values from an HTP1 block in a packet arena; returns 0 when absent or invalid.

### runtime/src/nd_intro_ot.c

Remembers the ordering-table base addresses of the ND intro wood batches so sibling scenes can place their depth correctly.

- `looks_like_ot_base` (L10) — 1 when the address is word aligned and inside the gameplay RAM window where wood batch OTs sit.
- `psx_nd_note_wood_batch_ot` (L16) — Last WoodEmit batch OT base (model+228).
- `psx_nd_note_wood_batch_ot_tagged` (L22) — Records a wood batch OT base under its four-letter tag (CODE, GLOW or BOX_) and also as the general base.
- `psx_nd_wood_batch_ot` (L36) — Returns the wood batch OT base, preferring the CODE layer, then GLOW, then BOX_, else the last noted base.
- `psx_nd_note_sibling_ot_hint` (L47) — Sibling-scene bump hint at s4+0xb4 (captured at NdIntroSiblingRtptEmit).
- `psx_nd_sibling_ot_hint` (L53) — Returns the sibling-scene OT hint last captured, or 0 when none was noted.

### runtime/src/netplay_bios_settle.c

Chooses which BIOS image every netplay peer boots, and formats, parses and describes the retail BIOS checksums shown to players.

- `netplay_bios_settle` (L9) — Picks OpenBIOS or the retail BIOS for a match from each seat's offer; returns NONE with the conflicting seats when no common choice exists.
- `netplay_bios_token` (L69) — Wire token for a settled kind: "openbios", "scph1001" (retail), or "".
- `netplay_bios_format_crc` (L78) — retail_crc on the wire: eight lowercase hex digits, "" for 0.
- `netplay_bios_parse_crc` (L88) — Parses eight hex digits (surrounding spaces allowed).
- `netplay_bios_describe_crc` (L109) — Short player-facing name for a retail image CRC ("SCPH-5552"), or the CRC in hex ("BIOS d786f0b9") when the image is not in psx_bios_known_images.h.
- `netplay_bios_describe_refusal` (L122) — Writes the player-facing reason a match cannot start over the BIOS choice, naming the two conflicting dumps when known; empty otherwise.

### runtime/src/netplay_exit_reason.c

Turns netplay start failures, bind errors and boot mismatches into the sentences shown to the player.

- `netplay_exit_reason_text` (L29) — The player-facing sentence for a netplay_soft_exit origin, or NULL when the player ended the match themselves (window close, Escape) or the origin is unknown.
- `bind_error_kind` (L49) — Maps a system socket bind error code to in-use, not-allowed, no-such-address or other error kind.
- `sys_text_fits` (L62) — The system's own text goes into a sentence only when it is short and plain ASCII: a text in the system's language and code page is not shown as broken letters, and a long one is not cut in the middle.
- `netplay_start_failure_text` (L73) — Writes the player-facing sentence explaining why netplay failed to start, with the bind address, peer or system error when known.
- `netplay_boot_mismatch_final` (L163) — Returns 1 once a boot mismatch has lasted at least grace_ms since it began; 0 when none is active.

### runtime/src/netplay_ice_hub.c

Decides the netplay transport and maps lobby seats onto the ICE hub's session slots.

- `psx_transport_decide` (L6) — Chooses the netplay transport (ICE hub, SFU, direct or error) from the config and launch flags; the hub wins when it is set.
- `psx_ice_hub_map_error_text` (L27) — Short English text for a seat-mapping error code, or unknown.
- `fail` (L39) — Stores the error code in err_out when given and returns -1.
- `psx_ice_hub_map_seats` (L45) — Maps lobby seats to session slots through the port map; returns -1 on error with the reason in err_out.

### runtime/src/netplay_input_hist.c

Converts pad states to and from the rollback input frames that netplay keeps in its history.

- `u8_to_i8_stick` (L11) — Converts an unsigned analog stick byte (centre 128) to a signed value centred on zero, clamped to the int8 range.
- `i8_to_u8_stick` (L19) — Converts a signed stick value back to the unsigned byte form centred on 128.
- `netplay_ih_pad_to_frame` (L24) — Packs a pad state into a rollback input frame for the given tick, marked predicted or not; does nothing when out is null.
- `netplay_ih_frame_to_pad` (L48) — Unpacks a rollback frame into a pad state; a null or invalid frame gives a released, centred, digital pad.

### runtime/src/netplay_snap_ring.c

Keeps a ring of recent machine-state snapshots so netplay can roll back to an earlier tick and resume.

- `netplay_snap_audit_note` (L30) — PSX_RB_SNAP_AUDIT=<dir>: one line per ring save -- mode (L live, R replay), tick, and per boot_state section the CRC32 (+ hex for sections <= 4 KiB).
- `snap_mono_ms` (L83) — Monotonic clock in milliseconds, from the performance counter on Windows and the monotonic clock elsewhere.
- `netplay_snap_ring_save` (L98) — Saves the CPU and machine state into the ring under tick, tagged with the BIOS checksum and entry PC; reports the save time for telemetry.
- `netplay_snap_ring_load` (L140) — Restores the CPU and machine state saved for tick; returns 0 when no snapshot exists for that tick.

- `netplay_spu_regs_digest` (L211) — CRC of the SPU registers only, through the snapshot module.
- `spu_dig_regs_only` (L216) — Reads PSX_RB_SPU_DIG_REGS_ONLY once; 1 means the SPU digest skips SPU RAM.

- `netplay_mdec_digest` (L249) — CRC of the MDEC decoder snapshot.

- `netplay_spad_digest` (L264) — CRC of the 1 KiB scratchpad; 0 when the scratchpad pointer is unavailable.
- `netplay_dma_digest` (L273) — uint32_t netplay_aux_digest(void); /* crc(spu, mdec) uint32_t netplay_spad_digest(void); /* 1 KiB scratchpad
- `netplay_sio_digest` (L278) — CRC of the SIO controller and memory-card state, folded through the FSM pace field only.

- `netplay_baseline_ext_digest` (L344) — Baseline dig_c: crc(aux, cd, spad, dma, sio).

- `append_history_record` (L595) — Append the canonical JSON array as one minified JSONL record.

- `overlay_autocapture_get_status` (L1062) — Reports whether auto-capture is enabled, how many triggers fired and the last instruction delta.

### runtime/src/overlay_path_canon.c

### runtime/src/pgxp.cpp

Implements PGXP, which tracks precise sub-pixel positions of GTE vertices and memory words alongside their integer values.

- `recompute_active` (L144) — Single hot-path gate for every hook.
- `pgxp_invalidate_all` (L157) — Drop all shadows (savestate load, raw RAM restore, timeline breaks).
- `pgxp_set_enabled` (L177) — Master arm. Allocates the RAM shadow lazily; fails closed (stays disabled) if the allocation fails.
- `pgxp_enabled` (L200) — 1 when PGXP is armed for this session.
- `pgxp_active` (L201) — Armed and not inside a suppression bracket (speculative/replay pass): whether the hooks record anything right now.
- `pgxp_set_cpu_mode` (L203) — Tier-2 propagation through CPU arithmetic (default off, like the reference implementations' default).
- `pgxp_cpu_mode` (L204) — 1 when tier-2 propagation through CPU arithmetic is on.
- `pgxp_set_projection_tracking` (L206) — Turns projection tracking on or off; a change drops all shadows.
- `pgxp_projection_tracking` (L211) — 1 when projection tracking is on.
- `pgxp_set_tolerance` (L213) — Reject a precise position whose sub-pixel offset from the native integer position exceeds this many pixels.
- `pgxp_tolerance` (L214) — Current tolerance, in pixels, for accepting a precise position.
- `pgxp_set_position_fallback` (L216) — Position-cache fallback tier (docs/ENHANCEMENTS.md G1.4/G1.11).
- `pgxp_position_fallback` (L219) — 1 when the position-cache fallback is on.
- `pgxp_set_preserve_projection` (L221) — Preserve projection precision (docs/ENHANCEMENTS.md G1.11).

- `pgxp_set_culling` (L226) — Precise culling (docs/ENHANCEMENTS.md G1.12).

### runtime/src/pgxp_session.cpp

Sets the PGXP session switches from the environment and the mod plan, and turns the memory and ALU settings into hook masks.

- `psx_pgxp_session_reset` (L15) — Session start, before plugin activation: forget any mod request.

- `psx_pgxp_load_masked` (L37) — The overlay DLLs' load/store hooks (overlay_loader.c hook table): the same mask as the generated code's PGXP_LOAD / PGXP_STORE.
- `psx_pgxp_store_masked` (L40) — Store hook for overlay DLLs: calls the PGXP store path only when the memory mask allows this instruction.
- `pgxp_mem_skip_from` (L46) — Turns the memory setting (all, words, live or a number) into the memory skip mask; the default depends on mem_words.
- `pgxp_alu_mask_from` (L56) — Turns the ALU setting (full, moves or a number) into the ALU hook mask, defaulting to moves when alu_light is set.
- `psx_pgxp_session_arm` (L65) — Arms PGXP for the session from the config, environment and plan inputs; returns the arm state and the inputs used.

### runtime/src/playtest_diagnostics.cpp

Records and replays controller input and state digests at each VBlank for playtest diagnostics, with an optional input overlay and telemetry.

- `build_identity` (L82) — Identity string for this build: the build id plus the SHA-256 of the executable, computed once.
- `application_directory` (L98) — Folder where the engine keeps settings, mods and saves, or the diagnostic default when none is known.
- `recording_location` (L106) — Writes the recording path to diagnostics-location.txt in the application folder; errors are ignored.
- `report_stats` (L116) — Prints the VBlank timing statistics to stderr when a session ends.
- `close_recording` (L127) — Closes the recording and telemetry files and reports the stats; also registered to run at exit.
- `plan_identity` (L143) — Plan fingerprint that ties a replay to its plan, in portable form when available.
- `state_digest` (L148) — FNV-style digest of a fixed sample of main RAM words, chosen by the sequence number.
- `sample` (L160) — The pad state the game reads for the frame this VBlank starts.
- `parse_row` (L175) — Parses one recorded row line (starting with N) into columns; false when the line is not a row or has too few columns.
- `source` (L199) — Supplies the recorded pad state for one seat during replay; neutral until the first row is loaded.
- `first_source` (L209) — Supplies the recorded pad state for seat 1 during replay.
- `second_source` (L210) — Supplies the recorded pad state for seat 2 during replay.
- `release_sources` (L211) — Unhooks the replay controller sources when this session owns them.
- `fail` (L217) — Stops a replay with a reason: logs the sequence, counts the failure and releases the replay sources.
- `next_row` (L227) — Load the next recorded row.
- `begin_replay` (L240) — Opens the replay file, checks its header and starts feeding the recorded input; refused during netplay.
- `seed_first_row` (L277) — A restore happens mid-frame, so a recorded segment's first row holds whatever the live host sampled between the restore and the first VBlank.
- `session_json` (L288) — Builds the session description JSON (format, game, digest and boundary) and notes whether netplay is on.
- `begin_recording` (L304) — Starts recording the session and registers the close function to run at exit.
- `capture_telemetry` (L383) — Adds one telemetry row for this VBlank with its input and timing, when telemetry is open.
- `completed_slot_load` (L431) — Parse savestate_status_json: did a slot-file load just complete?
- `read_slot` (L441) — Reads a savestate slot into memory and returns its bytes; empty on failure.
- `restored` (L452) — A state restore starts a new baseline segment, as a manual jump cannot be reconciled with earlier rows.
- `input_line` (L480) — Formats one seat's held buttons as a short text line, such as P1 X O, or a dash when none are held.
- `tick_osd` (L495) — Refreshes the on-screen input display for the current frame; cleared while netplay or the overlay is off.
- `column_name` (L508) — Name of one recorded column, used in divergence messages.
- `verify` (L515) — Compares the replayed row with the live row and reports the first column that differs.
- `tick` (L530) — Runs at each guest VBlank, before the VBlank IRQ is delivered to the game.
- `reset_session` (L575) — Closes the files, releases the sources and clears all session state back to its defaults.
- `activate` (L589) — Reads the diagnostic environment settings (input-only route, legacy connected seats) and enables the tool when debug tools are built in.
- `activate_osd` (L642) — Turns the input overlay on and resets its sequence counter.

### runtime/src/present_phase.c

Keeps the presentation phase in step with the display refresh by timing vblanks and holding each swap to the right moment.

- `qpc` (L40) — Current performance counter value.
- `grid_write` (L55) — Publishes the refresh grid (anchor, last vblank and period) for other threads, guarded by a sequence counter.
- `grid_read` (L64) — Reads a consistent copy of the refresh grid into g, retrying while a write is in progress.
- `cmp_i64` (L78) — Comparator for sorting 64-bit integers.
- `cmp_dbl` (L82) — Comparator for sorting doubles.
- `vb_note` (L94) — Records one vblank time and recomputes the refresh period and phase from the recent vblanks.
- `vblank_thread` (L123) — Thread that waits for the display's vblank signal and records each vblank time.
- `start_once` (L191) — Starts the phase tracking once: reads the timer frequency and the GPU time setting, then starts the vblank thread.
- `wait_until` (L217) — Waits until the performance counter reaches t, sleeping for the bulk of the wait and spinning for the last few microseconds.
- `present_phase_hold` (L236) — Composing thread, right before a real (not generated) swap.
- `present_phase_note_done` (L299) — Measurement (PSX_PRESENT_PHASE_PROBE=1, the renderer waits for the GPU after each real swap): the swap's and the GPU's end, in performance-counter ticks.
- `present_phase_correction` (L318) — Emulation thread, before each paced wait: ticks to add to the pacer's next deadline (phase lock), 0 while inactive.
- `present_phase_active` (L334) — 1 while the hold is engaged (the last present went through it).
- `present_phase_json` (L340) — JSON object body for the debug server (no braces).

### runtime/src/present_thread.c

Runs presentation on its own thread so the emulation thread can hand off finished frames without waiting for the display.

- `mtx_init` (L16) — Initialises a mutex (an SRW lock on Windows).
- `mtx_lock` (L17) — Locks the mutex.
- `mtx_unlock` (L18) — Unlocks the mutex.

### runtime/src/psx_net_pad.c

Normalizes netplay pad state so every consumer sees the same values, with a centre deadzone on analog axes.

### runtime/src/psx_netplay_rb.c

Rollback netplay engine: seals and replays episodes, manages snapshots, tip holds, realigns and FMV handling.

- `psx_netplay_rb_bind` (L6) — Binds the rollback engine to its CPU, session and host callbacks; a no-op in builds without recomp-net.
- `psx_netplay_rb_start` (L7) — Starts the rollback engine; a no-op in builds without recomp-net.
- `psx_netplay_rb_shutdown` (L8) — Shuts down the rollback engine; a no-op in builds without recomp-net.
- `psx_netplay_rb_cold_reset` (L9) — Soft-return / rematch: wipe RB host residue that rb_shutdown leaves (follow-NACK, tip-dense FIFO, episode wire, dig0 latch).
- `psx_netplay_rb_poll` (L10) — Safe BB-edge poll (mirror savestate_poll).
- `psx_netplay_rb_flush_resume` (L15) — If a baseline snap was applied without resume, longjmp to the scheduler (same as savestate_poll).
- `psx_netplay_rb_top_level_resume_active` (L16) — 1 after flush_resume longjmp until finish_frame / abort — top-level dispatch has no native call chain under the resume PC.
- `psx_netplay_rb_recover_null_pc` (L17) — After outermost psx_dispatch returns pc==0 following an RB resume: retry at $ra / sticky BB if safe.
- `psx_netplay_rb_request_snap` (L23) — After a live tick completes: request snap at tick for next safe poll.
- `psx_netplay_rb_begin_rewind` (L24) — Initiator: start episode from invent/contract rewind.
- `psx_netplay_rb_tip_extend` (L30) — Active episode: grow target / resign sealed rows for a late wire edge (press+release coalesce).
- `psx_netplay_rb_rewind_suppressed` (L36) — 1 while begin_rewind is suppressed (cooldown after abort / realign).
- `psx_netplay_rb_fmv_defer_rewind` (L37) — 1 during depth24 / recent MDEC / short post-FMV settle — MotK FMV.
- `psx_netplay_rb_fmv_media_active` (L38) — 1 while depth24 or recent MDEC (not settle).

- `psx_netplay_rb_fmv_settle_active` (L40) — 1 while sim is still inside the short post-FMV settle tail (before MIN).

- `clear_tip_extend_prime` (L5246) — Clears the tip-extend prime tick.
- `tip_hold_peek_buttons` (L5252) — Peek pad buttons from the delay ring at sim-keyed 'tick' (0xFFFF if missing).
- `tip_hold_held_split` (L5281) — TipHold SAFETY/quiet "held" split (§36/§37): - Local: live physical pad (sim/staged stay frozen under invent-cap).
- `tip_hold_wire_pending_release` (L5318) — 1 if wire tip+1..tip+runway has an unabsorbed RELEASE vs tip for a remote seat.
- `ownership_chain_next_span` (L5365) — §47/§48: after chunk/final Verify POST match — stay in Replay ownership while contiguous confirmed work remains; otherwise Final Verify → Live.
- `ownership_on_post_match` (L5491) — Handles a matching post digest at the tip and decides whether ownership moves on, using the frontier and min-ahead rules.
- `enter_tip_hold` (L5680) — Enters tip hold at the target tick, sizing the runway from the session settings.
- `clear_tip_hold_rereplay_pending` (L5779) — Clears the deferred tip-hold rereplay request and its starting tick.
- `tip_hold_absorb_frontier_before_flush` (L5791) — §66: flush batched TipHold tip-extend rereplay.
- `flush_tip_hold_deferred_rereplay` (L5846) — Sends the deferred tip-hold rereplay once it is due; returns 1 when a rereplay was flushed.
- `tip_hold_try_finalize` (L5944) — TipHold commit wall: repair deferred invent first, then commit.
- `finalize_tip_hold` (L5951) — Finishes a tip hold that is still holding: picks the target tick and commits the hold.
- `poll_tip_hold_finalize` (L6025) — Polls each pump whether a tip hold can be finalized, using the session stats to decide.
- `tip_extend_keep_live` (L6249) — §75: CPU still holds the sealed fin state at 'prefer' — refresh the ring from live and arm prefer+1 without reloading a possibly invent-poisoned snap.
- `schedule_episode_rereplay` (L6306) — prefer_plus_one: pass prior_tip+1 so prefer==prior tip (initiator and FOLLOW must agree).
- `commit_episode` (L6382) — Commits the finished episode at its target tick and returns the engine to live play.
- `rb_fmv_dense_snap_window` (L6727) — Dense tip snaps: settle + digest lockstep/+tip (§26) — first Cross/Start after FMV still wants a near-tip load.
- `try_apply_pending_load` (L6813) — Apply pending baseline/realign snap without longjmp.
- `psx_netplay_rb_post_fmv_heal_sticky` (L7420) — §111: 1 while heal sticky window is live (invent hold may be tip-lead only).
- `stash_peer_begin` (L8344) — Stashes a peer's BEGIN message for an episode not open yet; a BEGIN for the episode already running is skipped.
- `apply_stashed_begin` (L8373) — Applies a stashed BEGIN message once the engine can accept it.
- `maybe_rexmit_begin` (L8404) — §60: BEGIN was fire-and-forget; on TURN a single drop left the follower parked on "wait FOLLOW" while the initiator sat in rb_baseline forever.
- `begin_follower` (L8442) — Starts an episode as a follower from the peer's BEGIN, setting its epoch, mismatch, load, target and slot.
- `rb_post_fmv_platform_kf_stream_poll` (L9044) — §114/§115: initiator re-opens apply-only MEDIA_KF while platform nondet is armed and cores still disagree.
- `boot_dig0_rexmit_local` (L9766) — Retransmits the local boot digest (dig0) to the peer while the boot digest check is pending.

### runtime/src/psx_netplay_sched.c

Glue that binds MotK's FMV, dig0 and round-trip gates to the recomp-net netplay pacing scheduler and keeps the np_sched_* call surface.

- `np_sched_bind` (L11) — Binds the scheduler to a session bridge (session, input delay and prediction, local slot, turn flag) and its gate callbacks; NULL unbinds.
- `np_sched_reset_session` (L12) — Clear session-scoped pacing/invent state (cushion rebuild, pcap freeze, timesync debt, tip cadence).
- `np_sched_wire_for_sim` (L13) — sim→wire CONSUMPTION mapping.
- `np_sched_real_delay_enabled` (L14) — Returns 1 when real input-delay pacing is enabled; delegates to recomp-net.
- `np_sched_sync_delay_from_session` (L15) — Mid-session DELAY_SYNC commit → mirror into *input_delay.
- `np_sched_pre_admit` (L16) — Pre-admit gate, in original np_try_admit_rollback order: tip cadence tracking, timesync throttle (live only), lead sampling, runway/phase logs, cushion-rebuild clearing, auto-delay resolution.
- `np_sched_on_remote_miss` (L21) — Called when a remote input row is missing at the consumption wire; forwards to recomp-net, returns its verdict and a reason string in reason_out.
- `np_sched_note_remote_hit` (L29) — Remote row present at the consumption wire (gap1 grace paid off).
- `np_sched_post_admit` (L30) — End of a successful admit: leave pcap freeze, flush periodic stats.
- `np_sched_set_admit_stall` (L31) — MotK-side admit stall tag for barrier logs.
- `np_sched_clear_admit_stall` (L32) — Clears the admit-stall tag set for barrier logs.
- `np_sched_admit_stall_tag` (L33) — Returns the current admit-stall tag string, used in barrier logs.
- `np_sched_note_mispredict` (L34) — Reconcile caught a genuine mispredict (published != wire) that rode 'age' ticks before being caught — feeds the pacing debt of the ahead peer.
- `np_sched_note_episode_boundary` (L35) — Episode boundary (commit/abort): clear the pegged-streak off-guard and arm cushion rebuild.
- `psx_netplay_timesync_on_episode_boundary` (L36) — Clear timesync pegged-streak at episode/tip-hold boundaries so resim cost cannot look like WAN transit and trip adaptive-off (see §22).
- `np_sched_arm_absurd_invent_catchup` (L37) — §83 C: after baseline-abort Live realign, allow invent despite absurd remote_lead for a short window so recovery can catch up (soak: lead=500 refuse invent → crawl).
- `np_gate_now_ms` (L49) — Gate callback returning the monotonic clock in milliseconds.
- `np_gate_rtt_ms` (L55) — Gate callback returning the netplay round-trip estimate in milliseconds.
- `np_gate_episode_active` (L61) — Gate callback: 1 while a rollback episode is active.
- `np_gate_tip_holding` (L67) — Gate callback: 1 while the netplay tip is held.
- `np_gate_lockstep_no_invent` (L73) — Gate callback: 1 when lockstep forbids inventing input rows.
- `np_gate_media_active` (L79) — Gate callback: 1 while FMV media is playing.
- `np_gate_desync_hold` (L85) — Gate callback: 1 while the FMV desync hold is active.
- `np_gate_lockstep_stall_tag` (L91) — Gate callback naming why lockstep is stalled: fmv_media, fmv_desync_hold, heal_sticky, fmv_settle or fmv_lockstep.
- `np_gate_episode_count` (L106) — Gate callback returning the rollback episode count.
- `np_gate_replay_ticks_total` (L112) — Gate callback returning the total number of replayed ticks so far.
- `np_gate_pre_admit_hold` (L119) — MotK rematch dig0 CRC gate — host-specific; kept out of portable sched.

### runtime/src/psx_openxr.c

Opt-in Win32 OpenXR lifecycle: headset session, controller and hand input, render views and overlay surfaces.

- `hands_clear` (L28) — Resets the located-hands state and stamps a new sequence number with no age.
- `valid_pose_numbers` (L37) — 1 when a pose quaternion is finite with norm between 0.5 and 1.5 and its position is finite within 100 m.
- `psx_openxr_hands_override` (L43) — Injects synthetic hand poses for tracking; NULL clears the override; returns 0 when the values are refused.
- `psx_openxr_input_override` (L65) — Injects a synthetic controller sample (sticks, triggers, buttons); NULL clears it; returns 0 when values are out of range.
- `psx_openxr_input_snapshot` (L80) — Copies the last sampled controller input into out.
- `psx_openxr_pair_metadata` (L81) — Tags the next frame as a paired guest frame with an id and cycle, clearing the native frame number.
- `psx_openxr_native_metadata` (L82) — Tags the next frame as native with a frame number, clearing any pair id and cycle.
- `psx_openxr_surface_valid` (L83) — 1 when an overlay surface has a valid id, size up to 1024 px, known flags, and sane position, orientation and size.
- `check` (L131) — Records an OpenXR call result in the stats and returns 1 on success; a lost session or instance flags a reset.
- `input_initialize` (L142) — Creates the gameplay action set with stick, trigger, squeeze, button and pose actions for both hands, bound to the Touch controller profile.
- `initialize` (L207) — Checks for the OpenGL extension, creates the OpenXR instance and head-mounted system, then waits for a session.
- `events` (L278) — Polls runtime events, begins or ends the session on state changes, and flags a reset or exit on loss.
- `sync_actions` (L314) — Sync the gameplay action set.
- `hands_locate` (L322) — Focus for hands comes from the session state events and a successful action sync in this call, never from whether the plugin polled psx_mod_openxr_input.
- `xr_destroy` (L354) — Destroy every XR object (children before parents).
- `service_loss` (L378) — Act on a flagged loss.
- `psx_openxr_hands` (L395) — Copies current hand tracking into out with its age in ms, or the injected hands while overridden.
- `psx_openxr_interp_gate` (L408) — Pure gate: presentation-side frame interpolation must be OFF while a headset session is running (the compositor reprojects).
- `psx_openxr_session_active` (L411) — 1 when OpenXR is compiled in, enabled, initialized and running.
- `psx_openxr_stats` (L414) — Copies the current OpenXR stats (state, stage, failures, versions) into out.
- `psx_openxr_recenter` (L421) — Clears the hand state and drops the origin so the next pose re-anchors.
- `psx_openxr_shutdown` (L427) — int psx_openxr_session_active(void); /* gate applied to the live state
- `psx_openxr_enable` (L442) — Shuts down and resets stats, then requests OpenXR on or off; returns 0 when enabling a build without OpenXR.
- `psx_openxr_view` (L450) — Copies the render view for eye 0 or 1 into out while a frame is open and tracking; returns 0 otherwise.
- `psx_openxr_input` (L456) — Fills out with a fresh controller sample (the injected one when set); returns 0 only if struct_size is wrong.
- `psx_openxr_begin` (L515) — Opens a frame when OpenXR is enabled and none is open; syncs actions and locates the views when focused.
- `psx_openxr_quad` (L596) — Makes the frame a flat quad at distance metres with width and height; distance 0 turns it off; returns 0 when out of range.
- `psx_openxr_end` (L611) — Closes the open frame, submitting the copied eye images as projection layers when keep and copy are given and tracking is live.
- `psx_openxr_surface` (L680) — Uploads a valid RGBA overlay surface (id 0 or 1, up to 1024 px) for the open frame, copying its pixels; returns 1 on success.
- `psx_openxr_surface_get` (L693) — Copies the uploaded overlay surface with the given id into out while a frame is open; returns 0 otherwise.

### runtime/src/psx_pad_apply.c

The single path that applies a resolved netplay pad to the SIO controller port.

- `psx_pad_apply_to_sio` (L5) — The one way a resolved pad reaches SIO, shared by offline sampling, netplay (delay and rollback apply) and selfcheck replay: buttons, the type's axes (NeGcon unpacked to twist + I/II/L), and a deferre

### runtime/src/psx_ram_geometry.c

Holds the live main-RAM size: retail 2 MiB by default, with an opt-in 8 MiB expansion applied once per boot.

- `memory_get_ram_bytes` (L23) — Returns the current main RAM size in bytes (2 MiB retail, or 8 MiB when expanded).
- `psx_ram_8mb_active` (L24) — 1 when main RAM is currently expanded beyond the retail 2 MiB.
- `psx_ram_reset_size_request` (L28) — Clears the 8 MiB request so the next boot falls back to retail RAM.
- `psx_mod_set_main_ram_8mb` (L32) — Opt into expanded 8 MiB main RAM for this launch.
- `psx_ram_apply_size_request` (L37) — memory_init(): latch the requested geometry for this boot.

### runtime/src/psx_rewind.c

Rewind feature: a ring of recent machine snapshots with thumbnails, plus the on-screen filmstrip panel for stepping back in time.

- `psx_rewind_title_blocked` (L107) — 1 while the running title has blocked rewind, so no history is captured and Rewind will not open.
- `psx_rewind_set_title_blocked` (L114) — Title block (mod API psx_mod_set_rewind_blocked): while set, Rewind refuses to open and captures no history (the ring keeps what it has).
- `psx_rewind_snap_count` (L115) — Snapshots in the ring (debug/status).
- `psx_rewind_set_depth` (L116) — Snap count kept in the local rewind ring.
- `psx_rewind_set_interval` (L117) — Sets the preferred capture interval in frames, snapped to the nearest offered value (1, 4, 8, 12 or 15).
- `psx_rewind_set_enabled` (L118) — Settings/launcher preference.
- `psx_rewind_configure` (L119) — Builds the snapshot ring and thumbnail and tick buffers for this BIOS and entry point when rewind is wanted; disables it on allocation failure.
- `psx_rewind_shutdown` (L124) — Frees the ring and buffers and resets the panel, slide and any pending load or capture.
- `psx_rewind_discard_history` (L125) — A different mounted disc invalidates every earlier rewind snapshot.
- `psx_rewind_enabled` (L126) — 1 when rewind is wanted and configured with a live snapshot ring.
- `psx_rewind_is_open` (L127) — 1 while the rewind panel is open.
- `psx_rewind_needs_present` (L128) — 1 while open or slide animation still visible.
- `psx_rewind_note_frame` (L129) — Guest vblank: bump frame counter / schedule capture when not paused.
- `psx_rewind_poll` (L130) — Safe BB-edge (beside savestate_poll): capture due snap / apply load.
- `psx_rewind_toggle` (L135) — Opens or closes the panel; refuses with an on-screen message when rewind is off, in netplay or title-blocked; returns 1 when the state changed.
- `psx_rewind_cancel` (L136) — Closes the open panel without loading anything; returns 1 if it was open.
- `psx_rewind_accept` (L137) — Schedules a load of the selected snapshot for the next poll and closes the panel; returns 0 when nothing is selected.
- `psx_rewind_move` (L138) — Moves the panel selection by delta, clamped to the stored snapshots.
- `psx_rewind_nav_held` (L139) — Turns held left/right, accept and cancel input into edges, moving the selection with key repeat while open.
- `psx_rewind_present_tick` (L145) — Advances the panel slide animation toward open or closed using now_ms.
- `psx_rewind_overlay_image` (L146) — Bottom-panel ARGB8888 (little-endian).
- `psx_rewind_slide` (L153) — 0..1 slide (0 = off-screen below, 1 = docked).
- `env_u32` (L196) — Reads a non-negative integer from an environment variable, clamped to lo..hi, or returns def when unset.
- `normalize_rewind_depth` (L211) — UI offers 50/100/150/200; nearest match keeps hand-edited toml values sane.
- `normalize_rewind_interval` (L228) — UI offers 1/4/8/12/15.
- `rewind_wanted` (L272) — Resolves on/off, capture interval, FMV interval and depth once from environment variables and preferences; returns whether rewind is enabled.
- `rewind_fmv_media_active` (L307) — Same heuristic as netplay rb_fmv_media_active — denser snaps while media runs.
- `rewind_capture_interval` (L318) — Returns the capture interval in frames, denser while FMV media is running.
- `resume_pc_ok` (L326) — 1 when a PC is word-aligned, dispatchable and not an exception or reset vector.
- `rewind_resolve_resume_pc` (L334) — Mid-FMV / present-edge IRQ paths often pass hint=0 — same latch walk as savestate_resolve_resume_pc / selfcheck sc_pick_snap_pc.
- `capture_thumb` (L356) — Fills a 128 by 96 thumbnail from the current display, black when the display is off.
- `list_drop_after` (L377) — Removes list entries newer than tick and keeps the selection in range.
- `list_push` (L395) — Adds a tick and its thumbnail to the list, replacing the same tick or dropping the oldest when full.
- `do_capture` (L513) — Saves a machine snapshot at a safe resume point into the ring, with its thumbnail; returns 1 on success.
- `do_load` (L543) — Restores the snapshot at tick, drops newer snapshots, resyncs timing and resumes; returns 0 on failure.
- `blit_thumb` (L749) — Draws a thumbnail scaled into a panel cell, with a border highlighted when selected.
- `glyph_fill_rect` (L782) — Fills a clipped rectangle in the panel buffer with a colour.
- `glyph_fill_disc` (L796) — Fills a clipped solid disc of radius r in the panel buffer.
- `glyph_line` (L809) — Draws a thick line into the panel buffer by stepping pixels from one end to the other.
- `draw_psx_button` (L838) — Draws a PSX pad button glyph (x, o or square) at a position on the panel.
- `draw_char` (L856) — Draws one 8 by 8 font glyph into the panel buffer, clipped to its bounds.
- `draw_text` (L880) — Draws a string in the panel font, uppercased, advancing 8 pixels per character.
- `rasterize_panel` (L895) — Redraws the whole filmstrip panel: title, counter, snapshot cards, selection and key hints.

### runtime/src/psx_savestate_menu.c

Full-screen save-state slot browser drawn into a software panel, with optional title canvases, HUD and toast notices.

- `fill_rect` (L90) — Fills a clipped rectangle of the menu panel with a colour.
- `stroke_rect` (L103) — Draws a one-pixel outline rectangle on the menu panel.
- `fill_disc` (L111) — Fills a clipped solid disc of radius r on the menu panel.
- `draw_line` (L123) — Draws a thick line into a buffer by stepping pixels from one end to the other.
- `draw_psx_button` (L151) — Draws a PSX pad button glyph (x, square or circle) at a position on the menu panel.
- `draw_char` (L173) — Draws one 8 by 8 font glyph at a scale factor, uppercased, with '?' for unknown characters.
- `draw_text` (L196) — Draws a string at a scale factor, advancing 8 times the scale per character.
- `psx_ui_text` (L206) — Draws text into any ARGB buffer with the menu font and scale; returns the x position after the text.
- `blit_thumb` (L229) — Scales a save thumbnail into a rectangle of the panel, forcing it opaque.
- `format_slot_status` (L243) — Writes a slot's status line: NEW SLOT when empty, otherwise the save's date and time.
- `refresh_thumbs` (L262) — Reloads every slot's thumbnail from its save file.
- `rasterize_panel` (L272) — Redraws the whole slot browser panel: header, slot cards, selection and key hints.
- `psx_savestate_menu_set_state` (L341) — Sets whether the menu is open and which slot is selected (clamped), marking it for redraw when changed.
- `psx_savestate_menu_note_slots_changed` (L351) — Marks the menu for redraw after the save slots changed.
- `psx_savestate_menu_needs_present` (L356) — 1 while the menu, page or a notice is visible, so the frame must be presented.
- `psx_savestate_menu_set_renderer` (L361) — Sets the renderer that paints the selected slot's title canvas and marks the menu for redraw.
- `all_dirty` (L367) — Marks the menu, page, HUD and notices for redraw.
- `psx_savestate_menu_set_window` (L375) — The window's size, for the canvas' aspect (redrawn when it changes).
- `psx_savestate_menu_set_scale` (L383) — Every title canvas (this menu's, the page's, the HUD's, the notices') is 240 x scale lines and 320..1024 x scale columns (1 or 2; 1 by default): a title drawing the PSX picture's pixels as scale x sca
- `psx_savestate_menu_scale` (L392) — Returns the canvas scale factor (1 or 2).
- `psx_savestate_menu_set_page` (L397) — Sets the title's full-screen page drawn behind the menu; marks the menu and HUD for redraw.
- `psx_savestate_menu_page_redraw` (L405) — Asks for the title page to be drawn again at the next present.
- `psx_savestate_menu_set_hud` (L410) — Sets the title's HUD renderer; clearing it turns the HUD off.
- `psx_savestate_menu_hud_redraw` (L417) — Asks for the HUD to be drawn again at the next present.
- `psx_savestate_menu_set_toast` (L422) — A title's notices over all of it (psx_mod_set_title_toast): blended over the menu's or page's canvas or the HUD, or shown alone; a renderer that returns 2 is drawn again at the next present.
- `psx_savestate_menu_toast_redraw` (L429) — Asks for the notices to be drawn again at the next present.
- `psx_savestate_menu_overlay_blend` (L434) — The current image has transparency (a title's canvas): blend it.
- `canvas_height` (L440) — Canvas height in pixels: 240 lines times the scale.
- `canvas_width` (L445) — Canvas width in pixels matching the window aspect, clamped between 320 and the maximum times the scale.
- `canvas_buffer` (L453) — Allocates the canvas buffer on first use at maximum size and returns it.
- `render_canvas` (L462) — The title's canvas, when it has a renderer and draws this time.
- `title_canvas` (L472) — Draws the title's canvas with its renderer into the buffer; returns 1 when it drew.
- `give` (L482) — Returns an image pointer and its size through the out parameters; reports whether pixels exist.
- `base_image` (L491) — The menu's, page's or HUD's image, without the notices.
- `toast_update` (L529) — The notices' canvas, drawn when asked or while moving (renderer 2).
- `blend_over` (L546) — Straight-alpha "over": the notices on top of the canvas under them.
- `psx_savestate_menu_overlay_image` (L566) — Returns the final overlay image: the base image, with the notices blended on top when they are shown.

### runtime/src/psx_sdl_audio.cpp

SDL audio glue for the runtime: opens the playback stream, feeds it through a callback, and exposes queue controls.

- `psx_sdl3_audio_feed` (L12) — SDL stream callback: pulls audio from the runtime callback in chunks of up to 16 KiB until the requested amount is filled.
- `psx_sdl_audio_open` (L24) — Opens the default playback stream in the wanted format and reports the stream spec in have; returns the device id, or 0 on failure.
- `psx_sdl_audio_resume` (L63) — Resumes the playback stream; returns 0 on success, -1 otherwise.
- `psx_sdl_audio_set_paused` (L70) — Host pause (host_overlay.h P1): stop/start the device without dropping queued samples.
- `psx_sdl_audio_close` (L77) — Destroys the playback stream and clears its callback.
- `psx_sdl_audio_clear` (L85) — Drops all audio queued in the stream.
- `psx_sdl_audio_queued_size` (L90) — Returns the number of bytes queued in the stream.
- `psx_sdl_audio_queue` (L97) — Appends bytes to the stream; returns 0 on success, -1 otherwise.
- `psx_sdl_audio_lock` (L106) — Locks the audio stream so the audio thread cannot run while the caller changes shared state.
- `psx_sdl_audio_unlock` (L111) — Releases the lock taken by psx_sdl_audio_lock.

### runtime/src/psx_segment_miss.c

Records accesses to code at a segment alias that has no compiled row, in a ring log with unique-address counts.

- `psx_segment_miss_home` (L28) — The other segment's PC with a compiled row at addr's physical word, or 0 when there is none (addr itself is not consulted).
- `psx_segment_miss_record` (L40) — Records a game-code segment miss with its home, return address, stack pointer and frame.
- `psx_segment_miss_record_kind` (L46) — Stores a miss entry of the given kind (game or BIOS) in the ring log and counts it as a unique address.
- `psx_segment_miss_note` (L79) — If addr is not a valid entry, finds its alias home and records the miss; returns the home, or 0 when none.
- `psx_segment_miss_total` (L89) — Returns the total number of misses recorded.
- `psx_segment_miss_unique` (L90) — Returns how many distinct missing addresses have been seen.
- `psx_segment_miss_get` (L92) — The i-th recorded entry, i < total; only the last RING_CAP are kept.
- `psx_segment_miss_kind_name` (L97) — "game" or "bios", for reports.
- `psx_segment_miss_summary` (L102) — Fills up to max rows of misses sorted by count then address; returns how many rows were written.
- `psx_segment_miss_reset` (L134) — Clears the ring log, the unique table and the counters.

### runtime/src/psx_selfcheck.c

Solo rollback self-check: records a window of pad input, rewinds to a snapshot, replays it and compares state digests to catch non-determinism.

- `sc_free_blob` (L146) — Frees the saved snapshot blob and clears its length.
- `sc_schedule_next` (L153) — Sets the next self-check window to the current boundary plus the interval.
- `sc_freeze_overlays` (L158) — Freezes or unfreezes the overlay loader so areas do not load during a window.
- `sc_cancel` (L163) — Aborts the current window with a logged reason, freeing the snapshot and clearing the overlay freeze and load state.
- `sc_capture_digests` (L176) — Computes the core, audio/video and auxiliary state digests at the boundary, with the PC cleared first.
- `sc_raw_pc` (L191) — Returns the CPU's current PC, or 0 when there is no CPU.
- `sc_arm_span_end_load` (L198) — Arm span-end load: prefer flush_load after present-body RAII so every rewind happens at the same VBlank boundary (no post-span BB walk).
- `sc_apply_rows` (L205) — Applies each present recorded row's buttons and analog axes to its pad slot.
- `sc_diff_parts` (L222) — Append the name of each differing partition to buf.
- `sc_env_u32` (L254) — Reads an unsigned integer from an environment variable, clamped to lo..hi, or returns def when unset.
- `sc_mash_rng_next` (L291) — xorshift32 random generator for the button-mash mode; the state never becomes zero.
- `sc_mash_advance` (L302) — Returns the mash button word for this boundary, holding an open chord or sitting idle by a random rate.
- `psx_selfcheck_mash_override` (L330) — 1 when mash owns this boundary's P1 pad word (active-low).
- `psx_selfcheck_init` (L348) — Turns the self-check on when PSX_RB_SELFCHECK is set, provided the HLE scheduler is enabled for rewind.
- `psx_selfcheck_enabled` (L397) — 1 when the self-check is in any phase other than off.
- `psx_selfcheck_defer_present` (L398) — 1 while a window is open (record/replay/load).

### runtime/src/render_thread.c

Render thread core: a single-producer ring that hands draw records from the emulation thread to a render thread that owns the GL context.

- `mtx_init` (L24) — Initializes the render thread's lock.
- `mtx_lock` (L25) — Takes the render thread's lock.
- `mtx_unlock` (L26) — Releases the render thread's lock.
- `cnd_init` (L27) — Initializes a condition variable.
- `cnd_wait` (L28) — Waits on a condition variable with the lock held, with no timeout.
- `cnd_wait_ns` (L29) — Waits on a condition variable for at most the given nanoseconds, and at least 1 ms.
- `cnd_bcast` (L33) — Wakes every thread waiting on the condition variable.
- `now_ns` (L34) — Returns a monotonic clock reading in nanoseconds.
- `cpu_relax` (L40) — Hints to the CPU that the thread is spinning.
- `rt_running` (L155) — 1 while the render thread is running.
- `rt_on_render_thread` (L156) — 1 when called from the render thread.
- `rt_held` (L157) — 1 when the emulation thread holds the GL context.
- `rt_render_idle_ns` (L158) — Render-thread query: the consumer's running idle total (waiting for records, or parked while the emulation thread holds the context).
- `rt_now_ns` (L159) — Monotonic nanoseconds (the clock tick deadlines use).
- `rt_backpressure_events` (L160) — Any thread: running count of times the emulation thread blocked on the in-flight bound or a full ring (it waited on the render thread).
- `rt_tick_at` (L161) — Render thread, from tick or exec: ask for tick at 'deadline_ns' (earliest wins over the one tick last returned).
- `run_tick` (L167) — Consumer: run tick when its deadline has passed.
- `align_up` (L177) — Rounds n up to the ring's record alignment.
- `wake_emu` (L183) — Wakes the emulation thread if it is sleeping for ring space or a drain.
- `serve_release_locked` (L193) — Called with mtx held when the ring is empty: hand the context over while the emulation thread asks for it.
- `render_main` (L209) — The render thread's entry point: runs the consumer loop until it is stopped.
- `wake_render` (L287) — Wakes the render thread once enough bytes or records are unwoken, or when forced.
- `emu_wait` (L305) — Blocks the emulation thread until its predicate holds, waking the render thread first.
- `pred_space` (L318) — 1 when the ring has room up to need_end.
- `pred_drained` (L321) — 1 when the render thread has consumed everything up to w.
- `space_seen` (L322) — Like pred_space, but refreshes the consumer position seen so far when the cached one is too old.
- `pred_frames` (L327) — 1 when the frames in flight are at most limit.
- `pred_released` (L330) — 1 once the render thread has released the context.
- `rt_cmd_begin` (L332) — Append a record with room for payload_bytes; returns the payload pointer (16-byte aligned) or NULL when the record can never fit (larger than half the ring) — the caller then acquires and runs the wor
- `rt_cmd_commit` (L364) — Publishes the pending record to the render thread and updates the high-water mark.
- `commit_marker` (L381) — Writes a pad marker record into the ring, waiting for space if needed.
- `rt_frame_end` (L391) — Close a guest frame: enqueue a frame marker, then block while more than max_frames closed frames are unconsumed.
- `rt_frames_in_flight` (L412) — Producer query: closed frames the render thread has not finished yet (0 = it has caught up with every frame end).
- `rt_frames_ahead` (L417) — Render-thread query while executing: how many complete frames are queued after the frame whose record is being executed (0 = it is the newest).
- `rt_drain` (L423) — Wait until every committed record has executed (context stays where it is).
- `rt_acquire` (L429) — Sync point. Drain, then move the context to the calling thread (held).
- `rt_release` (L449) — Hand the context back to the render thread.
- `rt_start` (L462) — Start: the context must be current on the calling thread; on success it is released here and made current on the new render thread.
- `rt_stop` (L509) — Stop: drain every record, join the thread and make the context current on the calling thread again.
- `rt_get_stats` (L531) — Copies the render thread's counters into o.
- `rt_acquire_events` (L553) — Copies the most recent context acquire events into out, newest first; returns the count.

### runtime/src/save_slots.c

Many save slots in place of one memory card: keeps each save as a card image on disk and mounts one slot at a time on the player's port.

- `lock` (L44) — Takes the slot store's lock.
- `unlock` (L45) — Releases the slot store's lock.
- `make_dir` (L74) — Creates each folder along a path, like mkdir -p.
- `read_all` (L97) — Whole file into a malloc'd buffer (caller frees).
- `slot_path` (L115) — Builds the file path for a slot with the given extension.
- `frame_at` (L121) — Returns the card image's directory frame for a block.
- `block_at` (L122) — Returns the card image's 8 KB data block for a block number.
- `rd32` (L124) — Reads a little-endian 32-bit value.
- `wr32` (L127) — Writes a little-endian 32-bit value.
- `frame_seal` (L131) — Sets the frame's last byte to the XOR checksum of the rest of the frame.
- `frame_name` (L138) — Copies a frame's 20-byte save name into out, terminated.
- `is_kept` (L143) — 1 when a file name starts with a kept prefix, so it stays on every card.
- `file_chain` (L152) — Blocks of the file starting at 'first', in order.
- `extract_file` (L171) — One save as .mcs bytes: its first frame (next cleared) then its blocks.
- `place_file` (L190) — Place a .mcs save on the card under 'name' (NULL = its own).
- `remove_file` (L222) — Frees every block in a file's chain, clearing its directory frames.
- `find_file` (L233) — Returns the first block of the file with the given name, or -1 when absent.
- `text_add` (L252) — Appends a formatted string to the text buffer, if room remains.
- `put_str` (L262) — Appends a key and its escaped string value as one text line.
- `get_str` (L273) — Copies an escaped string value into dst, unescaping it and stopping at capacity.
- `write_info` (L286) — Writes the slot's info text with its format, details and name.
- `parse_info` (L324) — Parses the slot's info text lines into the save info and details.
- `cache_from_mcs` (L382) — Fill a cache entry from a .mcs buffer (header and icon).
- `cache_load` (L396) — Loads a slot's card image and info from disk into its cache entry.
- `slot_ok` (L417) — 1 when a slot number is open and in range.
- `psx_save_slots_open` (L421) — Open the slot store for 'count' slots (1..PSX_SAVE_SLOTS_MAX) in <memcard_dir>/slots (or 'dir' when not NULL) and read what is there.
- `psx_save_slots_count` (L440) — Returns how many save slots are open.
- `psx_save_slots_get` (L442) — Copy slot 'slot''s summary into out.
- `psx_save_slots_icon` (L451) — Decode frame 'frame' of the save's icon into 16x16 RGBA (1024 bytes), transparent where the game's palette says so.
- `psx_save_slots_keep_files` (L476) — Files whose card name starts with 'prefix' stay on every mounted card and are written back to the player's card (a title's settings file, say).
- `psx_save_slots_mount` (L486) — Mount on card port 'card' (0 or 1) a RAM card with the kept files and the save in 'slot' (0 = no save: a card ready for a new one).
- `psx_save_slots_commit` (L536) — Store into 'slot' the save the game wrote on the mounted card, with 'details' (may be NULL), and record the time.
- `psx_save_slots_unmount` (L613) — Put the player's card back on the port (reported as freshly inserted).
- `psx_save_slots_mounted` (L626) — The slot whose card is mounted (0 for the empty card), or -1.
- `psx_save_slots_rename` (L628) — Name a save ("" or NULL clears it).
- `psx_save_slots_delete` (L642) — Remove a save. 0 = ok, -1 bad slot, -3 the files could not be removed.
- `psx_save_slots_copy` (L656) — Copy a save with its details and name.
- `psx_save_slots_import_card` (L685) — Put each save of a .mcd card whose name starts with 'prefix' (NULL = all saves) into the first free slots.

- `savestate_poll` (L889) — Called every block from psx_check_interrupts (in_exception == 0).

### runtime/src/sgl/sgl_gpu.c

Translates the GL-style draw stream into SDL_GPU calls, covering devices, pipelines, textures, samplers, HDR swapchain output and GPU timing.

- `sgl_set_hdr` (L19) — HDR for the next context: a float16 default framebuffer, shown as scRGB (HDR_EXTENDED_LINEAR) where the window supports it (gl_hdr.inc), else as HDR10 (ST 2084 PQ, BT.2020: what gamescope / the Steam
- `sgl_stats_note` (L24) — Bumps one of the SGL statistics counters by index; out-of-range indices are ignored.
- `sgl_caps` (L28) — Returns a read-only pointer to the capabilities record of the active context.
- `sgl_impl_name` (L30) — "sdl_gpu (vulkan)" etc.; "sdl_gpu" before a context exists.
- `sgl_set_driver` (L37) — Window flags the window needs for the driver sgl will use (SDL_WINDOW_VULKAN / SDL_WINDOW_METAL / 0).
- `driver_wanted` (L40) — Picks the SDL_GPU driver name: the PSX_SGL_DRIVER variable first, then the set driver, else vulkan on Windows and Linux.
- `sgl_window_flags` (L50) — Returns the SDL window flags the chosen driver needs: Vulkan, Metal, or 0.
- `sgl_arena_reserve` (L62) — ---- arenas and ops ------------------------------------------------------
- `sgl_arena_put` (L75) — Copies n bytes into an arena at the given alignment and returns the offset where they were placed.
- `sgl_push_op` (L81) — Appends an empty op of the given type to the current stream, growing the op list when full; NULL on allocation failure.
- `sgl_release_texture` (L94) — Queues a texture to be freed once the stream is submitted; frees it at once if the queue cannot grow.
- `fmt_for` (L108) — Maps a GL internal format to an SDL_GPU texture format, kind and bytes per pixel; returns 0 when the format is not offered.
- `sgl_gpu_alloc_image` (L128) — Creates a 2D GPU texture of the given GL format and size, falling back to RGBA8 when the format is not offered.
- `fmt_bpp` (L173) — Returns the bytes per pixel of an SDL_GPU texture format, defaulting to 4.
- `fmt_is_uint` (L182) — Returns 1 when the texture format is an unsigned integer format.
- `sgl_gpu_dummy_texture` (L190) — Returns the shared 1x1 placeholder texture for float (0) or unsigned integer (non-zero) sampler slots.
- `wrap_of` (L196) — Maps a GL texture wrap mode to the SDL_GPU address mode: repeat, mirrored repeat, or clamp to edge.
- `filter_of` (L201) — Maps a GL filter to linear or nearest; every linear variant becomes linear.
- `sgl_sampler` (L205) — Returns a cached or newly created sampler for the given min and mag filters and wrap modes.
- `key_hash` (L252) — Hashes a pipeline key into a 32-bit value used by the pipeline cache table.
- `blendf` (L266) — Converts a GL blend factor to the matching SDL_GPU blend factor.
- `blendop` (L287) — Converts a GL blend equation to the SDL_GPU blend op, defaulting to add.
- `cmpop` (L296) — Converts a GL depth or stencil comparison to the SDL_GPU compare op, defaulting to always.
- `stencilop` (L308) — Converts a GL stencil operation to the SDL_GPU stencil op, defaulting to keep.
- `vfmt` (L320) — Chooses the SDL_GPU vertex element format for an attribute from its GL type, size and normalization.
- `vfmt_size` (L335) — Returns the byte size of one vertex attribute from its GL type and component count.
- `create_pipeline` (L341) — Builds an SDL_GPU graphics pipeline from a pipeline key and the vertex and fragment shaders.
- `pipe_lookup` (L413) — Finds the cached pipeline for a key and shaders, creating and storing it on a miss; grows the table when half full.
- `sgl_gpu_forget_program` (L447) — A program goes away: its pipelines too, once the stream that may still draw with them is submitted.
- `key_target` (L479) — Copies the color and depth-stencil target formats and presence into a pipeline key.
- `sgl_pipeline` (L487) — Returns the graphics pipeline for a program, vertex layout, draw mode and target, creating it when needed and listing the buffers to bind.
- `sgl_internal_program` (L624) — Returns a built-in helper program by index, linking it from embedded shaders on first use; NULL when out of range.
- `sgl_internal_pipeline` (L639) — Returns a pipeline for a built-in helper program such as clear, for the given target and color and depth write masks.
- `make_xfer` (L668) — ---- device --------------------------------------------------------------
- `sgl_gpu_download_buffer` (L675) — Creates a download transfer buffer of the given size for reading results back from the GPU.
- `present_mode_for` (L679) — Picks immediate or mailbox present mode when the interval is 0 and supported, otherwise vsync.
- `display_hdr` (L690) — The window shown in HDR now.
- `hdr_output_wanted` (L698) — The output HDR asks for: scRGB, else HDR10 (PSX_HDR_FORMAT=hdr10 first).
- `apply_swapchain` (L718) — Sets the swapchain composition and present mode for the wanted HDR output and swap interval; returns 0 on failure.
- `sgl_hdr_output` (L732) — The output now: 0 SDR, 1 scRGB, 2 HDR10 (gl_hdr.inc runs its pass when not 0; the swap encodes HDR10 itself).
- `hdr_follow` (L735) — After each swap: HDR follows the display (Windows' HDR switch, the window moved to another screen) without reopening the game.
- `upload_now` (L743) — Uploads pixel data to a texture at once through a transfer buffer and copy pass; returns 1 on success.
- `create_device` (L770) — Creates the SDL_GPU device for SPIR-V shaders with the chosen driver, debug mode from PSX_SGL_DEBUG, and reports failure.
- `sgl_gpu_probe` (L777) — Makes the SDL_GPU device for the driver sgl will use, before any window (kept for the context that follows): 0 when there is none (no Vulkan driver or device), so the frontend can take OpenGL instead.
- `sgl_gpu_init` (L782) — sgl_gpu.c
- `sgl_gpu_shutdown` (L851) — Flushes and waits for the GPU, then releases pipelines, samplers, back buffers and the device.
- `timed_thread` (L899) — Background thread that waits on each submitted GPU fence and records when the stream finished, for GPU timing.
- `sgl_gpu_timing_enable` (L924) — GPU time (timer queries on sgl): the GPU's busy clock at a submitted stream.
- `timing_shutdown` (L936) — Stops the timing thread and destroys its mutex, condition variables and state.
- `timed_push` (L949) — Queues a fence with its submit id and time for the timing thread, waiting while the queue is full.
- `timed_wait` (L957) — Blocks until the timing thread has passed the given submit id.
- `sgl_gpu_last_submit` (L962) — Returns the id of the most recently submitted stream.
- `sgl_gpu_clock_at` (L963) — Writes the GPU clock time of a submitted stream id into ns, waiting for it when asked; returns 1 when the time is known.
- `cmp_u64` (L981) — qsort comparator for 64-bit unsigned values.
- `acquire_json` (L985) — Appends swapchain acquire timing statistics as a JSON fragment for the debug server; only the count when samples are few.
- `fence_keep` (L1013) — Stores a GPU fence for a stream id in a 16-slot ring, releasing the older fence held in that slot.
- `sgl_gpu_wait_stream` (L1019) — Waits until the GPU has finished the given stream id, flushing first if it is still open; returns 1 on success.
- `same_target` (L1031) — ---- encoding -----------------------------------------------------------
- `begin_pass` (L1034) — Starts a render pass on the command buffer for a target, clearing color or depth when a clear op is given.
- `note_once` (L1068) — One line per kind of failure, the first time only: a failure that repeats every frame would flood the output.
- `ensure_buffer` (L1074) — Grows a vertex buffer to hold at least need bytes, doubling from 1 MB; returns 1 on success.
- `ensure_xfer` (L1088) — Grows a transfer buffer of the given usage to hold at least need bytes; returns 1 on success.
- `stream_reset` (L1099) — Frees deferred resources, clears the op and arena lists, and starts a new stream id.
- `stream_has` (L1112) — Returns 1 when the current stream already holds an op of the given type.
- `sgl_flush` (L1117) — Encode and submit the stream; wait for the GPU when wait != 0.
- `sgl_gpu_read_now` (L1413) — Reads a texture rectangle back to CPU memory at once, flushing the stream first; the pixels are returned through out.
- `sgl_create_context` (L1438) — ---- the context API ----------------------------------------------------
- `sgl_make_current` (L1444) — Reports success for the single shared context: true when ctx is NULL or that context.
- `sgl_delete_context` (L1448) — Shuts down the GPU when the given context is the one in use.
- `sgl_swap_window` (L1451) — Flushes the stream with a present, follows window moves, updates HDR, and returns whether the flush worked.
- `sgl_set_swap_interval` (L1458) — 1 = vsync, 0 = immediate (mailbox when available), -1 = adaptive (vsync).
- `sgl_get_swap_interval` (L1462) — Writes the current swap interval through the pointer and returns success.
- `sgl_stats_json` (L1467) — Counters for the debug server (TCP "sgl"): passes, draws, uploads...

### runtime/src/sgl/sgl_shader.cpp

Compiles GLSL to SPIR-V with glslang, caches the result on disk, and builds SDL_GPU shaders with reflected resource layouts.

- `glslang_init` (L41) — Initializes the glslang compiler process once; later calls do nothing.
- `set_log` (L57) — Replaces the program's info log with the given message and returns the message.
- `compile_program` (L64) — ---- compile ------------------------------------------------------------
- `spv_cache_dir` (L130) — Returns the folder for cached SPIR-V, or an empty string when caching is turned off with PSX_SGL_SHADER_CACHE=0.
- `fnv1a` (L149) — Folds n bytes into a running 64-bit FNV-1a hash and returns the new value.
- `spv_cache_path` (L154) — Builds the cache file path from a hash of the cache version, the GL rules flag and both shader sources; empty when caching is off.
- `spv_cache_load` (L167) — Reads both SPIR-V stages from the cache file after checking its header; returns true only when the file is valid.
- `spv_cache_store` (L182) — Writes both SPIR-V stages to the cache file through a temporary file.
- `spv_set_decoration` (L201) — Set (or add) 'OpDecorate id dec value'.
- `spv_remove_decoration` (L220) — Removes every OpDecorate instruction for the given id and decoration from a SPIR-V module.
- `gl_type_of` (L233) — Returns the GL type enum for a SPIR-V type; image types get a placeholder that the caller refines.
- `uniform_get` (L254) — Returns the uniform record with the given name, adding an empty one to the list when it is missing.
- `match_varyings` (L270) — GL matches varyings by name; glslang's automatic locations follow each stage's declaration order.
- `place_and_reflect` (L304) — Put the stage's resources where SDL_GPU wants them and read the catalog.
- `make_shaders` (L402) — Creates the SDL_GPU vertex and fragment shaders from the two SPIR-V stages and adds the time to the shader timing counter.
- `link_common` (L424) — Loads or compiles both stages, reflects their resources and builds the shaders; returns nonzero when linking succeeded.
- `sgl_shader_link` (L470) — sgl_shader.cpp Compile + link vs/fs GLSL into prog (SPIR-V, reflection, SDL shaders).
- `sgl_shader_link_internal` (L473) — Internal programs: GLSL 450 written for Vulkan.
- `sgl_shader_shutdown` (L476) — Does nothing; glslang keeps its process state for a later context.

### runtime/src/sio.c

Emulates the console serial port: the controller and memory card protocols, the multitap, their interrupts, diagnostics and the save-state snapshot of all of it.

- `sio_debug_poll_maybe` (L41) — Calls the debug server poll once every 1024 SIO register accesses.
