- `probe_impl` (L19) — Reads the size and channels of an encoded image, enforcing the encoded size limit and the decoded budget.
- `texture_image_probe` (L64) — Checks an encoded texture image against the decoded budget without decoding it and fills the probe result.
- `texture_image_decode` (L75) — Decodes an encoded texture image into pixels within the decoded budget; returns false with an error message on failure.

### runtime/src/timers.c

Simulates the console's three root counters: counting, targets, interrupts, clock sources, the debug view and register access.

- `timers_get_debug` (L65) — Copies one timer's counter, target, mode and interrupt count into the given pointers; does nothing for an invalid timer.
- `timers_init` (L79) — Clears all three timers and their fractional cycle counters.
- `timers_get_snapshot` (L84) — Copies the counter, mode, target, interrupt line and fraction of all three timers into arrays for a save state.
- `timers_set_snapshot` (L96) — Restores the counter, mode, target, interrupt line and fraction of all three timers from arrays.
- `timers_snapshot_mode_ok` (L110) — Range check for a saved mode word (pass 1 of a .pst load): the guest can only produce bits 0-12, plus the internal one-shot-spent bit.
- `timer_stopped` (L118) — CPU-3 (partial): timer 2 with sync enabled and sync mode 0 or 3 stops at its current value until the next mode write (psx-spx, counter 2 sync modes).
- `timer_uses_sysclk` (L124) — Determine whether this timer uses system clock ticks
- `timer_fire_irq` (L136) — Fire IRQ for a timer — sets I_STAT bit; a one-shot timer (mode bit 6 = 0) fires only once until the next mode write.
- `timer_tick_one` (L167) — Tick a single timer by one count.
- `timer_advance_counts` (L186) — Adds the given number of counts to one timer, handling target and overflow events along the way.
- `timer_advance_divided` (L217) — Advances one timer by cycles divided by its divisor, keeping the remainder for the next call.
- `timers_advance` (L226) — Advance all timers by guest CPU cycles.
- `timer_divisor` (L248) — Cycles until this timer's clock advances by one count, given its source.
- `timers_cycles_to_irq` (L264) — Cycle-budgeted precise event slicing: distance (in guest CPU cycles) to the next moment this timer block would raise a DELIVERABLE IRQ — i.e.
- `timers_read` (L300) — MMIO read/write for 0x1F801100..0x1F80112F.
- `timers_write` (L339) — Handles a guest write to a timer register in the 0x1F801100 to 0x1F80112F range, setting its counter, target or mode.
- `timers_tick` (L366) — Legacy coarse tick used by interpreter/oracle builds.

### runtime/src/traps.c

Handles guest traps and the thread scheduler: crash and break reporting, saving and restoring thread contexts, and fiber-based thread switching.

- `traps_parity_rw` (L24) — RAM reader adapter for the parity trace (cpu->read_word takes only addr).
- `sched_escape_ring_log` (L70) — Logs a scheduler escape with its reason, current and target thread and resume PC into a ring for diagnostics.
- `psx_is_dispatchable` (L89) — Fail-closed guard: is 'pc' a valid, dispatchable guest resume point?
- `psx_bail_record` (L139) — Counts one wild return by its call site and target, and keeps the first one seen.
- `psx_bail_ledger_top` (L170) — Read the highest-count ledger entry (the dominant wild-return source).
- `psx_ra_tripwire` (L199) — Latches the first time the return address register is set to 1 by a jump, recording the site, PC, frame and stack pointer.
- `trap_crash` (L212) — Writes the message to psx_crash.txt, dumps the trace ring, then halts for debugging or exits in release builds.
- `psx_is_valid_tcb` (L221) — Returns 1 when a thread control block lies inside the kernel's thread table.
- `psx_current_tcb_ptr` (L246) — Returns the address of the current thread control block, read from the kernel's pointer.
- `psx_set_current_tcb` (L252) — Stores a thread control block address as the current thread in the kernel's pointer.
- `thread_ctx_ring_log` (L284) — Logs a thread context save or restore with its block, resume PC and operation into a ring for diagnostics.
- `psx_assert_no_sentinel_pc` (L306) — Fail-closed: the host exception sentinel must NEVER be persisted into a TCB as a thread's resume PC, nor read back out of one.
- `psx_save_context_to_tcb` (L317) — Saves the CPU registers and the resume PC into a thread's control block.
- `psx_store_change_thread_result` (L342) — ChangeTh (B 10h) returns 1 to its caller.
- `psx_restore_context_from_tcb` (L347) — Loads the CPU registers of a thread from its control block and returns its resume PC.
- `psx_sched_save_context` (L388) — Deferred cooperative thread switch (Ape Escape memcard fix #2).
- `psx_sched_set_current_tcb` (L393) — Sets the current thread control block for the scheduler.
- `psx_sched_current_tcb` (L398) — Returns the current thread control block address for the scheduler.
- `psx_tcb_state` (L417) — Returns the state word of a thread control block, or 0 when the block is not valid.
- `psx_current_host_fiber` (L422) — Returns the host fiber of the main thread, converting the current thread to a fiber on first use.
- `psx_find_host_thread` (L434) — Returns the host fiber slot bound to a thread control block, or NULL when none is bound.
- `psx_alloc_host_thread` (L444) — Returns a free host fiber slot, cleared, or NULL when all slots are in use.
- `psx_bind_current_host_thread` (L457) — Binds a thread control block to a host fiber slot, creating the binding for the current thread.
- `psx_thread_fiber_entry` (L473) — Entry point of a host fiber that runs a guest thread.
- `psx_fiber_nesting_save` (L528) — Saves the dispatch depth and bail flags of the host nesting before a fiber switch.
- `psx_fiber_nesting_restore` (L540) — Restores the dispatch depth and bail flags saved before a fiber switch.
- `psx_fiber_drop_threads` (L564) — Releases all host thread fibers except the current one.
- `psx_fiber_take_restore` (L579) — Called where the main fiber resumes after a switch: if a restore is waiting, unwind this fiber's stack to the scheduler loop, as the HLE scheduler unwinds its single stack.
- `psx_fiber_take_restore_unnested` (L588) — Takes a pending fiber restore when there is no nesting record.
- `psx_get_or_create_host_thread` (L593) — Returns the host fiber of a thread control block, creating one when the thread is in the expected state; NULL otherwise.
- `psx_change_thread_fiber` (L635) — Switches the running guest thread to the target thread by way of a host fiber.
- `psx_fiber_preempt_switch` (L751) — In-exception thread switch on the host-fiber scheduler.
- `psx_request_thread_switch` (L803) — ── Deterministic TCB scheduler — LIVE (carve-out, replaces the fiber bridge) ─ psx_request_thread_switch performs a cooperative thread switch by committing the yielding thread's full context to its TC
- `psx_scheduler_top_level_resume_active` (L868) — After resume_at, dispatch is top-level — there is no abandoned mid-block native chain under the resume PC.
- `psx_scheduler_top_level_resume_clear` (L873) — Clears the flag that marks the scheduler resume as top level.
- `psx_scheduler_resume_at` (L880) — Save-state restore: unwind to psx_scheduler_run and re-dispatch resume_pc (the restored CPUState's PC).
- `psx_hle_scheduler_set_default` (L936) — HLE-tier standing subsystem replacement (CLAUDE.md §0 amendments 2026-06-29 + 2026-07-02).
- `psx_hle_scheduler_enabled` (L941) — Returns 1 when the HLE scheduler is enabled by PSX_HLE_SCHEDULER, read once.
- `psx_change_thread` (L952) — Switches to a target thread through the HLE scheduler or the fiber path, depending on whether the HLE scheduler is enabled.
- `psx_clear_return_to_lobby` (L962) — Clears the pending return-to-lobby request.
- `psx_return_to_lobby_requested` (L967) — Returns 1 when a return to the lobby has been requested.
- `psx_request_return_to_lobby` (L972) — Soft-exit netplay back to the lobby UI.
- `psx_scheduler_can_resume_at` (L984) — Returns 1 when the scheduler can resume at the PC: it is inside the scheduler run, the HLE scheduler is on and the PC is dispatchable.
- `psx_scheduler_rfe_resume` (L990) — Records a resume at the given PC for the current thread in the scheduler escape, for an exception return.
- `psx_scheduler_run` (L1000) — Runs the scheduler loop, dispatching guest code until it escapes or the run ends.
- `psx_syscall` (L1138) — Trap trampolines — defined in runtime/src/traps.c psx_syscall returns 1 if control transfers (cpu->pc set to a dispatch target; the caller must return to the trampoline), 0 for a directly-handled "voi
- `psx_break` (L1287) — Reports a BREAK instruction with its PC and code as a crash.
- `psx_arith_overflow` (L1295) — Reports an arithmetic overflow at the CPU's PC as a crash.
- `psx_unaligned_access` (L1303) — Logs an unaligned memory access, up to three times, and lets the current function return early.
- `psx_unknown_dispatch` (L1319) — Unknown dispatch — defined in runtime/src/traps.c

### runtime/src/video_telemetry.cpp

Publishes a passive snapshot of the video output state, such as renderer, scale and sizes, for the debug tools to read.

- `psx_video_telemetry_compose` (L11) — Publishes the renderer, scale, source and display sizes as one snapshot that the reader can pick up without waiting.
- `psx_video_telemetry_present` (L22) — Call after the backend's swap/present API returns.
- `psx_video_telemetry_snapshot` (L27) — Bounded passive read: valid=0 if a coherent composition was unavailable.

### runtime/src/video_texture_filter.c

Converts texture filter and edge mode names to and from their numeric values.

- `psx_texture_filter_from_ui` (L6) — A launcher value to the enum: in-range values pass through (xBR included), anything else is nearest, the native default.
- `psx_texture_filter_parse` (L17) — Config names: "nearest", "bilinear", "stable", "xbr", "sharp_bilinear", "jinc2", "monotonic_cubic", "dcci", "scale2x" (or "epx"), "scale3x", "mmpx"; edges "ps1", "clean", "soft".
- `psx_texture_filter_name` (L26) — Returns the config name of a texture filter value, defaulting to nearest for an out-of-range value.
- `psx_texture_edge_parse` (L29) — Returns the edge mode number for a config name, or -1 when the name is NULL or unknown.
- `psx_texture_edge_name` (L35) — Returns the config name of an edge mode value, defaulting to ps1 for an out-of-range value.

### runtime/src/vr_geometry_math.c

Holds the VR geometry math: matrix inversion with a determinant check, box visibility and ray-box intersection.

- `finite9` (L6) — Returns 1 when all nine values are finite numbers.
- `finite3` (L15) — Returns 1 when all three values are finite numbers.
- `psx_vr_inverse3x3` (L24) — Inverts a 3 by 3 matrix when its determinant is within the policy limits; returns 0 otherwise.
- `psx_vr_box_visible` (L69) — Returns 1 when an axis-aligned box, placed by the model and eye transforms, projects onto the screen.
- `psx_vr_ray_box` (L136) — Tests a ray against an axis-aligned box; returns 1 on a hit and writes the entry distance to t_enter.

### runtime/src/vr_pose_math.c

Turns VR head and controller poses, a quaternion plus a position, into view and transform matrices.

- `matrix` (L4) — Converts a quaternion into a 3 by 3 rotation matrix; returns 0 when it is not finite or not close to unit length.
- `vr_pose_to_view` (L13) — Builds the view render data from the head and eye poses, the unit scale and the screen size; returns 0 on invalid input.
- `vr_pose_to_transform` (L41) — Builds a rotation matrix and translation from two poses and a unit scale; returns 0 on invalid input.

### runtime/src/ws_aspect_cone_math.c

Checks whether a point falls inside the widened view cone used by the widescreen aspect logic.

- `psx_ws_widen_angle_q12` (L5) — Widen a positive PSX 12-bit angular half-extent by the same horizontal projection scale used by a 320-wide 4:3 viewport.
- `psx_ws_aspect_cone_contains` (L20) — Returns 1 when a point lies inside the widened cone around the forward direction for the threshold and extent; 0 for an invalid threshold.

### runtime/src/ws_ui_group.c

Groups nearby HUD elements into one unit that gets a shared screen anchor, so they stay together when the screen width changes.

- `ws_ui_anchor_for_bounds` (L5) — Returns the screen anchor for an element by its center: the left third, center or right third of the display.
- `axis_gap` (L13) — Returns the gap between two ranges on one axis, or 0 when they overlap.
- `interval_gap` (L19) — Returns the horizontal gap between two items' bounds, or 0 when they overlap.
- `same_element` (L47) — Are the two primitives one visual element -- drawn over or directly against each other -- as opposed to merely close?
- `touching` (L57) — Close enough on screen to be part of the same widget: horizontally within a glyph-gap, vertically overlapping or all but touching.
- `items_join` (L90) — The three ways two primitives are one HUD element.
- `root_of` (L98) — Finds the root of a union-find set and compresses the path on the way.
- `run_anchor` (L106) — Returns the anchor for a run of items: the center of the item when placed in place, else the screen anchor.
- `ws_ui_group_assign` (L112) — Assigns each HUD item an anchor and a group root; in dense menus every item gets the screen center and no run.
